title: Port v2's issue grouping and ordering as tested pure functions
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

The grouping and order of the v2 beads page is what Jack's eyes are trained on, so it must match exactly. In the issues layer, implement pure functions over the issue list: top-level epics (an epic whose parent is not an epic) become groups; child epics nest recursively with a cycle guard; issues whose parent is not an epic fall into a final ungrouped bucket; each group carries open and total counts over all descendants; closed epics with nothing visible are hidden unless "show closed" is on. Sibling order is: hierarchical id sequence, then numeric-aware title collation, then a topological pass so an issue blocked by a sibling sorts after it. Cover with unit tests built from fixtures, including a cycle and a blocked sibling.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests pass for grouping, nesting, counts, hidden closed epics, the ungrouped bucket, and all three ordering passes; the functions have no UI dependencies.
notes:
Grouping + ordering pure functions (3.6 consumes these). Auto-imported from apps/web/layers/issues/app/utils/; no Vue/Nuxt imports (only types from @candy-mountain/shared), so tests import them directly.

ORDER app/utils/issues-order.ts
- issuesSortSiblings<T extends IssuesOrderable>(issues: readonly T[]): T[]  (new array, input untouched). IssuesOrderable = { id, title, dependencies: readonly IssueDependency[] }.
- Port of v2 lib/bead-order.ts sortBeads: (1) hierarchical id sequence = numeric parts after the first '.' (x.2 < x.2.9 < x.2.10 < x.3.1; ids with a sequence before opaque ids; non-numeric suffix = opaque); (2) Intl.Collator numeric, sensitivity base ('Phase 2' < 'Phase 2b' < 'Phase 10'); tie -> id; (3) topological pass: repeatedly take the first ranked issue whose 'blocks' deps on SIBLINGS are all placed; blockers not in the passed list are ignored; a blocking cycle takes the head.
- Deviation: collator/tie-break use fixed locale 'en' (v2 used runtime default) so SSR and hydrated order match.

TREE app/utils/issues-tree.ts
- issuesGroupTree<T extends IssuesTreeItem>(issues: readonly T[], { showClosed?: boolean } = {}): IssuesTree<T>
  IssuesTreeItem = Pick<Issue,'id'|'title'|'type'|'status'|'parentId'|'dependencies'> (pass the full Issue[] from api.list; T is preserved in nodes).
- IssuesTree<T> = { groups: IssuesEpicNode<T>[]; ungrouped: IssuesUngroupedBucket<T> | null }
- IssuesEpicNode<T> = { epic: T; issues: T[] (visible direct non-epic children, sorted); epics: IssuesEpicNode<T>[] (nested, sorted, recursive); openCount; totalCount }
- IssuesUngroupedBucket<T> = { issues: T[] (visible, sorted); openCount; totalCount }
- issuesParentId(issue): parentId ?? first 'parent-child' dependency's dependsOnId ?? null.
Rules (v2 BeadsPage.vue groups computed): epic = type 'epic', closed = status 'closed'. Top-level group = epic whose parent is not an epic id (no parent, or a non-epic parent). Child epics nest recursively with a seen-set guard. Non-epic issues whose parent is not an epic (none/missing/non-epic) go to ungrouped. Closed non-epic issues filtered out unless showClosed (filter happens BEFORE the topological pass, like v2). A closed epic with no visible issues and no visible nested epics is dropped (top-level and nested) unless showClosed. ungrouped is non-null whenever any non-epic issue is outside an epic, even if all are closed (issues may be []), matching v2 'No epic' which showed when orphans existed.
- Counts: DEVIATION from v2 per bead text: openCount/totalCount = non-epic issues across the WHOLE subtree (incl. inside hidden closed nested epics), ignoring showClosed; on every node (v2 had direct children only, top-level only). Epics themselves are not counted. open = status !== 'closed'.
- Parent cycles among epics (A->B->A, self-parent) have no root, so those epics and their issues are not shown at all (same as v2).

HOW 3.6 CALLS IT: const tree = computed(() => issuesGroupTree(issues.value, { showClosed: showClosed.value })). Render tree.groups as collapsible EpicGroup cards ('N open / M total' from openCount/totalCount, title/assignee/id from node.epic), recurse node.epics for nested sections, rows from node.issues; render tree.ungrouped last as the 'No epic' bucket when non-null. Apply ready/blocked/search filters to the input list or to node.issues as 3.6 decides (note counts come from the input passed in). Use issuesSortSiblings for any other flat sibling list.

TESTS apps/web/layers/issues/test/issues-order.test.ts (13) + issues-tree.test.ts (16), picked up by apps/web vitest include layers/*/test/**. Root lint, typecheck, test (98 files / 930 tests) pass.
close_reason: issuesGroupTree + issuesSortSiblings ported from v2, 29 tests

title: Watch each project's .beads directory and push change notifications
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Jack uses `bd` from terminals and agents use it from sessions, so the page must refresh itself. Watch the `.beads` directory of every project that has one (debounced, tolerant of the directory appearing or disappearing while the daemon runs), invalidate that project's list cache on change, and expose a per-project server-sent event stream that emits a "changed" notice. Keep one watcher per project regardless of how many clients listen, and stop watching archived or deleted projects.
acceptance_criteria: Running `bd create` in a project's checkout emits a changed event on the project's stream within a second or two; a burst of ten writes emits a handful of events, not ten; removing the project stops the watcher.
notes:
Issue change stream decisions (3.7 and later beads depend on these). Short how-to also in apps/daemon/README.md "Issues".

SSE ROUTE: GET /projects/:slug/issues/events (daemon path). Browser: new EventSource('/api/projects/<slug>/issues/events'); shared helper projectIssueEventsPath(slug), constants ISSUE_CHANGED_EVENT='changed', type IssueChangedEvent { projectId } (packages/shared/src/issues.ts). Wire format: ': connected' comment sent immediately (Node only flushes headers with the first body bytes), ': ping' comment every ISSUE_EVENTS_HEARTBEAT_MS=30000 (web proxy's undici fetch cuts bodies silent for 300s), and on change 'event: changed' + 'data: {"projectId":"<uuid>"}'. No payload beyond that: clients refetch the list (and open detail) on changed. Unknown slug -> 404 not_found JSON (EventSource then stops retrying). Archived projects still open a stream but get only heartbeats. Streams end when the watcher closes (daemon shutdown); client disconnect unsubscribes. Auth applies like every other route (EventSource sends the cookie same-origin).

MOUNT: issueEventRoutes(watcher, { heartbeatMs? }) in src/issues/events-routes.ts, mounted in app.ts at PROJECTS_PATH only when AppDeps.issueWatcher is given, and BEFORE issueRoutes() (otherwise /:slug/issues/:id claims 'events'). index.ts passes platform.issueWatcher.

WATCHER MODULE (src/issues/watcher.ts, re-exported from issues/index.ts): startIssueWatcher({ db, invalidate? = invalidateIssueList, debounceMs? = 250, maxWaitMs? = 1000, minIntervalMs? = 2000, reconcileMs? = 2000 }) -> IssueWatcher { subscribe(projectId, listener) -> unsubscribe; isWatching(projectId); reconcile(); signal: AbortSignal (aborted on close); close() (idempotent) }. Also exports beadsFingerprint(beadsDir) and the ISSUE_WATCH_* constants. One recursive fs.watch (Node 24 on Linux, persistent:false, no chokidar needed) per active project with a .beads dir, shared by all subscribers; on a detected change it calls invalidate(projectId) then every listener.

KEY GOTCHA (measured with bd 1.2.2): bd rewrites embedded Dolt files (manifest, journal.idx, temp manifests) on EVERY read, and bd show writes .beads/last-touched; comment/dep/label writes touch no top-level file. So raw fs events cannot distinguish reads from writes and would loop (refetch -> bd list -> event -> refetch). Events therefore only trigger a check: after the debounce the watcher computes beadsFingerprint = sha1 of issues.jsonl + each .beads/**/.dolt/noms/manifest (depth<=3, covers embeddeddolt/<db> and server-mode dolt/) + Dolt journal file size; manifest root hash and journal length only change on commits. Verified: list/ready/show/comments/dep list leave it unchanged; create/update/close/comment add/label add change it.

DEBOUNCE: trailing 250ms quiet, flushed at most 1s into a continuous burst; then notifications per project are spaced at least 2s apart (a scripted burst is many bd processes, each ~0.3-0.7s, so pure debouncing gave one event per write). Live: single bd create -> event 0.8s after start (0.25s after bd exits); ten sequential creates over 5s -> 4 events; reads -> 0 events.

PROJECT LIFECYCLE: polling, no hook in projects/*.ts. The watcher reconciles every 2s (unref'd interval; errors logged, never thrown) against listProjects(db) (active only): new/unarchived projects get a watch, archived/deleted ones are closed, a changed checkout path replaces the watch and emits changed. The same tick stats each .beads (inode) so the directory appearing, disappearing or being recreated (rm -rf + bd init: a recursive watch reports neither) is picked up; appearing/disappearing emits changed. If fs.watch throws (e.g. inotify limit) it warns once and polls the fingerprint each tick. Chose polling over an emitter so concurrent beads editing projects.ts are untouched and changes made any way (direct DB edits) are seen; cost is one SQLite query + one stat per project per 2s, and up to 2s lag on create/archive/delete.

PLATFORM: startPlatform starts it as platform.issueWatcher; platform.close() closes it before the DB. index.ts shutdown closes the watcher BEFORE server.close() since open SSE streams would otherwise keep server.close waiting forever (verified: SIGTERM with an open stream exits in ~0.3s).

TESTS: src/issues/watcher.test.ts (real temp workspaces via createTempBeadsWorkspace; bd writes run async because execFileSync would block the loop and fold events): bd create -> event + invalidate within 2s; reads -> no events; ten creates -> 1..5 events with production spacing; two subscribers share one watch, unsubscribe works; archive/unarchive/delete stop/resume; new project picked up by reconcile; .beads removed and re-inited; no-tracker/missing checkout tolerated. src/issues/events-routes.test.ts: SSE framing, changed event, heartbeat (50ms), subscribe/unsubscribe per connection, stream ends on watcher close, 404 unknown slug, createApp mounts it ahead of /:id, real bd create reaches the stream. Tests that need several events pass minIntervalMs: 0.

VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (56 files / 507 tests), build pass. Live: node --import tsx src/index.ts on port 5437 with throwaway CM_DATA_DIR and a temp bd workspace; curl -N of the stream showed ': connected', changed after bd create, nothing for 3 list GETs, 4 events for a 10-create burst, ': ping' at 30s, no events after DELETE /projects/live, reconnect -> 404, SIGTERM with a stream open -> clean exit.
close_reason: fingerprint-based watcher + SSE stream verified live; gates green

title: Add the Issues capability manifest and layer skeleton
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Register the `issues` capability: manifest in the daemon (member of the `issues` module, no required plugins, a project-fact readiness requirement that the project has a `.beads` directory, ladder none then read then write, where write adds the editing tools) and a layer in the web app with an empty issues list view and an issue detail view at a path that carries the issue id. Add the layer's API client composable for the daemon's issue endpoints. Pages render placeholders; the real UI is separate work.

Shared names: Capability ids are fixed: `overview`, `issues`, `chat-claude-code`, `chat-codex`, `bots`, `team`, `uptime`, `deployments`, `platform-agent`. Module ids are fixed: `issues`, `agent-hub`, `operations`.
acceptance_criteria: Enabling Issues on a project with `.beads` shows the Issues view; a project without `.beads` shows the soft lockout naming the missing directory; lint passes.
notes:
Issues capability + layer skeleton decisions (3.5-3.15 build on these).

MANIFEST apps/daemon/src/capabilities/manifests/issues.ts (issuesCapability), in CAPABILITIES after overview.
- One view { id 'issues', label 'Issues', icon 'i-lucide-list-todo', path 'issues' } -> /p/<slug>/issues. VIEW_PATH_PATTERN allows no params, so there is NO separate 'issue' view: the detail page is an undeclared child route /p/<slug>/issues/:id gated with view 'issues'.
- requiresPlugins [], requiresProjectFacts ['hasBeads'] (reason "The project has no .beads directory."; lockout action 'Re-check the project').
- tools: 'issues.write' and 'issues.comment', both kind 'operation', unscoped.
- ladder: none -> read (views ['issues'], no tools) -> write (views ['issues'], tools issues.write + issues.comment).
- Module: ISSUES_MODULE.capabilities = [overview read, issues write] (defaultRung 'write').

DAEMON GATE (done here): src/issues/write-routes.ts mounts requireCapability({ capability: 'issues', tool: 'issues.write' }) on POST issues, POST issues/bulk, PATCH issues/:id, POST issues/:id/close, and tool 'issues.comment' on POST issues/:id/comments + PATCH issues/:id/comments/:commentId. Refusals: module off 404 not_enabled; no .beads 409 not_ready (admin message names .beads); rung read 403 not_granted. READ routes (list/show/dependencies/comments) and the SSE stream are still UNGATED (not asked; add requireCapability({capability:'issues', view:'issues'}) later if wanted). write-routes.test.ts now enables the issues module for its project and has a test for not_enabled/not_ready.

WEB LAYER apps/web/layers/issues/
- nuxt.config.ts: components prefix 'Issues' (app/components/ not created yet).
- app/pages/p/[project]/issues/index.vue: <CapabilityViewGate capability="issues" view="issues"><UDashboardPanel id="issues"> + UEmpty placeholder. 3.6 replaces the body with a component (e.g. IssuesList) that fetches INSIDE the slot.
- app/pages/p/[project]/issues/[id].vue: same gate (view 'issues'), UDashboardPanel id="issue", navbar title = route.params.id, back button (aria-label 'Back to issues') to issuesPagePath(slug), UEmpty placeholder. 3.8 replaces the body with the detail component. Sibling of index.vue (no issues.vue parent), so both are children of core p/[project].vue; projectSwitchPath drops the :id on project switch.
- app/utils/paths.ts: issuesPagePath(slug: string, issueId?: string): string -> /p/<slug>/issues or /p/<slug>/issues/<encoded id>.
- app/composables/useIssuesApi.ts: useIssuesApi() -> object of $api calls (all slug-first, return Promises, reject with FetchError whose data is ApiErrorBody):
  list(slug) -> IssueListResponse
  show(slug, id) -> IssueResponse
  dependencies(slug, ids: readonly string[]) -> IssueDependencyListResponse (GET .../issues/dependencies?ids=a,b; max 200)
  comments(slug, id) -> IssueCommentListResponse
  create(slug, body: CreateIssueRequest) -> CreateIssueResponse
  update(slug, id, body: UpdateIssueRequest) -> IssueResponse
  close(slug, id, body: CloseIssueRequest = {}) -> IssueResponse
  bulkUpdate(slug, body: BulkUpdateIssuesRequest) -> BulkUpdateIssuesResponse
  addComment(slug, id, text) -> IssueCommentResponse
  editComment(slug, id, commentId, text) -> IssueCommentResponse
  Type IssuesApi = ReturnType<typeof useIssuesApi>. Call useIssuesApi() in setup (it uses useNuxtApp). For SSR data use useAsyncData(key, () => api.list(slug)).
- app/composables/useIssuesEvents.ts: useIssuesEvents(slug: MaybeRefOrGetter<string|null|undefined>, onChanged: (event: IssueChangedEvent) => void) -> { connected: Readonly<Ref<boolean>>, close() }. Opens new EventSource('/api' + projectIssueEventsPath(slug)) in onMounted (never SSR), listens for ISSUE_CHANGED_EVENT, reopens when slug changes, closes on scope dispose. Does NOT fire onChanged after a reconnect; 3.7 may want to refetch on connected false->true.
- README 'Views, the sidebar and the gate' gained a paragraph on param child routes.

VERIFIED: tsx daemon :6741 (throwaway CM_DATA_DIR, development auth) + built web (.output copied to scratch) :6740. Projects cm (this repo) and plain (empty dir), PUT modules ['issues'] on both. Registry: cm issues rung write ready, sidebar /p/cm/issues; plain issues ready false, reason '.beads'. Headless Chromium 10/10: cm sidebar link + list placeholder, detail placeholder + back link client nav, plain list and detail show lockout 'Issues needs setup for this project / The project has no .beads directory. / Re-check the project', 390px no overflow, no console errors. curl via proxy: dependencies, comments, SSE ': connected'. Write gate: plain POST -> 409 not_ready naming .beads; cm POST {} -> 400 (passes gate).
Root gates: lint pass, typecheck pass, build pass, test 3 failures all in src/registry/agent-hub.test.ts caused by another agent's chat-claude-code/chat-codex manifests joining agent-hub (not this bead).
OBSERVED (core, not changed): on /p/<slug>/issues the sidebar also highlights Overview (its to '/p/<slug>' prefix-matches every project route) - for the 2.13/2.7 owner.
close_reason: issues manifest, write-route gating, layer skeleton + composables; browser-verified

title: Add the bd runner and issue read endpoints with a short cache
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

v2 spawned a `bd` process per click through a generic tool-execute route and had no cache. The daemon must own a small runner that executes the `bd` CLI with `--json` in a project's checkout path, and dedicated per-project REST endpoints for reading issues: list (all issues including closed, with no limit so parent epics are never truncated, plus a readiness flag taken from `bd ready`, never from a list filter), show one issue (an unknown id returns an error payload with exit code zero from `bd`, so detect it and answer 404), dependencies for a set of ids, and comments for an issue. Cache the list per project for a few seconds and expose an invalidation hook the watcher will call. Refuse to run when the project has no `.beads` directory. Surface `bd` failures as errors with the CLI's message.
acceptance_criteria: Listing a real project returns every issue with correct ready flags; an unknown id yields 404; two list calls within the cache window run `bd` once (test with a spy); a project without `.beads` yields a clear error.
notes:
Issues read path decisions (later beads depend on these). Short how-to also in apps/daemon/README.md "Issues".

MODULE: apps/daemon/src/issues (index.ts re-exports). No DB table/migration.
- bd-runner.ts: runBd: BdRunner = (cwd: string, args: readonly string[], options?: { timeoutMs?: number }) => Promise<unknown>. Spawns execFile('bd', [...args, '--json'], { cwd, timeout, maxBuffer 64MB }), no shell. BD_TIMEOUT_MS = 15000. Env: BD_NON_INTERACTIVE=1, BEADS_DIR/BEADS_DB removed (they would redirect every project to one workspace). requireBeadsDirectory(cwd) runs first: without <cwd>/.beads it throws no_issue_tracker (bd otherwise walks up to an enclosing workspace). Writes (3.2) should reuse runBd.
- errors.ts: IssueError(code, message) with .status. Codes = shared ISSUE_ERROR_CODES.
- mapping.ts: bd snake_case JSON -> shared camelCase wire types (missing strings -> null, labels [] default).
- service.ts: createIssuesService({ run?, ttlMs?, now? }) -> IssuesService { list(project), show(project, id), dependencies(project, ids), comments(project, id), invalidate(projectId) }; project = Pick<Project,'id'|'source'>, cwd = sourcePath(project.source). Default singleton issuesService; exported hook invalidateIssueList(projectId: string): void (3.3 watcher and every 3.2 write call it).
- routes.ts: issueRoutes(service = issuesService), mounted in app.ts as app.route(PROJECTS_PATH, issueRoutes()) next to projectRoutes (routes are '/:slug/issues...'). Project resolved with getProjectBySlug (unknown slug -> 404 not_found via ProjectError).

ROUTES (daemon paths; browser uses /api prefix):
- GET /projects/:slug/issues -> IssueListResponse { issues: Issue[] }. bd list --all --limit 0 + bd ready --limit 0 run in parallel; ready = id in bd ready output (in_progress is never ready, bd semantics). bd's order is kept; UI sorts.
- GET /projects/:slug/issues/:id -> IssueResponse { issue: IssueDetail }. Runs bd show <id> + bd dep list <id> --direction up in parallel; ready taken from the cached list snapshot. dependsOn = bd show's dependencies (IssueLink incl. parent edge); dependents = dep list up (children = dependents with dependencyType 'parent-child').
- GET /projects/:slug/issues/dependencies?ids=a,b (comma list and/or repeated ids; max MAX_DEPENDENCY_IDS=200) -> IssueDependencyListResponse { dependencies: IssueDependency[] } = outgoing edges of each id (bd dep list, direction down). Unknown ids contribute nothing (no 404). No ids -> 400. Registered before /:id so 'dependencies' is never read as an id.
- GET /projects/:slug/issues/:id/comments -> IssueCommentListResponse { comments: IssueComment[] } (bd comments <id>); unknown id -> 404.
- Ids must match ISSUE_ID_PATTERN /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/ (refuses flag-like ids such as --help) else 400.

SHARED TYPES (packages/shared/src/issues.ts): IssueSummary { id, title, status, priority (0-4), type }; IssueFields extends it with description, acceptanceCriteria, notes, assignee, owner (string|null), labels string[], parentId, createdAt, createdBy, updatedAt, startedAt, closedAt, closeReason (string|null), commentCount, ready; Issue = IssueFields + dependencies: IssueDependency[]; IssueDetail = IssueFields + dependsOn: IssueLink[] + dependents: IssueLink[]; IssueLink = IssueSummary + dependencyType; IssueDependency { issueId, dependsOnId, type } (issueId depends on dependsOnId; no timestamps); IssueComment { id, issueId, author|null, text, createdAt|null }. IssueStatus/IssueType/IssueDependencyType are KNOWN_* unions widened with (string & {}). Helpers projectIssuesPath(slug), projectIssuePath(slug, id). ISSUE_ERROR_CODES / IssueErrorCode.

CACHE: per project id (also misses if the checkout path changed), ISSUE_LIST_TTL_MS = 3000 from when the load settles; concurrent callers share one in-flight load; failed loads are not cached; invalidate deletes the entry so a load already in flight is not reused by later callers. Only the list (list+ready snapshot) is cached; show/deps/comments always run bd.

ERROR MAPPING (body { error: { code, message } }): no .beads -> 422 no_issue_tracker (message names the path); unknown id -> 404 not_found (bd message matching /no issues? found matching/, from an { error } payload or stderr); bd non-zero exit or { error } payload with exit 0 -> 502 tracker_failed with bd's message (JSON error field preferred, else stderr minus 'warning:' lines and 'Error: ' prefix); non-JSON stdout -> 502 tracker_failed; bd not on PATH -> 503 tracker_unavailable; timeout -> 504 tracker_timeout; bad id/ids -> 400 invalid_request.

BD 1.2.2 QUIRKS FOUND: bd show <unknown> --json prints {"error": "no issues found matching the provided IDs"} on stdout and here exits 1 (older bd exited 0); the runner treats any { error } payload as failure regardless of exit code. bd dep list prints edge records ({issue_id, depends_on_id, type}) when >=2 ids resolve but issue rows with dependency_type when exactly one resolves (unknown ids are skipped with a stderr warning); service normalises both (single id -> rows mapped onto that id; multi-id batch where only one resolved -> per-id fallback). bd ready default limit is 100, so --limit 0. bd show of an epic has no 'dependents' key, hence the dep list --direction up call. Parallel bd reads on embedded Dolt do not conflict.

TESTS: service.test.ts fakes the runner with vi.fn<BdRunner>() returning fixture rows (cache window with injected now(), in-flight sharing, invalidation, path change, failed load not cached, ready mapping, dep-list shape normalisation). bd-runner.test.ts puts a fake bd shell script first on PATH via vi.stubEnv (exit-0 error payload, stderr message, non-JSON, timeout, missing binary) plus a real-workspace check. routes.test.ts runs createApp against a real temp workspace from createTempBeadsWorkspace(prefix) (src/issues/test-workspace.ts: mkdtemp + bd init --non-interactive --skip-agents --quiet, ~2s; helpers bd(...args) and create(title, ...flags)); real-bd suites skip when bd is not installed (hasBd).

VERIFIED: 23 tests in src/issues; root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (37 files / 248 tests), build pass. curl on tsx daemon port 5131 with throwaway CM_DATA_DIR and this repo registered: list 112 issues, ids and ready set identical to bd list/bd ready, first call ~1s then 2ms cached, re-runs after 3s; show epic -> dependents incl. 15 children; unknown id 404; --help id 400; deps for two ids -> 4 edges; comments 200; project without .beads 422 no_issue_tracker; unknown project 404.
close_reason: bd runner, read routes, 3s cache + invalidation verified against real bd; gates green

title: Add issue write endpoints including bulk update and comment editing
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Editing from the UI must go through `bd` so beads stays the only store. Add per-project write endpoints: create (title, type, priority, labels, parent, description, acceptance criteria, notes, assignee, dependencies), update fields (title, description, acceptance, notes, type, priority, labels, parent where an empty parent detaches, assignee, status), close with optional reason, a bulk update that applies one change to many ids server-side rather than a client loop, add comment, and edit comment. `bd` 1.2.2 cannot edit comments; keep v2's workaround of updating the comment row directly in the project's embedded Dolt database and reading it back, isolated behind one function so it can be replaced when `bd` gains the feature. Every write invalidates the list cache.
acceptance_criteria: Each endpoint's effect is visible through `bd show` or `bd list`; bulk update of five ids changes all five in one request; editing a comment persists and survives a `bd` restart; tests run against a temporary beads repo.
notes:
Issue write path decisions (UI beads 3.11-3.14 build on these). Also in apps/daemon/README.md "Issues".

FILES: apps/daemon/src/issues/writes.ts (createIssueWriter({ run?, reads?, editComment? }) -> IssueWriter; default issueWriter), write-routes.ts (issueWriteRoutes(writer = issueWriter), mounted in app.ts as app.route(PROJECTS_PATH, issueWriteRoutes()) after issueRoutes), write-validation.ts (body parsers -> 400 invalid_request), comment-edit.ts (CommentEditor, createDoltCommentEditor(run), editCommentInDolt). routes.ts now exports onIssueError (shared error mapping). No DB table/migration.

COMMON: every write runs bd through runBd with --actor=<c.var.actor.username> (so created_by / comment author / Dolt history name the platform user; 'admin' under the dev strategy) and calls reads.invalidate(projectId) (= invalidateIssueList) in a finally, so even partial failures drop the list cache. All values go as --flag=value so text starting with '-' is never read as a flag. Responses that return an issue re-read it with issuesService.show after invalidation (bd update/close output lacks parent). Errors: body validation 400 invalid_request; unknown issue 404 not_found; bd refusals 502 tracker_failed with bd's message (e.g. 'cannot close X: blocked by open issues [...] (use --force to override)', 'cannot close epic X: 1 open child issue(s)', invalid custom status/type); unknown project 404.

ROUTES (daemon paths; browser adds /api; path helpers in shared issues.ts):
- POST /projects/:slug/issues  body CreateIssueRequest { title (required, trimmed, <=500), type?, priority? 0-4, labels?: string[], parentId?: string|null, description?, acceptanceCriteria?, notes?, assignee?: string|null, dependsOn?: string[] } -> 201 CreateIssueResponse { issue: IssueDetail, warnings: string[] }. bd create, then one 'bd dep add <new> <dep>' per dependsOn id (bd create --deps only warns on refusal); refused edges (unknown id, 'epics can only block other epics') become warnings '<depId>: <bd message>' while the issue stays created. Parent labels are inherited (bd default). Helper projectIssuesPath(slug).
- PATCH /projects/:slug/issues/:id  body UpdateIssueRequest { title?, description?, acceptanceCriteria?, notes?, type?, priority?, labels?, parentId?, assignee?, status? } -> IssueResponse { issue }. Omitted = untouched; null or '' clears description/acceptance/notes/assignee; parentId null or '' DETACHES; labels replaces the whole set ([] clears by removing each current label because bd ignores an empty --set-labels). Empty body / unknown keys -> 400. status 'closed' here goes through bd update (no reason); use /close for a reason. Helper projectIssuePath(slug, id).
- POST /projects/:slug/issues/:id/close  body CloseIssueRequest { reason?: string|null, force?: boolean } (body optional) -> { issue }. force = bd close --force: closes despite open children or open blockers. Closing an already-closed issue is a no-op success (reason unchanged). Helper projectIssueClosePath(slug, id).
- POST /projects/:slug/issues/bulk  body BulkUpdateIssuesRequest { ids: string[] (1..MAX_BULK_ISSUE_IDS=200, deduped, full ids), changes: BulkIssueChanges { status?, priority?, type?, assignee?: string|null, parentId?: string|null (null detaches), addLabels?: string[], removeLabels?: string[] } } -> BulkUpdateIssuesResponse { updatedIds: string[], missingIds: string[] }. ONE 'bd update <ids...> <flags>' process for all ids. bd skips unknown ids (exit 0) and they come back in missingIds; all unknown -> 200 with every id in missingIds. A bd refusal on one id (e.g. a self-parent) can leave earlier ids updated and returns 502; the cache is still invalidated. Helper projectIssuesBulkPath(slug).
- POST /projects/:slug/issues/:id/comments  body IssueCommentRequest { text } (non-empty, <=30000) -> 201 IssueCommentResponse { comment: IssueComment }. Text goes through a temp file (bd comments add -f) since it is positional. Helper projectIssueCommentsPath(slug, id) (GET on the same path lists).
- PATCH /projects/:slug/issues/:id/comments/:commentId  body { text } -> { comment } as bd reads it back. commentId must match ISSUE_COMMENT_ID_PATTERN (bd uses UUIDs). 404 when the issue or the comment on THAT issue is unknown. Same text -> returns existing, no write. Helper projectIssueCommentPath(slug, id, commentId).
Limits: ISSUE_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH 500, ISSUE_TEXT_MAX_LENGTH 30000 (args are capped at 128 KiB by the OS); labels non-empty, no commas (bd splits on commas); type/status must be a word starting with a letter or digit; unknown type/status values pass to bd, which rejects them (502).

COMMENT EDIT (comment-edit.ts, the one function to replace when bd can edit comments): bd 1.2.2 has no comment edit and 'bd sql' says 'not yet supported in embedded mode'. editCommentInDolt(cwd, { issueId, commentId, text, actor }) runs 'bd dolt show --json' (needs embedded: true; gives data_dir e.g. .beads/embeddeddolt and database = prefix), then pipes to 'dolt --data-dir <data_dir> sql' on stdin: USE `db`; UPDATE comments SET text = CONVERT(X'<hex>' USING utf8mb4) WHERE id = <hex> AND issue_id = <hex>; CALL DOLT_ADD('comments'); CALL DOLT_COMMIT('--skip-empty','-m','bd: comment edit by <actor> [<id>]','--author','<actor> <<actor>@candy-mountain>'). User text is hex literals only (no SQL escaping). The writer first finds the comment via bd comments (404 if absent), then after the edit re-reads via bd comments and fails 502 if the text did not persist. Committing keeps the Dolt working set clean (verified dolt_status empty) and the edit shows in bd history. Concurrency: while a bd process holds the store the dolt CLI opens it read-only ('cannot update manifest: database is read only'); the editor retries up to 8 times with 150ms*n backoff (stress-tested with 6 parallel bd writes + 6 edits: all succeeded, no lost bd writes). LIMITS: needs the dolt binary on the daemon's PATH (else 503 tracker_unavailable); only embedded mode (server mode -> 502 'Comments can only be edited when bd uses its embedded Dolt database'); .beads/issues.jsonl reflects the edit only at bd's next auto-export; author and created_at are unchanged (no 'edited' marker).

WHAT THE UI SHOULD CALL:
- 3.11 inline field edit: PATCH projectIssuePath with only the changed field(s); use the returned issue to replace local state; parent picker sends parentId (null to detach); labels send the full array.
- 3.12 comments: list GET projectIssueCommentsPath; add POST same path { text } (201, returns comment); inline edit PATCH projectIssueCommentPath { text }.
- 3.13 bulk bar: POST projectIssuesBulkPath { ids, changes } once per action: add to epic { parentId: epicId }, remove from epic { parentId: null }, assign { assignee } (null unassigns), change status { status }; new epic = POST projectIssuesPath { title, type: 'epic' } then bulk { parentId: newId }. Show missingIds if non-empty; refetch the list (the cache is already invalidated, and 3.3's SSE 'changed' also fires).
- 3.14 write-it-yourself form: POST projectIssuesPath { title, type, priority, labels, parentId, description, acceptanceCriteria, dependsOn }; on 201 navigate to issue.id and toast any warnings.

TESTS: src/issues/writes.test.ts (fake runner: flag shapes incl. --title=--help and --actor last, label clearing, invalidation on failure, bulk single call + missingIds, all-missing, create dep warnings, comment edit read-back/not-found, non-embedded refusal). src/issues/write-routes.test.ts (real temp workspace via createTempBeadsWorkspace('wr'), createApp): create with every field + parent + 2 deps confirmed by bd show (created_by admin); refused dep -> warning; update every field + clear + detach confirmed by bd show; list reflects an update inside the cache window; close with reason / empty body; epic with open child refused then forced; bulk of five changes all five (bd list) incl. parent, then detach + removeLabels, unknown id -> missingIds; comment with leading dash; comment edit with quotes/backslash/unicode/newline/SQL-looking text survives a fresh bd read, neighbour untouched, bd writes still work after, dolt_status empty; comment on another issue -> 404; 16 x 400 cases. ~60s (real bd).

VERIFIED: 37 new tests pass. curl against built daemon (node dist/index.mjs, CM_DAEMON_PORT=5317, throwaway CM_DATA_DIR, temp bd project 'cv'): create with all fields/parent/2 deps -> 201, bd show matches; update/detach; close of blocked issue -> 502 with bd's message, force -> closed with reason; bulk of 5 -> all 5 changed in bd list; unknown bulk id -> missingIds; comment add/edit; after daemon restart GET comments and plain 'bd comments' show the edited text; dolt_log has 'bd: comment edit by admin [cv-vga.1]'. Root gates: see handoff (claude-acp lint/typecheck and 3.3 watcher test failures are other agents' in-flight work).
close_reason: Verified by agent against real bd / mocked API; gates green except in-flight files

title: Install the daemon and web server as a systemd user service through the CLI
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Jack runs on WSL now and a home server later; both use systemd, and a user service lets Candy Mountain survive reboots without root. Extend the CLI with install-service and uninstall-service commands that write a systemd user unit (or two units, implementer's choice) running the same start command the CLI uses, enable it, and enable lingering so it starts without a login session. Report clearly when systemd is not available (for example WSL without systemd enabled) instead of failing obscurely. Document the setup in the README.
acceptance_criteria: install-service creates and enables the unit; after a reboot the daemon and web app are running; uninstall-service removes it; running on a system without systemd prints an explanatory error.
notes:
Service decisions (full how-to in apps/cli/README.md).

COMMANDS
- candy-mountain install-service [--timeout s] / uninstall-service. One unit running the CLI's foreground 'run' supervisor (not two units).
- Code: apps/cli/src/unit-files.ts (paths, renderUnit, renderEnvFile, parseEnvFile), systemd.ts (checkSystemd detection, Runner, SystemdHost injectable for tests), service.ts (install/uninstall, routed start/stop/restart/status). main.ts wires them; MainContext gained home? and systemd? so tests never touch the real ~/.config.

UNIT: ~/.config/systemd/user/candy-mountain.service (always ~/.config, not $XDG_CONFIG_HOME, since the user manager decides its search path)
  [Unit] Description=Candy Mountain daemon and web server
  [Service] Type=simple, WorkingDirectory=<repo>, EnvironmentFile=<env file>, ExecStart=<process.execPath of the installing node> <repo>/apps/cli/dist/index.mjs run, Restart=on-failure, RestartSec=5, TimeoutStopSec=45 (run stops web then daemon with 15s grace each)
  [Install] WantedBy=default.target
  Paths are escaped (% -> %%, $ -> $$ in ExecStart, quoted if they contain spaces); line breaks rejected. No secrets in the unit.

ENV FILE: ~/.config/candy-mountain/service.env (dir 0700, file 0600). DEVIATION from the suggested <dataDir>/candy-mountain.env: apps/daemon/README.md says to keep CM_SECRETS_KEY outside the data directory (copying the data dir must not carry the key), and this file is where the key goes. Created only if missing (kept on reinstall) with CM_DATA_DIR, CM_DAEMON_HOST/PORT, CM_WEB_HOST/PORT resolved from the installing shell, PATH from the installing shell (systemd does not read the shell profile; daemon runs git/bd), and a commented '# CM_SECRETS_KEY=' placeholder. While the unit file exists, the CLI overlays the env file's CM_* values over the shell env for every command (and install-service always does when the file exists), so status/logs/health waits look where the service runs.

INSTALL RUNS, in order: checkSystemd (fails before writing anything); checks apps/cli/dist/index.mjs, apps/daemon/dist/index.mjs, apps/web/.output/server/index.mjs exist; stops a detached copy from 'candy-mountain start' if one runs; writes env file if missing; writes/updates unit; then
  systemctl --user is-active --quiet candy-mountain.service   (probe)
  systemctl --user daemon-reload
  systemctl --user enable --now candy-mountain.service
  systemctl --user restart candy-mountain.service   (only if it was active and the unit content changed)
  loginctl enable-linger $USER   (failure -> hint 'sudo loginctl enable-linger', exit 1, unit stays installed)
  then polls both health URLs up to --timeout (60s); on failure prints log tails and journalctl hint, exit 1.
Rerun install-service after an nvm node switch (the unit pins the absolute node path) or after moving the checkout.

UNINSTALL: not installed -> message, exit 0. Else systemctl --user disable --now candy-mountain.service; rm unit and default.target.wants link; systemctl --user daemon-reload; systemctl --user reset-failed candy-mountain.service (result ignored). Keeps the env file (may hold the key) and leaves lingering on (prints loginctl disable-linger hint). If systemd is unreachable it only removes the files.

ROUTING when the unit file exists: start -> systemctl --user start (refuses if already active) + health wait; stop -> systemctl --user stop; restart -> systemctl --user restart + health wait; status -> existing per-process lines plus 'service  candy-mountain.service  <is-active>, <is-enabled>'. If systemctl --user is unreachable those commands error and suggest uninstall-service. 'run' is never routed.

DETECTION (checkSystemd, in order): 'systemctl --version' cannot spawn -> no systemd; /run/systemd/system missing -> systemd not PID 1 (names /proc/1/comm); on WSL (WSL_DISTRO_NAME or 'microsoft' in osrelease) adds the /etc/wsl.conf [boot] systemd=true + 'wsl.exe --shutdown' steps; 'systemctl --user show-environment' non-zero -> user bus unreachable (quotes stderr, e.g. 'Failed to connect to bus'). Every message ends with 'candy-mountain start' as the fallback.

WSL PREREQUISITE: /etc/wsl.conf needs [boot] systemd=true (this machine currently has only [network] generateResolvConf=false; PID 1 is init(Ubuntu)), then wsl.exe --shutdown. Caveat documented: WSL only runs when something opens it and may stop an idle distro after the last terminal closes, so on WSL the service returns once WSL is running, not at Windows logon.

VERIFY AFTER REBOOT: systemctl --user status candy-mountain (active (running)); candy-mountain status (daemon/web running healthy + service active, enabled); loginctl show-user $USER --property=Linger (Linger=yes).

VERIFIED HERE: unit tests (unit-files.test.ts snapshots of unit + env file with fake paths, escaping; systemd.test.ts detection messages; service.test.ts install/route/uninstall through main with a fake systemctl that starts stand-in servers, and unavailable-systemd writes nothing). Live: node apps/cli/dist/index.mjs install-service on this WSL (no systemd) -> WSL explanation, exit 1, ~/.config/systemd and ~/.config/candy-mountain not created. uninstall-service live -> 'not installed', exit 0. NOT exercised live: real enable, reboot survival, linger, real uninstall (systemd is not running on this machine).
close_reason: Unit/env rendering and no-systemd error verified; live enable/reboot/uninstall need systemd (human test)

description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. title: Add the CLI that starts, stops, restarts and tails the daemon and web server
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Jack currently runs his tools from a dev server in an editor and wants Candy Mountain to run like an app. Add a small CLI (its own workspace package, installable as a binary) that manages the two built processes: the daemon and the web app's built Nitro server. Commands: start, stop, restart, status, and logs (tail). Start launches both processes detached from the terminal, records their pids and writes logs under the daemon's data directory; stop terminates them cleanly; status reports whether each is running and on which port. Ports and the data directory come from configuration shared with the daemon. Non-goals: service installation (separate work), development mode (already exists as a root script).
acceptance_criteria: After `pnpm build`, the CLI's start brings both processes up and they survive closing the terminal; status shows both running; logs tails the daemon log; stop ends both; restart cycles them.
notes:
CLI decisions (bead 1.17 builds on these):

PACKAGES
- apps/cli -> @candy-mountain/cli, bin `candy-mountain` (no short alias). tsdown bundle apps/cli/dist/index.mjs (shebang, chmod +x), bundles @candy-mountain/*, no third-party runtime deps. Built by root `pnpm build` (pnpm --recursive). Tests: apps/cli/src/*.test.ts (vitest project 'cli'; lifecycle test runs start/status/double-start/stop against stand-in node servers in a temp fake repo).
- NEW packages/config -> @candy-mountain/config (node-only, TS source, no build; vitest project 'config'). Shared by daemon and CLI: resolveDaemonAddress(env) {CM_DAEMON_HOST|127.0.0.1, CM_DAEMON_PORT|4310}, resolveWebAddress(env) {CM_WEB_HOST|127.0.0.1, CM_WEB_PORT|4300}, resolveDataDir(env), addressUrl(addr), connectHost(host) (0.0.0.0->127.0.0.1, ::->::1). Kept out of @candy-mountain/shared because shared is imported by browser code and this needs node:os/node:path.
- apps/daemon/src/config.ts now imports resolveDaemonAddress/resolveDataDir from @candy-mountain/config and re-exports resolveDataDir (drizzle.config.ts and tests unchanged). Daemon package.json gained "@candy-mountain/config": "workspace:*". dataPaths/ensureDataDir stay in the daemon; the CLI joins logs/ and run/ itself.
- web proxy (apps/web/server/utils/daemon-proxy.ts) still has its own fallback; the CLI always sets NUXT_DAEMON_URL so it is not relied on.

RUNNING IT
- Before install: `node apps/cli/dist/index.mjs <command>` (after pnpm build), from any cwd.
- Install: symlink the built file onto PATH, e.g. `ln -s "$PWD/apps/cli/dist/index.mjs" ~/.local/bin/candy-mountain` (verified). The CLI finds the repo from its own real path (dist/../../..), so it must stay inside the repo checkout and the symlink must point at it.
- Commands: start | stop | restart | status | logs [--web|--all] [-n N] [--no-follow] | run. Options: --timeout <s> (start/run health wait, default 60; stop wait before SIGKILL, default 15). help/-h.

START (detached)
- Refuses if apps/daemon/dist/index.mjs or apps/web/.output/server/index.mjs is missing, if either pid file points at a live process ("already running: daemon (pid N), web (pid N); use restart, or stop first", exit 1), or if either port already accepts connections (exit 1).
- mkdir -p dataDir, logs/, run/ (0700). Spawns `process.execPath <entry>` with detached:true (new session, setsid), stdio -> log file (append, 0600), unref. Daemon first, waits for GET <daemon>/health = {"status":"ok"}; then web, waits for GET <web>/api/health through the proxy. If either fails (exit or timeout) prints the reason + last 20 log lines, SIGTERMs what it started, exit 1.
- cwd: apps/daemon and apps/web respectively. Env: inherited env plus CM_DATA_DIR=<absolute resolved dir>, CM_DAEMON_HOST, CM_DAEMON_PORT (both children); web also HOST, PORT, NITRO_HOST, NITRO_PORT (=CM_WEB_HOST/CM_WEB_PORT, default 127.0.0.1:4300) and NUXT_DAEMON_URL=http://<daemon>. CM_SECRETS_KEY is only passed if it is in the caller's env.
- Files: <dataDir>/run/daemon.pid, <dataDir>/run/web.pid (JSON {pid, entry, host, port, startedAt, supervisor?}); <dataDir>/logs/daemon.log, <dataDir>/logs/web.log (each start appends a "--- <iso> starting <name> on <url> ---" line). No log rotation.
- Liveness = kill(pid,0) AND /proc/<pid>/cmdline contains the entry path AND not a zombie (guards pid reuse). Stale pid files are removed.

STOP: web then daemon; SIGTERM, poll up to --timeout (15s), then SIGKILL; removes pid files; "not running" is fine. Both apps exit 0 on SIGTERM (verified ~0.2s).
STATUS: one line per process: "daemon  running  http://127.0.0.1:4310  pid N  healthy" (or "not responding", plus "(foreground, supervisor pid N)" under run) or "web     stopped  <url>"; then data and logs dirs.
LOGS: `tail -n N [-F] <files>`; default daemon log, --web, --all.

EXIT CODES: 0 ok; 1 failure (already running, port in use, not built, failed to come up, could not signal, no log yet); 2 usage/invalid config (unknown command, bad flag, invalid CM_*_PORT); 3 status: at least one process not running.

FOREGROUND MODE FOR SYSTEMD (bead 1.17)
- `candy-mountain run` (= node <repo>/apps/cli/dist/index.mjs run): same pre-checks and health waits, but children are NOT detached; writes the same pid files with supervisor=<cli pid> so status/logs work; children still log to <dataDir>/logs/*.log (journald only sees the supervisor's few lines). On SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP: SIGTERMs web then daemon, waits, exits 0. If a child exits on its own: stops the other, exits 0 if the child exited with code 0 (e.g. `candy-mountain stop` was used) else 1 (crash -> Restart=on-failure restarts). Verified: SIGTERM -> 0, daemon SIGKILL -> 1, cli stop -> 0.
- Suggested unit: Type=simple, ExecStart=<abs path to node> <repo>/apps/cli/dist/index.mjs run, WorkingDirectory=<repo> (not strictly required; the CLI resolves paths from its own location), Restart=on-failure, KillMode=control-group (default), TimeoutStopSec>15. Environment/EnvironmentFile for CM_SECRETS_KEY, CM_DATA_DIR, ports; PATH must include node's dir only if relying on /usr/bin/env node (use absolute node path instead, it is nvm here: ~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.x/bin/node). The repo checkout and built output must exist (daemon reads apps/daemon/drizzle at runtime).
- When the service is installed, `start`/`restart` from the CLI would launch detached copies outside systemd (start refuses while the unit's processes run, but restart would stop them then detach new ones); 1.17 should route start/stop/restart to systemctl --user when the unit is installed/active.

VERIFIED (CM_DATA_DIR in scratchpad, CM_DAEMON_PORT=4711, CM_WEB_PORT=4710): start (1.1s) -> status both healthy, curl :4710/api/health {"status":"ok"}, children have own session (SID=PID, no tty); start inside `script` pty that then closed -> both survived; double start refused (exit 1); port-in-use refused; logs (no-follow, follow, --web, --all); restart; stop (0.2s) -> ports free, status exit 3; symlinked bin works from /. pnpm lint, typecheck, test (106), build, daemon db:check all pass.
close_reason: CLI start/stop/restart/status/logs/run verified end to end; gates green

title: Build the project picker with URL-scoped selection
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Every page in later phases is per project and must be linkable, so the selected project is part of the URL rather than hidden state. Build the picker in the header: it lists projects grouped by organisation with ungrouped projects in a final group at the bottom, shows each project's colour and name, and offers search when the list is long. Organisations are headings, not selectable. Selecting a project navigates to the same page for that project. Routes that need a project carry its slug as a path segment; a composable exposes the selected project to any page. Remember the last selected project so opening the app root sends Jack there; when nothing was ever selected, open the Projects system page. Non-goals: project CRUD UI.
acceptance_criteria: The picker groups projects by organisation with ungrouped last; selecting a project changes the URL; reloading keeps the selection; opening the root URL goes to the last project; organisations cannot be selected.
notes:
Project picker + URL scoping decisions (later beads rely on these):

ROUTES
- Project-scoped pages live under /p/<slug>/..., route param name 'project' (PROJECT_ROUTE_PREFIX='/p', PROJECT_ROUTE_PARAM='project' in app/utils/project-scope.ts, auto-imported).
- app/pages/p/[project].vue is the PARENT route for every project page: layout 'dashboard' (inherited by children via route meta), awaits the project list, renders <NuxtPage/> only when the slug is an active (non-archived) project, else a 'Project not found' UEmpty (SSR 404) or 'Couldn't load projects' on daemon error. Children never need to handle a missing project.
- app/pages/p/[project]/index.vue = project home placeholder (overview card: org, path, beads/remote facts).
- Capability pages: add pages/p/[project]/<capability>.vue (or <capability>/index.vue, <capability>/[id].vue) — from a layer too; they nest automatically. e.g. /p/acme-api/issues. Each renders its own UDashboardPanel.
- Build links with projectPath(slug, ...segments) -> '/p/<slug>/<segments>' (e.g. projectPath(slug, 'issues')). Do not hardcode '/p'.
- Root '/' (app/pages/index.vue) is a redirect only (inline route middleware): last project -> /p/<slug>, else PROJECTS_PAGE_PATH '/projects'. Works in SSR (302). The old Home/health card page is gone.

COMPOSABLES (app/composables/useSelectedProject.ts)
- useSelectedProject() -> { slug: ComputedRef<string|null> (from route param), project: ComputedRef<Project|null>, projects, organisations, groups: ComputedRef<ProjectGroup[]>, status: ComputedRef<'pending'|'success'|'error'>, loaded: Promise<void>, refresh(), switchPath(otherSlug): string, select(otherSlug) (navigateTo switchPath) }.
- useProjectDirectory() -> same data minus slug/project/switchPath/select. Uses useApi with fixed keys PROJECT_DIRECTORY_KEYS ['project-directory:projects','project-directory:organisations'] (GET /projects default = archived excluded, GET /organisations), so all callers share one fetch. After mutating projects/orgs elsewhere (Projects page), call useProjectDirectory().refresh() or refreshNuxtData(PROJECT_DIRECTORY_KEYS) so the picker updates (the picker also refreshes whenever it opens).
- useLastProjectSlug() -> useCookie<string|null>.

SAME PAGE, OTHER PROJECT
- switchPath(slug) = projectSwitchPath(route.matched.at(-1)?.path, slug): swaps the slug and keeps the static segments after it, stopping at the first dynamic segment (item ids belong to the old project); query and hash dropped. /p/a/issues -> /p/b/issues; /p/a/issues/:id -> /p/b/issues; from non-project pages (/projects, /settings) -> /p/b.

LAST SELECTION
- Cookie 'cm-last-project' (LAST_PROJECT_COOKIE), Max-Age 1y, Path=/, SameSite=Lax; cookie (not localStorage) so the root redirect works during SSR. Set by the [project].vue parent whenever a valid project is shown (also during SSR); cleared when the remembered slug turns out to be missing/archived (not on daemon errors).

PICKER / COMPONENTS
- app/components/ProjectPicker.vue: USelectMenu (ghost, value-key 'value') in the header, rendered from layouts/dashboard.vue via AppHeader's #project slot. Items from projectPickerItems(groupProjectsByOrganisation(projects, organisations)): organisations sorted by name as type:'label' headings (not selectable), empty orgs omitted, ungrouped projects last under 'Ungrouped' (heading omitted when there are no org groups), projects sorted by name then slug, archived excluded, orphaned organisationId -> ungrouped. Search input appears when > PROJECT_PICKER_SEARCH_THRESHOLD (8) projects. Footer 'Manage projects' -> /projects. Zero projects -> 'Add a project' button to /projects. Outside a project route it shows placeholder 'Select a project'.
- app/components/ProjectColorDot.vue (prop color: hex) — reusable colour swatch.
- Pure helpers + types in app/utils/project-scope.ts (ProjectGroup, ProjectPickerItem, groupProjectsByOrganisation, projectPickerItems, projectPath, projectSwitchPath, constants). Unit tests: apps/web/test/unit/project-scope.test.ts.

VERIFIED: dev and prod builds, daemon on 4932/4942 with temp CM_DATA_DIR, 2 orgs + archived project + 10 projects; headless chromium: grouping order, org heading click does nothing, select changes URL, reload keeps selection, root redirects to last project (and to /projects with no cookie), search filters, daemon-unreachable state still shows and recovers on /p/<slug>. Root lint/typecheck/test/build pass.
close_reason: Picker, /p/<slug> routes, cookie-remembered selection verified in browser; gates green

title: Build the Projects system page with inline organisation management
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Jack needs to register and maintain codebases from the UI. Build the Projects page in the sidebar's system group: a list of projects (name, colour, organisation, path, beads-present and git-remote facts, archived state), a create/edit form (name, slug auto-derived but editable, colour, organisation, local path) that surfaces the daemon's verification result inline, and archive and delete actions with confirmation. Organisations are managed inline on the same page (create, rename, delete) rather than on a separate page. Use Nuxt UI primitives.
acceptance_criteria: Creating two organisations and four projects from the page works end to end; a project at a path without `.beads` shows that fact; editing a path re-verifies; archiving hides the project from the picker; deleting an organisation ungroups its projects in the list.
notes:
Projects page decisions (picker bead 1.13 and later beads rely on these).

FILES (apps/web/app)
- pages/projects.vue: dashboard layout, UDashboardPanel id=projects. Navbar right: 'Show archived (n)' USwitch + 'New project' button. Body: grouped project list (left) + Organisations card (right, stacks below on mobile). Fetches useProjects({ includeArchived: true }) and filters archived client-side (hidden by default). Groups = organisations (only those with visible projects, in daemon order) then 'No organisation' last (projects with null or unknown organisationId). Row actions: Edit, Re-check path (POST /projects/:slug/verify), Archive (confirm) / Unarchive, Delete (confirm). Action errors show as an inline UAlert (message + code); save results as a toast summarising the facts.
- components/projects/ (auto-imported with the Projects prefix deduped):
  ProjectsList (props groups: ProjectGroup[] {id,label,projects}; emits edit/verify/archive/unarchive/delete),
  ProjectsVerificationFacts (prop verification: PathVerification; badges 'Path not found' | 'Issue tracker'/'No issue tracker' (tooltip names .beads) + 'Remote: <name>' (tooltip = remoteUrl)/'No git remote'/'Not a git repo'),
  ProjectsFormModal (v-model:open, props project: Project|null (null = create), organisations; emits saved(project, created)),
  ProjectsColorPicker (v-model hex; PROJECT_COLOR_PALETTE swatches, plus the current colour if it is off-palette),
  ProjectsOrganisations (props organisations, projects; inline create/rename/delete),
  ProjectsConfirmModal (useOverlay target; props title, description, confirmLabel, color; emits close(boolean)).
- composables/useProjects.ts: useProjects({ includeArchived? }) -> useApi result + projects: ComputedRef<Project[]>; keys PROJECTS_DATA_KEY='projects' (default list, archived excluded) and ALL_PROJECTS_DATA_KEY='projects:all'. refreshProjectData() = refreshNuxtData() (no keys).
- composables/useOrganisations.ts: useOrganisations() -> useApi result + organisations computed; key ORGANISATIONS_DATA_KEY='organisations'.
- utils/apiError.ts: toApiError(error) -> { code, message } from the daemon's {error:{code,message}} body ('unknown' otherwise).
- apps/web/package.json: added zod ^4.6.7 (already in the lockfile via @mastra/core) for UForm schemas.

FORM SCHEMA (zod, UForm): name trim 1..200; slug trim, required, <= SLUG_MAX_LENGTH, SLUG_PATTERN; color PROJECT_COLOR_PATTERN; organisationId string with sentinel 'none' -> null (reka Select cannot hold null/''); path trim, required, must start with '/' or '~' (daemon still normalises). Create: slug auto-follows slugify(name) until the user types in the slug field; slug is only sent if the user edited it, so an untouched slug lets the daemon auto-suffix on collision. Edit: slug never follows the name (matches daemon); slug sent only if changed; PATCH always sends source so the daemon re-verifies. Error code -> field: slug_taken->slug, invalid_path/path_not_found->path, organisation_not_found->organisationId (form.setErrors); anything else -> UAlert at the top of the form. Org create/rename: zod name 1..200; create omits slug (daemon derives + suffixes); rename PATCHes name only; errors inline under the field. Org delete confirm states how many projects become ungrouped.

VERIFICATION PREVIEW: watching the path field; on change the old facts clear and 'Checking path...' shows immediately, then after 400 ms POST /projects/verify-path; stale responses are dropped via a request counter; the result renders ProjectsVerificationFacts in the path field's help slot (data-testid=path-preview). Edit mode starts with the stored verification labelled 'as last saved'. Non-absolute paths skip the preview (schema message instead). The facts returned by POST/PATCH are shown in the list row and the success toast.

FOR THE PICKER (1.13): every mutation on this page calls refreshProjectData() -> refreshNuxtData() with no keys, so the picker's useApi/useAsyncData refreshes whatever key it uses (verified: header switched from 'Add a project' to the select menu after the first create without reload; an archived project disappeared from the picker options). The picker's useProjectDirectory currently fetches with its own keys (project-directory:*); it could reuse useProjects()/useOrganisations() to share the cache and dedupe requests, but nothing depends on that. Note a slug edit here changes the URL slug of that project; the picker's selected slug in the URL/cookie can go stale after a rename or delete.

VERIFIED: headless Chromium (playwright-core) against nuxt dev + tsx daemon on 5140/5141 with a throwaway CM_DATA_DIR: 30/30 checks (2 orgs + 4 projects created through the UI; slug auto-derived incl. accent stripping; .beads/remote facts for 4 fixture repos incl. 'No issue tracker' for a plain dir; slug_taken, path_not_found, relative path shown inline; edit path re-verifies in preview and after save; archive hides from page list, default GET /projects and the header picker; show-archived + unarchive; org rename; org delete ungroups projects; project delete; no horizontal overflow at 390px). SSR /projects checked against the production build (built daemon + .output) on 5150/5151. Root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (248), build all pass.
close_reason: Projects page + inline orgs verified in browser (30/30); gates green

title: Add the login page and session handling in the web app
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

The daemon offers a password strategy with a session cookie; the web app needs the page that uses it. Add a login page (username and password, Nuxt UI form) that posts through the proxy, a route middleware that redirects unauthenticated visitors to it and back to where they were going afterwards, a current-user composable, and a logout action in the header. When the daemon runs the development strategy the login page must be skipped entirely. Non-goals: registration, password reset.
acceptance_criteria: Visiting any page unauthenticated redirects to login and returns to the original URL after success; a wrong password shows an inline error; logout returns to the login page; with the dev strategy no login is required.
notes:
Login/session decisions (web, apps/web/app).
COMPOSABLE: useCurrentUser() (composables/useCurrentUser.ts) -> { user: Ref<Actor|null> (useState 'current-user'), loaded: Ref<boolean> (useState 'current-user-loaded'), fetchUser(): GET /api/auth/me via $api, 401 -> null, other errors (daemon down) rethrown, setUser(actor|null) }. Pages read the actor with useCurrentUser().user.value (Actor from shared). SSR-aware: fetched once server-side with the forwarded cookie, hydrated to client.
MIDDLEWARE: middleware/auth.global.ts. Fetches the user once (cached by loaded); if signed out, reads GET /api/auth/strategy; redirects to /login?redirect=<encoded fullPath> ONLY for strategy 'password'. development/trusted-header never see login (/login itself redirects to / for them). Signed-in user hitting /login is sent to the redirect target. Daemon errors (502 unreachable, strategy fetch failure) make the middleware return without redirecting so app.vue's unreachable state shows (verified on /login too). Pure decision logic in utils/auth-redirect.ts: decideAuthRedirect, safeRedirectTarget (same-origin paths only, never /login), loginPathFor, LOGIN_PAGE_PATH='/login', LOGIN_REDIRECT_QUERY='redirect'; unit tests test/unit/auth-redirect.test.ts.
LOGIN: pages/login.vue, route /login, definePageMeta layout:false (no sidebar), UForm+zod, POST /api/auth/login, invalid_credentials shown inline in a UAlert, then setUser + navigateTo(safeRedirectTarget(query.redirect)).
LOGOUT: components/AppLogout.vue in the dashboard layout AppHeader #actions slot (after UColorModeButton). Shown only when strategy is password (useApi key 'auth-strategy') and a user is loaded; POST /api/auth/logout, setUser(null), navigateTo('/login'). Button aria-label 'Sign out', label = displayName.
LIMITS: a session expiring mid-visit is only noticed on next full load/login nav (client caches user); 401s from other API calls are not globally handled.
VERIFIED: daemon password strategy + built web: curl SSR 302 to /login?redirect=..., headless chromium wrong password inline error, right password back to /settings?x=1, logout to /login and guard re-applies; unreachable state shows on /login; development strategy: no login, /login -> /, no logout button.
close_reason: Login/redirect/logout verified in browser and SSR; dev strategy skips login

title: Add projects and organisations with path verification
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

A project is a registered codebase and the unit everything else is scoped to; organisations exist only to group projects in a picker and can never be selected. Add both to the platform database and expose them over REST: an organisation has a name and a stable slug; a project has a name, a stable slug, a colour, an optional organisation, an archived flag, and a source. The only source kind in v3 is a local path, but the source must be modelled so a managed-clone kind can be added later without a migration of meaning. On create and update the daemon verifies the local path exists, records whether it contains a `.beads` directory and whether it is a git repository with a remote (and the remote URL), and returns those facts with the project; verification can be re-run on demand. Support list, create, update, archive and delete for projects, and list, create, update and delete for organisations (deleting an organisation leaves its projects ungrouped). Slugs must be unique and URL-safe. Non-goals: no UI, no cloning.
acceptance_criteria: Creating a project with a non-existent path fails with a clear error; a project pointing at a repo with `.beads` and a remote reports both facts; archived projects are excluded from the default list; organisation deletion ungroups projects; tests cover verification and slug uniqueness.
notes:
Projects/organisations decisions (later beads depend on these). Short how-to also in apps/daemon/README.md "Projects and organisations".

ROUTES (daemon paths; web proxy maps /api/* -> daemon /*, so the browser calls /api/projects etc.)
Constants PROJECTS_PATH='/projects', ORGANISATIONS_PATH='/organisations' (shared).
- GET    /projects[?includeArchived=true]   -> 200 ProjectListResponse { projects: Project[] } (archived excluded by default; ordered by name, slug)
- POST   /projects  CreateProjectRequest { name, slug?, color?, organisationId?: string|null, source: { kind:'local-path', path } } -> 201 ProjectResponse { project }
- POST   /projects/verify-path  VerifyPathRequest { path } -> 200 VerifyPathResponse { verification } (preview, saves nothing)
- GET    /projects/:slug -> 200 { project }
- PATCH  /projects/:slug  UpdateProjectRequest { name?, slug?, color?, organisationId?: string|null, source? } -> 200 { project } (always re-verifies)
- POST   /projects/:slug/verify -> 200 { project } (re-runs verification on demand and stores it)
- POST   /projects/:slug/archive | /unarchive -> 200 { project } (idempotent)
- DELETE /projects/:slug -> 204 (hard delete)
- GET    /organisations -> 200 OrganisationListResponse { organisations }
- POST   /organisations  CreateOrganisationRequest { name, slug? } -> 201 OrganisationResponse { organisation }
- GET    /organisations/:slug -> 200 { organisation }
- PATCH  /organisations/:slug  UpdateOrganisationRequest { name?, slug? } -> 200 { organisation }
- DELETE /organisations/:slug -> 204; its projects get organisationId=null (ungrouped) in the same transaction (FK is also ON DELETE SET NULL).
Errors: ApiErrorBody { error: { code, message } }. Codes (ProjectErrorCode): invalid_request 400 (bad JSON/shape/slug/colour/name), not_found 404, slug_taken 409, invalid_path 422 (relative path), path_not_found 422 (missing or not a directory), organisation_not_found 422.

SHARED TYPES: import from '@candy-mountain/shared' (packages/shared/src/projects.ts, slug.ts, api-error.ts).
Project { id, slug, name, color, organisationId: string|null, archived: boolean, archivedAt: string|null, source: ProjectSource, verification: PathVerification, createdAt, updatedAt } (ISO strings; id is a UUID).
Organisation { id, slug, name, createdAt, updatedAt }.
ProjectSource = LocalPathSource { kind:'local-path', path } (PROJECT_SOURCE_KINDS = ['local-path']). Add managed-clone as a new union member; stored as JSON so no column change.
PathVerification { checkedAt, pathExists (false if missing or not a dir), hasBeads (<path>/.beads is a dir), isGitRepo (git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree), hasRemote, remoteName ('origin' if present else first remote), remoteUrl (http(s) credentials stripped) }.
Also: PROJECT_COLOR_PATTERN /^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/, PROJECT_COLOR_PALETTE (10 hex swatches; default colour is picked from it by slug hash), isApiErrorBody, request/response types above.

SLUG RULES: SLUG_PATTERN /^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/, SLUG_MAX_LENGTH 64, isValidSlug(), slugify() (NFKD, strip accents, lowercase, non-alnum runs -> '-'). Omitted slug is derived from the name and auto-suffixed -2, -3... on collision; an explicit slug that is taken -> 409 slug_taken. Name changes never change the slug; slugs change only via an explicit PATCH. Project slugs and organisation slugs are separate namespaces; archived projects keep their slug reserved.

PATHS: must be absolute after ~ expansion; normalised with path.resolve (trailing slash removed). Create/update fail if the (new) path is missing; updates that don't change the path still re-verify but don't fail; /verify records pathExists:false rather than failing.

DAEMON MODULE: apps/daemon/src/projects (index.ts re-exports).
- projects.ts: listProjects(db, {includeArchived?}), findProjectBySlug(db, slug) -> Project|null, getProjectBySlug(db, slug) (throws ProjectError not_found), findProjectById, createProject(db, req) async, updateProject(db, slug, req) async, reverifyProject(db, slug) async, archiveProject, unarchiveProject, deleteProject, sourcePath(source) -> checkout path (use this rather than source.path so managed-clone can slot in).
- organisations.ts: listOrganisations, findOrganisationBySlug/ById, getOrganisationBySlug, createOrganisation, updateOrganisation, deleteOrganisation (all sync).
- verification.ts: verifyPath(path) async, normaliseProjectPath(raw). errors.ts: ProjectError(code, message) with .status. routes.ts: projectRoutes(), organisationRoutes() (mounted in app.ts). test-repos.ts: createTempRepos() test helper making temp dirs with .beads/git/remotes.
Tables (src/db/schema/projects.ts): organisations(id PK, slug unique, name, created_at, updated_at); projects(id PK, slug unique, name, color, organisation_id FK->organisations ON DELETE SET NULL, archived_at nullable, source JSON, verification JSON, created_at, updated_at). Tables referencing projects later should use ON DELETE CASCADE on project_id since project delete is a hard delete.

MIGRATION: apps/daemon/drizzle/0001_projects.sql (tag 0001_projects).

VERIFIED: 24 tests in src/projects (verification, slug uniqueness, archive filtering, org-delete ungroup, HTTP routes) + shared slug tests; root pnpm lint/typecheck/test (71)/build pass; curl against built daemon (CM_DATA_DIR temp, port 4399) confirmed every route.
close_reason: Verified by agent; root gates green

title: Show a clear state when the daemon is unreachable
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

The daemon and the web app are separate processes; when the daemon is stopped the web app must not render a blank page or a wall of failed requests. Detect that the proxy cannot reach the daemon (connection refused or timeout), surface a full-page "daemon unreachable" state with the configured daemon address and a retry action, and recover automatically when the daemon returns. Ordinary API errors (4xx, 5xx from the daemon itself) are not this state.
acceptance_criteria: Stopping the daemon while the app is open shows the unreachable state within a few seconds; starting it again restores the app without a manual reload; a 500 from the daemon does not trigger the state.
notes: Daemon-unreachable decisions: MARKING: proxyToDaemon (apps/web/server/utils/daemon-proxy.ts) catches a failed upstream connection (refused/timeout; h3 proxyRequest throws only then) and answers 502 + header x-cm-daemon-unreachable: 1 + JSON {error:{code:'daemon_unreachable',message},daemonUrl}. Daemon-produced 4xx/5xx (even 502) pass through unmarked. Contract in packages/shared/src/daemon-unreachable.ts (DAEMON_UNREACHABLE_HEADER, DaemonUnreachableBody, isDaemonUnreachableResponse = status 502 AND header, isDaemonUnreachableBody). DETECTION: app/plugins/api.ts $api onResponseError calls reportDaemonError. STATE: useDaemonStatus() in app/composables/useDaemonStatus.ts -> { status: useState 'daemon-status' {unreachable, daemonUrl}, check() }; daemonUrl comes only from the unreachable response body.
