- Effort High: a second divider, and the launch has --settings {"effortLevel":"high"}.
- Reload replays all 3 sessions in order with both dividers.
- Mocked 409 thread_busy -> toast, and the select reverts. Mid-turn the selects are disabled, and a direct PATCH gets 409 thread_busy.
- Choosing Haiku in a draft creates the thread with model haiku (no divider).
- Codex: no selectors. At 390px there is no horizontal overflow. No console errors other than the mocked 409.
- Re-ran after 4.11's new Transcript landed: all pass.

title: Build the shared chat layer: rail, panel, threads and prompt bar
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Chat must be reachable from every page without leaving it. Build the shared `chat` Nuxt layer (infrastructure, not a capability) mounted by the dashboard layout: a rail on the right edge listing the agents the registry says the actor may chat with for the selected project (avatar, unread and working indicators, a "+" to start a thread), and a panel that opens from the rail with the thread list for the chosen agent, the transcript area (filled by separate work; render raw events as text for now), and a prompt bar with send and cancel. Threads are per actor and per project; switching project switches the rail. Support a deep link to a thread (query parameter) that opens the panel on load. The panel subscribes to the session's SSE stream with replay from the last seen sequence and reconnects on drop. Design the layer so bot agents and a native platform agent can appear later as entries in the same rail with no changes to the layer.
acceptance_criteria: The rail shows Claude Code and Codex for a project with both plugins healthy and nothing for a project without them; starting a thread and sending a prompt streams the reply; a reload mid-turn shows the full transcript and the turn finishes; the deep link opens the thread; lint passes.
notes:
Shared chat layer decisions (4.11 transcript, 4.12 model/effort, 5.1/5.2 seeded threads, 6.14 bots, 10.8 platform agent build on these). Layer: apps/web/layers/chat (prefix Chat; mounted by core via ONE line in app/layouts/dashboard.vue: <ChatDock /> after <slot /> inside the flex row).

COMPONENTS (layers/chat/app/components, auto-registered as Chat*):
• ChatDock (Dock.vue): the one mount point; computes rail entries once (useChatRailEntries) and runs useChatDeepLink, renders <ChatPanel :entries/> then <ChatRail :entries/> (fragment, both flex children of the dashboard row).
• ChatRail (Rail.vue): right-edge 3rem strip, data-testid chat-rail; hidden when there are no entries (no project, no chattable agents). Top '+' (chat-rail-new) = UDropdownMenu listing entries -> startThread(entry) (draft panel). One UButton per entry (chat-rail-entry-<id>, icon = entry.avatar) wrapped in UChip: shown when unread or working, color primary when working (data-working) else error (data-unread); tooltip '<label> (working|unread)'. Click toggles the panel on that entry.
• ChatPanel (Panel.vue): data-testid chat-panel; aside, fixed full-screen under md, static 26rem with border-l from md. Renders entry.panel (custom component, prop entry) or ChatAgentPanel. Escape closes. If the deep-linked entry is not (yet) in entries it falls back to { id, label: id, avatar: CHAT_DEFAULT_AVATAR, agentId: id }.
• ChatAgentPanel (AgentPanel.vue): default panel for registry agents. Header (chat-panel-title, chat-panel-back, chat-panel-new, chat-panel-close). Views: thread list (ChatThreadList) when no thread/draft; else ChatTranscript + ChatPromptBar. Draft = no thread yet: first send does POST threads {agentId} then POST prompt, then showThread. Mark-read: watch on [threadId, listed.unread] -> POST read whenever the shown thread is unread (on open and again after each turn end). Turn end (session.working true->false) -> threads.refresh() so flags/titles follow.
• ChatThreadList (ThreadList.vue): rows chat-thread-<id> with data-unread/data-working, title ?? 'Untitled thread', chatRelativeTime(lastActivityAt), spinner when working; UEmpty with 'New thread' action when empty.
• ChatTranscript (Transcript.vue) = THE 4.11 BOUNDARY. Props ChatTranscriptProps { events: readonly AgentSessionEvent[], working: boolean, connected?: boolean }. Today: one div per row (data-kind, data-seq) with chatEventText(event) (prompt/text/reasoning verbatim, every other kind as 'kind …json'), side via chatEventSide (user right / agent left / system mono), auto-scroll on new rows, 'Working' line (chat-working) while working, 'Reconnecting' when the stream dropped. 4.11 replaces this file only (and may drop the chatEvents.ts helpers); decision rows (decision_opened/answered/expired) already arrive in events, answer via sessionDecisionPath on the session id from useChatThread().session.
• ChatPromptBar (PromptBar.vue): UChatPrompt (data-testid chat-prompt lands on the textarea) + UChatPromptSubmit (chat-prompt-submit; status 'streaming' while working -> stop emits cancel). Props { working, error?: string|null }; emits send(text) (trimmed, ignored while working) and cancel. Named slot 'options' rendered inside UChatPrompt's #footer = THE 4.12 HOOK: put the model/effort USelects there; thread.model/effort are on the thread, options via GET chatAgentOptionsPath(slug, agentId) (no composable yet), change via useChatThreads().update(threadId, { model, effort }) which PATCHes, then useChatThread(...).refresh() -> new session id -> the SSE reopens from seq 0 (chat_thread_sessions history is in useChatThread().sessions for dividers). Expect thread_busy 409 while working.

COMPOSABLES (layers/chat/app/composables):
• useChatThreads(slug, agentId?) -> { threads (computed, filtered to registry.project.id and agentId, newest activity first), enabled, status, error, refresh, create({agentId,title?,model?,effort?}), prompt(id,text), cancel(id), markRead(id), update(id,{title?,model?,effort?}) }. One useAsyncData per project (key chatThreadsDataKey(slug) = 'chat-threads:<slug>'), unfiltered GET /projects/:slug/threads, run only when registry.agents is non-empty (awaits useProjectRegistry().loaded; watch: [enabled]); otherwise { threads: [] }. Every action patches the returned thread into the list so rail flags update at once.
• useChatThread(slug, threadId) -> { thread, session, sessions, status, error, refresh } (key 'chat-thread:<slug>:<id>', GET thread; null when no id; stale answers for another id are hidden).
• useChatSession(slug, sessionId) -> { events (shallowReadonly ref), status (SSE status event), connected, working (chatIsWorking(status)), close }. Client only (opens in onMounted, watches [slug, sessionId], closes on scope dispose). EventSource on '/api' + sessionEventsPath(slug, id, lastSeq); drops rows with seq <= lastSeq; on error closes and reopens itself with after=lastSeq after 1s doubling to 15s (the browser's own retry would replay from the original after). Never touches $api, so a dropped stream cannot trip useDaemonStatus.
• useChatPanel() -> { state: useState('chat-panel') { slug, entryId, threadId, draft }, open (entryId set AND state.slug === current slug), openEntry(id), startThread(id), showThread(entryId, threadId), showList(), close() }. showThread mirrors the id into ?thread= via router.replace (other query keys kept); showList/close/openEntry/startThread remove it.
• useChatDeepLink(): resets state when slug changes; on the client watches route.query.thread (immediate): GET thread -> showThread(thread.agentId, id); a failed GET (unknown id, agent no longer chattable) is ignored.
• useChatRailEntries() -> { entries, threads }: agents from chatAgentRailEntries(registry.agents, threads) (order 0) + chatRailSources() entries, flattened by order; polls threads.refresh() every CHAT_THREADS_POLL_MS 15s while enabled and the tab is visible.

RAIL ENTRY REGISTRATION POINT (6.14 bots, 10.x platform agent) in layers/chat/app/utils/chatRail.ts:
• ChatRailEntry { id (unique across sources; agents use the registry agent id, so namespace others e.g. 'bot:<id>'), label, description?, avatar (Iconify), unread?, working?, agentId? (registry agent id: the default ChatAgentPanel lists/prompts its threads), panel? (Component, markRaw; replaces the panel body, receives prop entry) }.
• chatRailRegister({ id, use: () => MaybeRefOrGetter<ChatRailEntry[]>, order? }) from a Nuxt plugin in the contributing layer, e.g. layers/bots/app/plugins/chat-rail.ts: export default defineNuxtPlugin(() => chatRailRegister({ id: 'bots', use: useBotsRailEntries })). The use() function runs once inside ChatDock's setup (so it may call useAsyncData/useSelectedProject and must be project-aware itself); order lower first, registry agents are 0, default 100. Capability -> chat imports/auto-imports are allowed by cm-layers; the chat layer never imports back.
• Platform agent (10.x): if it is a registry agent (RegistryAgent with family/avatar) it appears with NO work here; its threads go through the same thread routes. 10.8 start-chat action = useChatPanel().startThread(agentId) or showThread(agentId, threadId); navigate = navigateTo(chatThreadLink(threadId, path)).

DEEP LINK (5.1/5.2): '?thread=<threadId>' on any project page (/p/<slug>/...). Helpers in utils/chatLinks.ts: CHAT_THREAD_QUERY='thread', chatThreadLink(threadId, path?) -> RouteLocationRaw ({ query } on the current page, or { path, query }). Seeded flow: POST threads { agentId, title? } -> POST threads/:id/prompt { text } -> navigateTo(chatThreadLink(thread.id, projectPath(slug))) or, on the same page, useChatPanel().showThread(agentId, thread.id). Verified on /p/alpha/setup/plugins?thread=... (panel opens, page stays).

UTILS: chatEvents.ts (CHAT_WORKING_STATUSES queued/starting/prompting, chatIsWorking, chatEventSide, chatEventText), chatLinks.ts (above + chatThreadsDataKey/chatThreadDataKey, CHAT_THREADS_POLL_MS), chatRail.ts (above + CHAT_DEFAULT_AVATAR 'i-lucide-bot', chatAgentRailEntries, chatRailSources), chatTime.ts (chatRelativeTime). Unit tests layers/chat/test/unit/chat.test.ts (7).

VERIFIED 2026-10-28: daemon from source (tsx) on 127.0.0.1:7600 with throwaway CM_DATA_DIR, random CM_SECRETS_KEY, development auth; projects alpha (agent-hub, claude-code instance with config.claudePath = a scratch fake claude speaking stream-json: echo, 'slow:<ms>' two-part reply, interrupt-aware; codex instance) and beta (agent-hub, no plugins); both instances set healthy in sqlite. Built web (.output copied to scratch) on :7601 with CM_DAEMON_PORT=7600. Headless Chromium (playwright-core 1.59 + chromium-1217): rail shows Claude Code + Codex (SSR too) and nothing on beta; unread chip from a thread finished while the panel was closed; '+' menu -> draft -> Enter sends: transcript shows prompt, 'echo: ...', turn_end; URL gains ?thread=; title = first prompt; shown thread is read again after its turn (daemon unread false); 'slow:9000' then reload: panel reopens from ?thread=, replay shows all rows incl. part one, Working shown, part two + turn_end arrive, seqs 1..7 unique/ordered; cancel via the stop button -> turn_end (cancelled); deep link on /p/alpha/setup/plugins opens the thread and keeps the page; back/select/Escape sync ?thread=; Codex entry opens its (empty) list; client switch to beta hides rail+panel; 390px: no horizontal overflow, panel full-width; zero console errors. Root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (103 files, 988 passed, 3 skipped), build all pass.

OPEN: no DELETE thread route (lists only grow); codex not prompted live (needs a logged-in codex-acp); Nuxt UI's UChatPromptSubmit types status via 'ai', which the web app does not depend on (resolves to any; harmless); the registration mechanism is a plugin-called function like core's registerPluginPanel rather than app.config, although layers/README.md still says app.config for chat contributions (README not edited: outside this bead's file scope).
close_reason: chat layer: rail, panel, threads, prompt bar, SSE replay/reconnect, deep link; browser-verified

title: Add the chat capabilities, chat agents in the registry and thread endpoints
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Chatting with Claude Code and Codex are capabilities in the Agent Hub, each requiring its plugin. Register `chat-claude-code` and `chat-codex` capabilities (module `agent-hub`, required plugin `claude-code` and `codex` respectively, no views, ladder none then chat with the chat flag on) each contributing one chat agent with an id, label, avatar and family. Extend the registry so a chat agent is listed for a project only when its capability is ready and the actor's rung allows chat. Add threads: a thread belongs to an actor, a project and an agent, wraps one session at a time (a new session when model or effort changes), has a title (first prompt, truncated) and tracks unread and working state server-side. REST: list threads for the project (with unread and working flags), create, get with its current session, mark read, send prompt (delegates to the session), and the agent's supported model and effort options where the family exposes them. Run every route through the rung gate. Working directory for these threads is the project's checkout path.

Shared names: Capability ids are fixed: `overview`, `issues`, `chat-claude-code`, `chat-codex`, `bots`, `team`, `uptime`, `deployments`, `platform-agent`. Module ids are fixed: `issues`, `agent-hub`, `operations`. Plugin type ids are fixed: `repository`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `netlify`, `heroku`, `slack`.
acceptance_criteria: With only the Claude Code plugin healthy the registry lists one agent; enabling Codex adds the second; creating a thread and sending a prompt produces a session whose working directory is the project path; unread and working flags change as expected; an actor below the chat rung is refused.
notes:
Chat capabilities + chat threads decisions (4.10 chat layer, 4.12 model/effort selector, 5.1/5.2 seeded threads, 6.14 bots in rail, 10.7 platform agent build on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md '## Chat threads'.

MANIFESTS (src/capabilities/manifests/chat-claude-code.ts, chat-codex.ts; appended to CAPABILITIES after bots, team; AGENT_HUB_MODULE gains {chat-claude-code, defaultRung 'chat'}, {chat-codex, 'chat'}): no views/jobs/tools; ladder none -> chat (chat: true). chat-claude-code requiresPlugins ['claude-code'], agent { id 'claude-code', label 'Claude Code', family 'claude-code', avatar 'i-lucide-sparkles' }. chat-codex requiresPlugins ['codex'], agent { id 'codex', label 'Codex', family 'codex', avatar 'i-lucide-square-terminal' }.
SHARED: AgentManifest gained optional family?: AgentSessionFamily and avatar?: string (Iconify name); RegistryAgent gained the same optional fields (registry/compute.ts copies them when present). Registry already listed agents only when rung.chat && ready; verified.

TABLES (src/db/schema/chat-threads.ts; MIGRATION drizzle/0010_chat_threads.sql, tag 0010_chat_threads, after 0009_agent_sessions):
- chat_threads: id PK, project_id FK projects CASCADE, actor_id (no FK, like agent_sessions), agent_id (registry agent id), current_session_id FK agent_sessions CASCADE, title null, model null, effort null (null = agent default), unread bool, working bool, last_read_at null, last_activity_at, created_at, updated_at. Indexes (project_id, actor_id, last_activity_at), (current_session_id).
- chat_thread_sessions: thread_id FK CASCADE, session_id FK agent_sessions CASCADE, model, effort, created_at; PK (thread_id, session_id). Every session the thread wrapped, oldest first (4.12 divider data).

SERVICE (src/threads, import from '../threads'): threadServiceFor(db, sessions) -> ThreadService (one per SessionManager via WeakMap, so building the app repeatedly never doubles subscriptions); createThreadService; chatAgents(capabilities) / findChatAgent(capabilities, id) -> { id, label, capabilityId, family } (agents with a family); threadTitle(text); familyOptions/assertModelEffort/chatPosture (options.ts). Sessions are created with sessions.create({ projectId, family, actorId, cwd: sourcePath(project.source), posture: chatPosture(...) }). Mounted in app.ts next to sessionRoutes when deps.sessions is set.

UNREAD/WORKING: the service subscribes to every thread's current session (on boot for all threads, on create/model change for the new one). On each status message it reconciles in a microtask (the manager passes through 'live' synchronously between starting and prompting): working = session.status in {queued, starting, prompting}; a working -> not-working change sets unread=true and bumps last_activity_at. So it also tracks prompts sent through /sessions routes, crashes, start failures and queued cancels. POST read clears unread and sets last_read_at. Prompt and cancel through the thread mark it read for the sender (including when the prompt fails, e.g. auth_required). On boot working is recomputed from the (reset-to-idle) session status without setting unread.

ROUTES (src/threads/routes.ts; shared paths in packages/shared/src/threads.ts: projectThreadsPath(slug, agentId?), projectThreadPath, threadReadPath, threadPromptPath, threadCancelPath, chatAgentOptionsPath(slug, agentId)). Every route except the unfiltered list runs requireCapability({ capability: <agent's capability>, chat: true }) via a per-request middleware resolving the agent; another actor's or another project's thread -> 404 not_found.
- GET /projects/:slug/threads?agent=<id> -> { threads: ChatThread[] } most recently active first (gated on that agent). Without ?agent: threads of every agent the actor may chat with; refused with the first chat capability's refusal ONLY when none is allowed (so 4.10 should call it only when registry.agents is non-empty, or per agent).
- POST /projects/:slug/threads { agentId, title?, model?: string|null, effort?: string|null } -> 201 ChatThreadResponse { thread, session, sessions }. No prompt in create: 5.1/5.2 seeded threads = POST threads { agentId: 'claude-code'|'codex', title?: issue title } then POST threads/:id/prompt { text: seeded prompt }, then deep-link the thread id.
- GET /projects/:slug/threads/:id -> { thread, session (current AgentSession), sessions: ChatThreadSession[] }
- PATCH /projects/:slug/threads/:id { title?, model?, effort? } -> same shape; model/effort change creates a NEW session (new current_session_id + chat_thread_sessions row); refused thread_busy 409 while working; title-only patch keeps the session.
- POST .../:id/read -> { thread }; POST .../:id/prompt { text } -> 202 { thread, session } (delegates to sessions.prompt; title set from the first prompt, whitespace collapsed, truncated to CHAT_THREAD_TITLE_MAX_LENGTH 80 with an ellipsis, unless given); POST .../:id/cancel -> { thread, session }.
- GET /projects/:slug/threads/agents/:agentId/options -> { options: ChatAgentOptions { agentId, family, models: ChatOption[] {value,label,description?}, efforts: ChatOption[] } }.
- Streaming: 4.10 uses the existing session SSE route sessionEventsPath(slug, thread.currentSessionId, after) (not chat-gated; any authenticated actor, as 4.6 built it). Pending decisions: whatever 4.7 exposes, keyed by the session id.
- Errors (ApiErrorBody): THREAD_ERROR_CODES invalid_request 400, not_found 404, unsupported_agent 422 (agent without a family), thread_busy 409; plus session codes (session_busy, auth_required, family_unavailable, agent_failed) and gate codes (not_enabled 404, not_granted 403, not_ready 409, capability_unknown 404).

MODEL/EFFORT CONTRACT (for 4.12):
- claude-code: models = CLI aliases opus/sonnet/haiku (resolve to the latest of each tier; a full 'claude-*' id is also accepted), sent as posture flags ['--model', m]; efforts low/medium/high sent as ['--settings', '{"effortLevel":"<e>"}'] (the CLI has no effort flag; it reads settings.effortLevel or CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL; verified in the CLI source). Null = no flag = agent default. If chat ever adopts 6.7's posture (which requires exactly one --settings), merge effortLevel into that settings object.
- codex: options endpoint returns empty lists; create/patch with a model or effort -> 400. codex-acp 2.3.0 exposes models through ACP configOptions on session/new/load (config id 'model', category 'model'; 'reasoning_effort', category 'thought_level'; values are model ids, setter session/set_config_option or the legacy unstable_setSessionModel with 'model[effort]' ids). To support it, 4.12 must (a) capture configOptions from the newSession/loadSession response in the harness (acp/session.ts drops it today) and expose them (e.g. cache per project after the first session), and (b) apply the choice after start via setSessionConfigOption for 'model'/'reasoning_effort' only (never 'mode', per 4.3), or pass CODEX_CONFIG {model, model_reasoning_effort} through the launcher (families.ts). Then extend FAMILY_OPTIONS/chatPosture in src/threads/options.ts.

TESTS: src/threads/threads.test.ts (11) via startPlatform + fakeBins, healthy plugin instances written directly into plugin_instances.health: registry lists claude-code only, then both; developer with chat-claude-code none sees only codex; codex thread prompt -> session cwd = sourcePath(project) and live harness cwd = project path, working true mid-turn ('hang'), session_busy, cancel via manager -> working false + unread true, read clears, next turn unread again; cancel through the thread stays read; Claude with fake claude: options lists, create opus/high -> posture flags and launched argv contain --model opus --settings {"effortLevel":"high"}, title patch keeps session, model patch -> new session + sessions history, bad model 400; codex options empty + model refused, thread_busy mid-turn; validation/404s/per-actor lists; actor below chat rung -> 403 not_granted on list, filtered list, create, options, get/patch/read/prompt/cancel of own thread; not_ready after plugin turns unhealthy; restart clears working and resumes. src/registry/agent-hub.test.ts scoped to bots/team (filters capabilities/degraded) since the chat capabilities now share the module.
VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (93 files, 882 passed, 3 skipped), build all pass (first typecheck runs hit transient apps/web .nuxt missing and a src/decisions test type error from 4.7's in-flight work; both gone on rerun). Live: built daemon on 127.0.0.1:6619, throwaway CM_DATA_DIR + random CM_SECRETS_KEY, trusted-header auth (x-user): project + agent-hub; registry agents [] -> claude-code after sqlite health=healthy -> both after codex; unfiltered list with none ready 409 not_ready; options claude (3 models, 3 efforts) / codex (empty); create claude thread opus/high, prompt 'launch-env' (claudePath = fake claude fixture wrapper) 202 working:true title 'launch-env' cwd = project path; after the turn list shows working false unread true; session SSE replay prompt/text/turn_end; argv in the log had --model opus --settings {"effortLevel":"high"}; read -> unread false; PATCH model sonnet -> new session, 2 sessions; codex model 400; user 'dev' (role developer, chat-claude-code none): registry agents ['codex'], create claude 403 not_granted, options 403, admin's thread 404, codex thread 201, list only codex; SIGTERM exit 0, no agent processes left.
OPEN: session SSE/prompt routes (4.6) are not chat-gated; anyone authenticated who knows a session id can stream it. Consider a gated alias /threads/:id/events if that matters.
close_reason: chat-* manifests, chat_threads + sessions history, thread REST gated by chat rung; verified live

title: Add the login panels for the Claude Code and Codex plugin instances
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

The Plugins page can host a type-specific panel on an instance; the two agent plugins need one for their login flows. For Claude Code: a Start login button that shows the returned URL to open, a field to paste the code, the resulting status, an alternative "paste a setup token" form, and Revoke. For Codex: Start login showing the URL and the one-time code, a Check status button, and Revoke. Show the health result from the plugin instance and refresh it after each step.
acceptance_criteria: Completing both logins from the UI results in both instances showing healthy; revoke returns them to not configured; a wrong Claude code shows the failure.
notes:
Login panels for claude-code and codex (core, apps/web/app).

FILES: components/plugins/panels/ClaudeCodePanel.vue, components/plugins/panels/CodexPanel.vue; registered in plugins/plugin-panels.ts next to repository: registerPluginPanel('claude-code'|'codex', defineAsyncComponent(() => import('~/components/plugins/panels/<X>Panel.vue'))). Props { instance, type } inline; health itself is shown by the card's PluginsHealth above the panel, the panels only add step outcomes (UAlert) and refresh it via refreshPlugins().

CLAUDE CODE PANEL (data-testid claude-code-*): mode badge (Browser login / Long-lived token from config.authMode). Start login (label 'Log in again' when healthy; 'Switch to browser login' in token mode = PATCH config.authMode login then start-login) -> attempt box: URL as external link (target _blank, noopener) + copy, 'Expires in m:ss' countdown (attempt dropped with an 'expired, start again' note at 0), code input + Submit code -> submit-code; logged_in -> success alert, failed -> error alert with reason; both refreshPlugins() (daemon already stored health). 400 claude_code_invalid_code keeps the attempt; 404/409 attempt errors drop it.
