title: Add durable sessions with an event log, SSE replay, reaper and cap
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

v2 lost every transcript on reload or restart, which is why its harness chat felt unfinished. Add a session model in the daemon: a session belongs to a project, an agent family, an actor and a working directory, and records its upstream ACP session id so it can be resumed after a daemon restart. Every event the harness emits for a session is appended to a durable per-session event log in the platform database with a sequence number. Expose per-session REST: send a prompt (starting or resuming the live process on demand), cancel, and a server-sent event stream that first replays the log from a client-supplied sequence and then follows live. Reap idle live processes after a configurable timeout without deleting the session (it resumes on the next prompt), and enforce a configurable cap on concurrent live processes with a queue. Write a `session.started` activity event when a session is first created. Non-goals: decisions (separate work), threads and the UI.

Shared names: Activity event types are fixed strings: `session.started`, `run.started`, `bot.handoff`, `incident.opened`, `incident.closed`, `deploy.attempted`.
acceptance_criteria: Sending a prompt and reconnecting the stream mid-turn replays the earlier events and continues live; restarting the daemon and sending another prompt resumes the same upstream session; an idle session is reaped and resumes later; the cap queues an extra session; tests cover replay ordering and resume.
notes:
Durable session decisions (4.7 decisions, 4.9 threads, 6.13 bot sessions build on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md '## Durable agent sessions'.

TABLES (apps/daemon/src/db/schema/agent-sessions.ts; MIGRATION apps/daemon/drizzle/0009_agent_sessions.sql, tag 0009_agent_sessions, right after 0008_bots)
• agent_sessions: id uuid PK, project_id FK projects ON DELETE CASCADE, family 'claude-code'|'codex', actor_id text (no FK: actor ids are not guaranteed to be users rows in tests), cwd, upstream_session_id nullable (the agent's ACP session id, set when the first live process starts, passed back as upstreamSessionId to resume), status 'idle'|'queued'|'starting'|'live'|'prompting' (default idle; every non-idle row is reset to idle on boot), posture JSON nullable ({ flags?: string[] for Claude, codex?: { mode?: 'read-only'|'workspace-write', developerInstructions? } } reused on every resume), created_at, last_activity_at. Index (project_id, created_at).
• agent_session_events: session_id FK agent_sessions CASCADE, seq integer (1-based per session, assigned by the manager as max(seq)+1 in a transaction, so it keeps growing across resumes and restarts), kind, payload JSON (the event minus seq/at/kind, respond stripped), created_at (the harness event's 'at'). PRIMARY KEY (session_id, seq).

SESSION MANAGER (src/sessions/manager.ts; import from '../sessions'): createSessionManager(deps: PluginInstanceDeps & { paths, secretsReader, harness: AcpHarness }, { idleTimeoutMs?, maxLive?, reapIntervalMs?, now?, onDiagnostic? }) -> SessionManager. startPlatform creates platform.sessions (new PlatformOptions: sessions?: SessionManagerOptions, acp?: AcpHarnessOptions for the fake-agent bins seam); platform.close() and index.ts shutdown close it BEFORE the harness (await platform.sessions.close() then acpHarness.close(), so the 'exited' rows land while the DB is open). createApp({ sessions }) mounts sessionRoutes on /projects.
• create({ projectId, family, actorId, cwd, posture? }) -> AgentSession (sync; writes activity 'session.started' title '<Family> session started' payload { sessionId, family, actorId }). cwd must be absolute: REST uses sourcePath(project.source); 6.13 passes the worktree.
• list(projectId), get(id) -> AgentSession|null, events(id, { after? }) -> AgentSessionEvent[]
• prompt(id, text) -> Promise<AgentSession>: status must be idle or live else SessionError session_busy. Resolves the launch context first (claudeCodeLaunchContext / codexLaunchContext from src/plugins: plugin home as configHome, command, env; NO health probe and NO gate on stored health, the session's own auth error is the signal) -> SessionError family_unavailable 422 when the project has no instance (or Claude token mode without token). Logs { kind: 'prompt', text }. Live process present -> sends the turn. None: if lives+starting >= maxLive -> status queued + FIFO queue, returns at once (failures later surface only as log rows). Else awaits harness.startSession (session/new, or session/load with the stored upstream id), stores upstreamSessionId, subscribes AFTER the handshake (so history replayed on session/load is NOT re-logged), sets live, sends the turn and returns with status prompting (HTTP 202). Start failures: AcpAuthRequiredError -> log auth_required + turn_end cancelled, status idle, SessionError auth_required 409 'X is not logged in for this project; log in on its plugin page'; anything else -> log error { phase: 'start' } + turn_end cancelled, SessionError agent_failed 502.
• cancel(id): running turn -> acp.cancel() and waits for the turn; queued -> removed from the queue + turn_end cancelled row, status idle.
• subscribe(id, listener) -> unsubscribe; listener gets { type: 'event', event: AgentSessionEvent } | { type: 'status', status }.
• Status transitions: prompt -> prompting; turn_end row -> live (set in the event handler so it is visible as soon as turn_end is); exited row -> idle (process gone, row kept).
• REAPER: every reapIntervalMs (default min(30s, max(250ms, idleTimeout/10))) a live process with no running turn and lastActivity older than idleTimeoutMs is closed -> 'exited' row with expected: true, status idle, upstream id kept; next prompt resumes via session/load. Never reaps during a turn (pending decisions live inside a turn).
• CAP: maxLive counts live + starting processes across ALL projects. When the queue is non-empty and no slot is free, the least recently active idle live process is closed immediately to make room (so queued prompts do not wait for the idle timeout). Exit of any process drains the queue in FIFO order.
• ENV: CM_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT (default 15m; <n>s|m|h|d, at most 7d), CM_SESSION_MAX_LIVE (default 4, positive int). Parsed by resolveSessionSettings(env) in src/sessions/config.ts, wired into loadConfig().sessions.

PENDING-REQUEST HOOK FOR 4.7 (daemon-side only, no HTTP route here): platform.sessions.pendingRequests(id) -> [{ requestId, kind: 'permission_request'|'question' }] (only on a live process, only during a turn); respondToPermission(id, requestId, RequestPermissionResponse) and respondToQuestion(id, requestId, CreateElicitationResponse) -> boolean (false when unknown, already answered, voided by request_cancelled/turn end, or the process is gone; a kind mismatch is false too). The permission_request/question rows in the log carry requestId, toolCall/options or request (respond stripped); 4.7 should pick an option by option.kind, persist its decision, and treat request_cancelled rows as expiry. Unanswered requests fall back to cancelled at turn end (harness behaviour).

ROUTES (src/sessions/routes.ts, any authenticated actor, actor id recorded on create; shared paths projectSessionsPath(slug), projectSessionPath, sessionPromptPath, sessionCancelPath, sessionEventsPath(slug, id, after?)):
• POST /projects/:slug/sessions { family, posture? } -> 201 { session }; GET /projects/:slug/sessions -> { sessions } oldest first; GET /projects/:slug/sessions/:id -> { session } (404 not_found for another project's session)
• POST /projects/:slug/sessions/:id/prompt { text (non-empty, <= SESSION_PROMPT_MAX_LENGTH 200000) } -> 202 { session }
• POST /projects/:slug/sessions/:id/cancel -> 200 { session }
• GET /projects/:slug/sessions/:id/events?after=<seq> -> SSE. Contract: ': connected' first; every log row with seq > after as 'event: session' / 'id: <seq>' / 'data: AgentSessionEvent'; then 'event: status' data { status } (current); then live rows + status changes; ': ping' every SESSION_EVENTS_HEARTBEAT_MS 30000. The route subscribes before the replay query and drops duplicates by seq, so a row appended mid-replay is delivered exactly once in order. Reconnect with the last seq seen. Stream ends on daemon shutdown (manager signal). Errors as ApiErrorBody: invalid_request 400, not_found 404, session_busy 409, auth_required 409, family_unavailable 422, agent_failed 502 (SESSION_ERROR_CODES).

SHARED (packages/shared/src/sessions.ts): AGENT_SESSION_FAMILIES/AgentSessionFamily, AGENT_SESSION_FAMILY_NAMES, AGENT_SESSION_STATUSES/AgentSessionStatus, CODEX_SESSION_MODES, AgentSessionPosture, AgentSession, PERMISSION_OPTION_KINDS, SessionPermissionOption, AcpObject (Record<string, unknown>: ACP structures verbatim, shared has no SDK dep), AgentSessionEventPayload (harness kinds text/reasoning/tool_call/tool_result/usage/other/permission_request/question/request_cancelled/turn_end/error (phase adds 'start')/auth_required/exited + 'prompt' { text }), AgentSessionEvent = { seq, at } & payload, CreateSessionRequest, SessionPromptRequest, SessionResponse, SessionListResponse, SESSION_EVENT_NAME 'session', SESSION_STATUS_EVENT_NAME 'status', SessionStatusEvent, SESSION_ERROR_CODES.

FOR 4.9 (threads): a thread should reference agent_sessions.id (FK CASCADE); create the session with platform.sessions.create({ projectId, family, actorId: c.var.actor.id, cwd: sourcePath(project.source), posture }) and reuse the prompt/cancel/events routes (or call sessions.prompt/cancel/subscribe/events directly). 'Changing model/effort starts a fresh session' = create a new session row; posture is fixed per session. FOR 6.13 (bot sessions): sessions.create with cwd = the worktree and posture = 6.7's never-bypass posture ({ flags } for Claude, { codex: { mode, developerInstructions: persona } } for Codex), then sessions.prompt(id, instructions) and sessions.subscribe for decisions/handoff; auth problems show up as the auth_required SessionError/log row.

TESTS: src/sessions/sessions.test.ts (13) through startPlatform on a temp data dir with acp: { bins: fakeBins } (fake ACP agent as the Codex adapter) and a real codex plugin instance: create + activity + list/get/404 + validation; family_unavailable without plugin; turn + seq + session_busy + cancel; SSE replay mid-turn then live follow (seq 1..6 in order, after= tail); restart startPlatform on the same dir -> same upstream id, log kept incl. exited row, session/load ('(loaded)' history); reaper (200ms) keeps row and resumes; no reap mid-turn; cap maxLive 1 queues and runs after the idle process is reaped; cancel of a queued prompt; auth_required (env FAKE_ACP_AUTH=none wrapper) -> 409 + rows; pending request hook (permission answered by option id); close ends streams and kills processes; settings parsing. VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (755: 752 passed, 3 skipped), build pass. Live: platform+app via tsx on 127.0.0.1:6317 with a throwaway CM_DATA_DIR, CM_SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT=5s, CM_SESSION_MAX_LIVE=1 and the fake agent: curl flow confirmed 201 create + session.started activity, 422 before the plugin instance, 202 prompt, mid-turn stream replay (prompt, text, status prompting), 409 busy, cancel -> turn_end cancelled live, second session queued then served after the idle process was reaped (exited expected:true), 5s reaper, SIGTERM wrote the exited row, restart -> status idle + same upstream id, prompt after restart -> session/load, ': ping' at 30s, clean stop with no fake agents left.
OPEN: src/config.test.ts expectation updated for the new config.sessions field. Deviation from 4.5's note: the launcher does not gate on stored Codex health (stale until POST /test), the session's auth_required is the signal, as 4.4 recommends.
close_reason: agent_sessions + event log, SSE replay, reaper, cap, resume after restart; verified live

title: Model permission requests and agent questions as pending decisions
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Agents ask for permission and sometimes ask questions; the human must answer, and never by accident. Add a pending-decision model on top of sessions: each harness permission request or elicitation becomes a decision record (session, kind, the options the agent offered with their kinds, a timeout) that is logged as an event, and an endpoint answers it. Rules learned from v2 and Clanker: a decision is answered by option kind (allow once, always allow, deny, or a typed answer), never by position; "always allow" may only accept rules the agent itself proposed; an answer for an unknown or already-answered decision is rejected; an unanswered decision times out to refusal after a configurable period; anything unexpected is refused. Design the model so another surface (Slack, later) can answer the same decision, and the first answer wins. Add a never-bypass rule: no configuration path may launch either agent in a bypass-permissions mode; refuse such settings by name.
acceptance_criteria: A permission request appears as a pending decision on the stream; answering deny stops the tool; answering allow continues it; a second answer is rejected; a timed-out decision is refused; a launch configuration containing a bypass mode is refused; tests cover each.
notes:
Pending decisions (4.11 decision cards, 7.4 Slack answers, 6.13 bot sessions build on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md '## Pending decisions' and the never-bypass paragraph in '## Agent sessions (ACP harness)'.

CODE: apps/daemon/src/decisions/ (index.ts exports): config.ts (CM_DECISION_TIMEOUT), errors.ts (DecisionError), model.ts (option mapping, form validation, ACP responses), service.ts (createDecisionService), store.ts (fold from the log, lookup by id via json_extract; NO new table, NO migration), routes.ts (decisionRoutes). Shared wire types: packages/shared/src/decisions.ts (exported from index). AgentSessionEventPayload in shared sessions.ts now includes DecisionEventPayload.

MODEL (shared Decision): id (uuid), sessionId, requestId (harness request), kind 'permission'|'question', toolCall (permission, ACP ToolCallUpdate) | null, request (question, ACP form elicitation incl. requestedSchema/_meta) | null, options: DecisionOption[] { kind 'allow_once'|'allow_always'|'deny'|'answer', optionId (agent's id; null for a synthetic deny and for question options), label (agent's option name; for allow_always it describes the proposed rule), meta (the option's ACP _meta verbatim = agent-proposed rule payload, or null) }, createdAt, expiresAt, state 'pending'|'answered'|'expired', answer: { optionKind, optionId, answer (question content|null), explanation|null, surface 'web'|'slack', actorId, at } | null, expiry: { reason 'timeout'|'cancelled'|'exited'|'refused', message, at } | null.
Option mapping: ACP allow_once->allow_once, allow_always->allow_always, reject_once->deny; reject_always dropped; options whose id/name match /auto[\s_-]*review/i dropped (Codex 'strict auto review'); if no reject_once, a deny with optionId null is added (sent as outcome cancelled). Malformed/duplicate option ids, or a question that is not a form of string/number/integer/boolean/choice-array fields -> refused at once (decision_opened then decision_expired reason 'refused', agent gets cancelled/cancel). Question options: answer (optionId null), deny (= decline).

EVENT LOG ROWS (session log, same table, appear on the SSE stream as 'event: session' right after the permission_request/question row, seq-ordered):
- decision_opened { decision: Decision (state pending) }
- decision_answered { decisionId, answer: DecisionAnswerRecord }
- decision_expired { decisionId, expiry: { reason, message, at } }
Fold them (foldDecisions) to rebuild state; GET does this. A pending decision in the log with no live entry (daemon crashed) is reported expired/exited.

SERVICE: platform.decisions = createDecisionService({ db, sessions }, { timeoutMs?, now? }) (PlatformOptions.decisions; loadConfig().decisions wired in index.ts; createApp({ decisions }) mounts routes when sessions+decisions are given). API: list(sessionId) -> Decision[] oldest first; get(decisionId) -> Decision|null (memory, else log lookup); answer(decisionId, { optionKind, optionId?, answer?, explanation?, surface, actorId }) -> Decision (sync) or throws DecisionError; close().
ANSWER CONTRACT: by kind never position. optionId required only when the decision has >1 option of that kind (Codex: two denies, several allow_always; Claude shim: one allow_always per CLI suggestion) and must belong to that kind. allow_always only exists when the agent proposed it -> else option_not_offered. answer only for kind answer (validated vs requestedSchema: known fields only, required present & non-empty, number/integer/boolean types, choices enforced unless listed in _meta['clanker-corner'].freeText). explanation only with a permission deny (<=2000 chars), sent as _meta[DECISION_META_KEY].explanation. First answer wins (state flips synchronously); later -> already_answered. now() >= expiresAt -> agent refused + decision_expired(timeout) + error decision_expired. If the harness says the request is gone -> expired(cancelled). The decision is marked answered and logged only after respond() succeeded.
Refusals sent to the agent: permission { outcome: 'cancelled' }, question { action: 'cancel' }; human deny of a permission = selected reject_once option (or cancelled for the synthetic deny); question deny = { action: 'decline' }.
Expiry triggers: timer (CM_DECISION_TIMEOUT, default 5m, s|m|h|d, max 1d; unref'd), request_cancelled row (turn ended/cancelled) -> 'cancelled', exited row -> 'exited' and the session's entries are dropped from memory.
7.4 (Slack): call platform.decisions.answer(id, { optionKind, optionId?, answer?, explanation?, surface: 'slack', actorId: <slack user/actor id> }); render buttons per option (kind + optionId), not by index; subscribe via platform.sessions.observe((sessionId, message) => ...) for decision_opened/answered/expired rows to post/update messages. 4.11: render cards from decision_* rows on the stream (or GET list); POST the answer; show answer.surface/actorId and expiry.reason.

ROUTES (any authenticated actor; surface 'web'; actorId = c.var.actor.id): GET /projects/:slug/sessions/:id/decisions -> { decisions }; POST /projects/:slug/sessions/:id/decisions/:decisionId { optionKind, optionId?, answer?, explanation? } -> { decision }; unknown body fields refused. Shared paths: sessionDecisionsPath(slug, id), sessionDecisionPath(slug, id, decisionId). Errors (DECISION_ERROR_CODES): invalid_request 400, not_found 404 (session of another project, or decision not in this session), already_answered 409, decision_expired 409, option_not_offered 422, invalid_answer 422.

SESSION MANAGER CHANGES (src/sessions/manager.ts): observe(observer: (sessionId, message) => void) -> unsubscribe (global, called after the session's own listeners); record(id, payload) -> AgentSessionEvent|undefined (append + publish a daemon-written row); publish is now queued so rows appended from inside a listener are delivered to everyone in seq order; create() refuses a claude-code posture failing the never-bypass rule -> SessionError invalid_request (POST /sessions 400).
HARNESS CHANGE (src/acp/session.ts): cancel() now settles every pending request with its fallback (cancelled) after sending session/cancel, as ACP requires; before, a turn waiting on a permission hung on cancel with agents that do not abort it themselves (the fake agent). request_cancelled rows follow.

NEVER-BYPASS (src/acp/families.ts, exported from ./acp): assertClaudeNeverBypass(flags) runs in resolveFamilyLaunch for claude-code (so in every startSession, before configHome/spawn) and in sessions.create. Throws AcpBypassRefusedError extends AcpLaunchError { code: 'bypass_refused', setting } for: --dangerously-skip-permissions, --allow-dangerously-skip-permissions (CLAUDE_BYPASS_FLAGS); --permission-mode (space or = form) bypassPermissions or auto (CLAUDE_BYPASS_MODES) or anything outside CLAUDE_LAUNCH_PERMISSION_MODES (default plan acceptEdits manual dontAsk); --permission-prompt-tool; --allowedTools/--allowed-tools rules (variadic values, split on commas/spaces outside parens) that are '*', a tool-name wildcard other than mcp__<server>__*, bare Bash/PowerShell or Bash(*)/Bash(:*); --settings/--agents JSON (inline, or an absolute file that is read; relative/unreadable/invalid -> refused) with any defaultMode/permissionMode that is a bypass or unknown mode, or permissions.allow with such a rule; the tokens 'bypassPermissions' / 'dangerously-skip-permissions' anywhere in other flag values (--append-system-prompt/--system-prompt text excepted). 6.7's posture output passes (posture.test.ts still green). Codex stays covered by 4.3 (flags refused, modes allowlisted).

TEST SUPPORT: fake agent prompts 'guarded-tool' (tool_call + permission allow_once 'once'/reject_once 'no'; tool_call_update completed on allow, failed otherwise; text ran:<id> | skipped:<outcome json>) and 'guarded-rules' (adds allow_always rule-0/rule-1 with _meta.rule and an auto-review allow_once 'review').
TESTS: src/decisions/decisions.test.ts (12): stream order + pending decision, deny stops the tool (failed) with surface/actor logged, allow continues (completed) + second answer rejected (web and slack), first surface wins, real-timer timeout (300ms) refuses, injected-clock deadline refuses, kind/optionId/allow_always rules + auto-review dropped, question validation + decline, cancelled turn expires + 404, restart rebuilds from log, bypass posture refused at POST /sessions, CM_DECISION_TIMEOUT parsing. src/acp/never-bypass.test.ts (21): each refused config by name, settings file read, 6.7-like posture accepted, harness refuses before spawning.
VERIFIED 2026-10-28: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (93 files, 882 passed, 3 skipped), build pass; built daemon boots with CM_DECISION_TIMEOUT=45s, refuses 2d, exits cleanly on SIGTERM; claude-acp tree-shaken to the DECISION_META_KEY constant in the bundle.
OPEN: config.test.ts expectation updated for config.decisions. No live Claude/Codex run (no logins).
close_reason: Pending decisions in session log, answer by kind, first-answer-wins, timeout, never-bypass; 882 tests green

title: Add the Claude Code plugin type with a per-project login flow
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Different projects may use different Claude accounts, and no token may be stored by the platform beyond what the CLI itself writes. Add the `claude-code` plugin type (project scope, one per project). The instance owns a private config directory under the daemon's data directory (restrictive permissions) that is passed to the CLI as its config directory. Configuring means logging in: an endpoint starts the CLI's browser login in that directory, captures the login URL from its output and returns it; a second endpoint accepts the pasted code and writes it to the waiting process's stdin without storing it; the health check runs the CLI's own status command in that directory and reports logged in or not. Login attempts expire after ten minutes. As an alternative, accept a long-lived token obtained from the CLI's setup-token command, stored in the secrets store and injected as the CLI's token variable at launch. Revoking deletes the config directory and any stored token. Hard requirement learned in Clanker: never run the status command immediately before starting a session, because it can hold the CLI's OAuth refresh lock; health is checked on demand and cached, and session start treats an auth-required error as the signal instead.

Shared names: Plugin type ids are fixed: `repository`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `netlify`, `heroku`, `slack`.
acceptance_criteria: Start-login returns a URL; pasting the code completes the login and the health check reports logged in; a wrong code reports failure; the setup-token path reports healthy; revoke deletes the directory; the config directory is unique per project; tests cover the flow with a fake CLI.
notes:
Claude Code plugin decisions (4.2/4.3/4.8/6.13 depend on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md '### Claude Code'.
TYPE (src/plugins/types/claude-code.ts, claudeCodePluginType; registered in types/index.ts before codex): id 'claude-code', project scope, singleInstance. Config: authMode select 'login' (default) | 'token'; claudePath optional absolute path of the claude executable (blank = 'claude' on PATH). Secret: oauthToken (optional; the 'claude setup-token' value, used only in token mode). claudeCodeConfig(config) narrows a stored config like repositoryConfig.
CONFIG DIR: <data dir>/agent-homes/claude-code/<instance id>, 0700, refused if a symlink; claudeConfigDir(paths, instanceId) / ensureConfigDir / removeConfigDir / configDirExists in src/plugins/claude-code/cli.ts. Passed to the CLI as CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. The platform stores nothing in it; the CLI writes its own credential there. Unique per project because the instance is one per project.
CLI ENV (claudeCliEnv): allowlist PATH HOME LANG LC_ALL LC_CTYPE TERM TZ USER LOGNAME SHELL TMPDIR + NO_COLOR=1 FORCE_COLOR=0 + CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (+ CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN in token mode). Nothing else (API keys, gateways) reaches the CLI. Local to this module rather than importing 4.2's curateAgentEnv so the two beads stay decoupled; fold together later if wanted.
ACTIONS (POST /plugins/:id/<name>, admin only; names in CLAUDE_CODE_ACTIONS from @candy-mountain/shared claude-code.ts, wire types there too):
• start-login -> ClaudeCodeStartLoginResponse { attemptId, url, expiresAt }. Spawns 'claude auth login --claudeai' (detached, own process group) in the config dir, parses the first http(s) URL from stdout/stderr after ANSI/OSC-8 stripping, preferring the one with code=true. Open attempt for the instance -> returns it again (idempotent on reload). 409 claude_code_login_failed in token mode; 502 claude_code_login_failed with a fixed sentence (never CLI output) when no link within 30 s or the CLI exits first.
• submit-code { attemptId, code } -> ClaudeCodeSubmitCodeResponse { attemptId, status: 'logged_in' } | { attemptId, status: 'failed', reason } (both 200). Code must be '<code>#<state>' (no whitespace/control chars, <= 512) else 400 claude_code_invalid_code and the attempt stays open. Written to stdin once, never stored or logged; waits for exit (60 s exchange bound); exit 0 then confirmed with 'claude auth status --json' -> logged_in; non-zero -> failed 'Claude did not accept the code.' 404 claude_code_attempt_not_found for an unknown id or another instance's; 409 claude_code_attempt_not_waiting once the attempt ended/expired/already took a code (message says which).
• revoke -> ClaudeCodeRevokeResponse { directoryRemoved, tokenCleared }: cancels any open attempt (SIGTERM, SIGKILL after 2 s), rm -rf config dir, clears oauthToken via the new secretsWriter (which resets stored health). Idempotent.
ATTEMPT REGISTRY (src/plugins/claude-code/login-attempts.ts): LoginAttemptRegistry class + module singleton claudeLoginAttempts used by the actions; attempts in memory only, expire CLAUDE_CODE_LOGIN_ATTEMPT_TTL_MS (10 min, shared) after start: the process is ended and the attempt forgotten. Platform.close() calls claudeLoginAttempts.close() (SIGKILLs open ones, registry stays usable). Options for tests: ttlMs, promptTimeoutMs, exchangeTimeoutMs, killGraceMs, statusTimeoutMs, env.
HEALTH: 'claude auth status --json' in the config dir (10 s bound, 64 KB output cap); loggedIn true -> healthy, detail 'Logged in as <email> (<plan>) via <method>.' (whitelisted, pattern-checked fields only); loggedIn false -> 'Not logged in; start the browser login.' / token mode 'Claude does not accept the stored token...'. Login mode with no config dir -> unhealthy without running the CLI. Token mode: needs oauthToken set (else unhealthy), injects CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. CACHING RULE: health runs ONLY on demand (POST /plugins/:id/test) and the stored instance.health is the cache; nothing runs status automatically and a session launcher must NEVER run it (refresh-lock quirk) - read instance.health for the UI and treat the session's auth-required error as the signal.
LAUNCHER API (4.2/4.3/6.13): claudeCodeLaunchContext(deps: PluginInstanceDeps & { secretsReader, paths }, projectId) from src/plugins/claude-code (plugins index re-exports) -> null when the project has no instance, else { instance, config, configDir (ensured 0700), command (claudePath or undefined = PATH), env ({ CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN } in token mode, {} otherwise) }. Throws ClaudeCodeLaunchError in token mode with no token stored. Feed configDir to resolveFamilyLaunch('claude-code', { configHome: configDir, command }) and env to curateAgentEnv({ extra: env }). Never calls the CLI.
CONTRACT CHANGES (shared with 4.5): PluginHealthContext gains optional instance: PluginHealthInstance ({ id, scope, projectId }) and paths: DataPaths; checkPluginHealth options accept both; testPluginInstance deps accept paths? and pass them (c.var and Platform have paths; instanceHarness.app() now uses dataPaths(root) instead of { root }). PluginActionContext gains secretsWriter: PluginSecretsWriter<S> { set(name, value), clear(name) } built in instances/routes.ts over updatePluginInstance (validates like a PATCH, resets health).
PANEL (4.8) should: show instance.health; 'Log in' -> POST start-login, open url, input for the code -> POST submit-code, then POST /plugins/:id/test to store the fresh health (actions do not write health); 'Revoke' -> POST revoke then /test (or rely on tokenCleared resetting it); token path = PATCH { config: { authMode: 'token' }, secrets: { oauthToken } } then /test. Treat 409 claude_code_attempt_not_waiting / 404 attempt_not_found as 'start again'.
TESTS: src/plugins/claude-code/claude-code.test.ts (15) with the fake CLI src/plugins/claude-code/test-support/fake-claude.mjs (auth login prints an OSC-8 link, accepts FAKE_CLAUDE_CODE 'good#state', writes fake-login.json marker; auth status --json reads marker or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN ('bad-token' -> loggedIn false); FAKE_CLAUDE_MODE no-url|exit-early|hang|garbage; writes fake-env.json with pid + auth env names). Tests put a sh wrapper named claude on PATH that execs the fake with baked-in env.
VERIFIED AGAINST claude 2.1.311 --help only: 'claude auth login [--claudeai|--console|--email|--sso]', 'claude auth status [--json (default)|--text]', 'claude setup-token', 'claude auth logout'. The status JSON shape (loggedIn, authMethod, email, subscriptionType) and the login output format come from Clanker's runner against 2.1.281, not re-probed here (no login performed).
OPEN: the real CLI tries to open a browser on the daemon host when login starts (harmless headless; BROWSER not overridden). Health detail wording is derived from CLI fields and may need tweaking after a real login. No GET status action: start-login returns the open attempt instead.
close_reason: claude-code type with login/submit-code/revoke actions, token path, 15 fake-CLI tests; gates green

title: Add the Codex plugin type with the device login flow
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Codex uses a device-code login and must likewise be per project with no platform-stored token. Add the `codex` plugin type (project scope, one per project) owning a private Codex home under the daemon's data directory. Configuring means running the CLI's device-auth login in that home: an endpoint starts it and returns the verification URL and one-time code parsed from its output; the health check runs the CLI's login status command and reports logged in or not; attempts expire after ten minutes. Revoking deletes the home. Non-goals: API-key login.

Shared names: Plugin type ids are fixed: `repository`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `netlify`, `heroku`, `slack`.
acceptance_criteria: Start-login returns the URL and code; after completing in a browser the health check reports logged in; revoke deletes the home; tests cover the flow with a fake CLI.
notes:
Codex plugin type decisions (4.2/4.3/6.13 launchers and 4.8 login panel depend on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md "### Codex".

TYPE: src/plugins/types/codex.ts. createCodexPluginType(attempts) + codexPluginType (uses the module registry codexLoginAttempts), appended to PLUGIN_TYPES. id 'codex', scopes ['project'], singleInstance true, NO secretFields. Config: codexPath (string, optional, pattern '/.+' = absolute path; blank -> 'codex' on the daemon PATH, same lookup as the codex-acp adapter's CODEX_PATH ?? 'codex'). codexConfig(unknown) narrows stored config.

HOME: codexHome(paths, instanceId) = <dataDir>/agent-homes/codex/<instance id>, created 0700 (and agent-homes/codex chmod 0700) by start-login only. Passed to every codex child as CODEX_HOME. Unique per instance and therefore per project. Never touches ~/.codex.

ENV: codexEnv(home) = curateAgentEnv() from src/acp/env.ts (allowlist PATH/HOME/LANG/...; OPENAI_*, CM_* etc never pass) + CODEX_HOME, NO_BROWSER=1, NO_COLOR=1. Children spawned detached (own process group) with cwd = home; killed by group.

ACTIONS (admin only, /plugins/:id/<name>; wire types in packages/shared/src/codex-login.ts: CODEX_LOGIN_ACTIONS {start:'start-login', status:'login-status', revoke:'revoke'}, CodexLoginAttempt {attemptId, status: 'starting'|'waiting'|'succeeded'|'failed'|'expired', verificationUrl|null, userCode|null (both only while waiting), startedAt, expiresAt, endedAt|null, failure|null}, CodexLoginStatusResponse {attempt|null}, CodexRevokeResponse {removed}):
- POST start-login (no body) -> CodexLoginAttempt (status 'waiting') once `codex login --device-auth` printed the URL and one-time code (parsed after ANSI strip: first URL; first non-blank non-URL line after the 'one-time code' line). An already open attempt for the instance is returned unchanged. No code within 30 s, CLI exits first, or spawn fails -> 502 codex_login_failed with a fixed sentence (spawn errors include the OS message). Process keeps running: exit 0 -> confirm with `codex login status` -> 'succeeded' (else failed 'finished but does not report a login'); non-zero -> 'failed'; 10 min (CODEX_LOGIN_TTL_MS) -> 'expired' and the process group is SIGTERMed (SIGKILL after 2 s).
- GET login-status -> {attempt}: current or most recent attempt since daemon start, null if none (or after revoke / daemon restart).
- POST revoke -> {removed}: cancels any open attempt (waits for the process to exit), forgets it, rm -rf the home. removed=false when there was no home.

HEALTH: healthCheck uses 4.4's optional PluginHealthContext.instance/paths (unhealthy 'only for a saved plugin instance' without them); runs `codex login status` in the home (10 s cap, aborts on signal). Missing home -> 'not logged in' without spawning. 'Logged in using X' exit 0 -> healthy, detail 'Codex is logged in using ChatGPT.' (masked API key never read out); 'Not logged in' -> unhealthy 'Codex is not logged in for this project; start the device login.'; else unhealthy with reason. CACHING = the stored instance health: it only runs on demand via POST /plugins/:id/test (testPluginInstance); nothing probes before a session (refresh-lock quirk). Neither a successful login nor revoke updates the stored health (actions have no db access), so callers must POST /test afterwards.

LAUNCHERS (4.2/4.3/6.13): codexLaunchContext(platform, projectId) from src/plugins (codex/launch.ts) -> {instanceId, home, command: codexPath|undefined, health: stored PluginInstanceHealth|null} | null when the project has no codex instance. Feed into resolveFamilyLaunch('codex', { configHome: ctx.home, command: ctx.command }). Gate on ctx.health?.healthy; do not run login status first; on AcpAuthRequiredError tell the user to log in again.

LOGIN PANEL (4.8): POST /api/plugins (type 'codex', scope 'project', project slug) if missing; POST /api/plugins/:id/start-login -> show verificationUrl (link) + userCode (copyable) + countdown to expiresAt; poll GET /api/plugins/:id/login-status (~2 s) until status != 'waiting'; on 'succeeded' POST /api/plugins/:id/test and show health; on failed/expired show failure and offer retry. Revoke: POST /api/plugins/:id/revoke then POST /test. Optional codexPath via PATCH config.

REGISTRY: CodexLoginAttempts (codex/attempts.ts), module singleton codexLoginAttempts keyed by instance id, in memory only; Platform.close calls codexLoginAttempts.close() (ends open attempts, status failed 'The daemon stopped before the login finished.'). Options ttlMs/promptTimeoutMs/killGraceMs/statusTimeoutMs for tests.

TESTS: src/plugins/codex/codex.test.ts (12) with installFakeCodex(dir) from codex/fake-codex.ts: a sh script put first on PATH (or used as codexPath), steered through control files baked into the script (curated env blocks env vars): prints the real ANSI-coloured device prompt in two chunks, waits for complete-<instanceId>/fail-<instanceId>, records env + pid; `login status` reads $CODEX_HOME/auth.json. Covers: URL+code+attemptId+expiresAt (~10 min), home path + 0700, CODEX_HOME/NO_BROWSER set and OPENAI_API_KEY stripped, re-start returns open attempt; completion -> succeeded -> /test healthy; failure -> failed + unhealthy; revoke kills the process, deletes home, attempt null, /test unhealthy, second revoke removed=false; expiry (ttl 400 ms) kills the process and a new attempt starts; two projects get different homes and independent health + codexLaunchContext; missing CLI -> 502 codex_login_failed; codexPath override; close ends attempts; relative codexPath, second instance, global scope rejected; prompt and status parsers.
VERIFIED: root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (69 files, 611 passed, 3 skipped), build all pass. No Drizzle schema or migration.
OPEN: deleting the instance (DELETE /plugins/:id or project delete) leaves agent-homes/codex/<id> on disk (needs a per-type delete hook in instances.ts; same for claude-code). Revoke/login success leave stored health stale until POST /test (needs a health reset in PluginActionContext).
close_reason: codex type with device login actions, 12 fake-CLI tests; gates green

title: Build the ACP harness in the daemon on the ACP SDK
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Both predecessors wrapped ACP through Mastra and had to patch it; v3 uses the ACP SDK client directly. Build a harness in the daemon that, given an agent family (Claude Code or Codex), a working directory, a curated environment and a config home, spawns the agent process (the lifted Claude shim for Claude Code; the official Codex ACP adapter for Codex), performs the ACP initialise handshake, creates a new session or loads an existing one by upstream session id, sends prompts, cancels a turn, and emits every session update, permission request and elicitation as typed events on a stream the rest of the daemon consumes. The environment must be an allowlist: pass only what the CLIs need, never the daemon's own secrets or any API-key variables. Processes must be killed reliably when a session ends or the daemon stops. Non-goals: persistence, HTTP, the UI, posture flags (separate work) beyond passing through whatever flags the caller supplies.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test (skipped when the CLIs are absent) runs a prompt through each family and receives text events; loading a session by upstream id continues the conversation; cancel stops a running turn; the child environment contains no variable from a denylist; stopping the daemon leaves no orphan processes.
notes:
ACP harness decisions (4.3, 4.6, 4.7, 6.7 build on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md "Agent sessions (ACP harness)".

MODULE
• apps/daemon/src/acp/ -> import from './acp' (index.ts). Files: events.ts (types), env.ts (allowlist/denylist), families.ts (launch spec per family), process.ts (spawn + process-group kill), session.ts (ClientSideConnection session), harness.ts (registry), test-support/ (fake agent + helpers).
• Deps added to apps/daemon: @agentclientprotocol/sdk 1.4.0 (exact; ClientSideConnection is gone in 2.x), @candy-mountain/claude-acp workspace:*, @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp 2.3.0 (exact; the official adapter, formerly @zed-industries/codex-acp which stopped at 0.16.0; it bundles @openai/codex 0.164 ~165MB linux-x64 as an optional dep). The adapter speaks ACP wire v1, so SDK 1.4.0 on our side works (verified: initialize ok, session/new -> -32000 on a fresh CODEX_HOME).

HARNESS API
• createAcpHarness({ env?, bins?, startTimeoutMs?=60000, killTimeoutMs?=5000, onDiagnostic? }) -> AcpHarness { startSession(opts), list(), get(id), closed, close() }. env = base environment the allowlist is applied to (default process.env). bins = test seam { claudeShim?, codexAdapter? } each { command, args }.
• startSession({ family: 'claude-code'|'codex', cwd, configHome, env?, flags?, command?, upstreamSessionId?, onEvent?, turnTimeoutMs? }) -> Promise<AcpSession>. cwd and configHome must be absolute. configHome is mkdir'd 0700 (chmod 0700 if present, symlink refused -> AcpLaunchError). Completes initialize + session/new (or session/load when upstreamSessionId is given) before resolving. Rejects with AcpAuthRequiredError (code 'auth_required', ACP -32000) when the home has no login, AcpStartError (code 'start_failed', message includes the child's stderr tail) for anything else, AgentEnvError for a denied env name; in every failure the process is killed and nothing stays in the registry.
• AcpSession { id (daemon uuid), family, cwd, configHome, upstreamSessionId (the agent's ACP session id: pass it back as upstreamSessionId to resume; for Claude it is the --session-id/--resume uuid), pid, status: 'starting'|'idle'|'prompting'|'closed', exited: Promise<{code, signal}>, prompt(text | ContentBlock[]) -> Promise<{ stopReason, usage|null }> (one turn at a time, rejects on failure), cancel() (session/cancel; prompt then resolves stopReason 'cancelled'; no-op when idle), close() (kill; idempotent), subscribe(listener) -> unsubscribe, events() -> AsyncIterableIterator until the 'exited' event }.
• onEvent in startSession is attached BEFORE the handshake, so history an agent replays on session/load (user_message_chunk/agent_message_chunk) is delivered too; subscribe() only sees events from then on.

EVENT UNION (events.ts: AcpSessionEvent = { seq (1-based per session), at (ISO), sessionId } & payload). kinds:
• text { role: 'agent'|'user', text } (agent_message_chunk / user_message_chunk with text content)
• reasoning { text } (agent_thought_chunk)
• tool_call { toolCall: ToolCall } (ACP tool_call minus sessionUpdate)
• tool_result { update: ToolCallUpdate } (ACP tool_call_update: progress AND final status/content)
• usage { usage: UsageUpdate } (context usage_update: used, size, cost?)
• other { update: SessionUpdate } (plan, current_mode_update, available_commands_update, non-text chunks, ...; verbatim so nothing is dropped)
• permission_request { requestId (daemon uuid), toolCall: ToolCallUpdate, options: PermissionOption[], respond(RequestPermissionResponse) -> boolean }
• question { requestId, request: CreateElicitationRequest (form mode), respond(CreateElicitationResponse) -> boolean }
• request_cancelled { requestId } (pending request voided because its turn ended or the session closed; respond() returns false afterwards)
• turn_end { stopReason, usage|null }
• error { phase: 'prompt'|'cancel'|'connection', message, code|null }
• auth_required { message } (login expired mid-conversation; the prompt also rejects)
• exited { code, signal, expected } (expected=true when the daemon closed it)
Persistence note for 4.6: permission_request/question carry a respond function; persist everything else as-is and strip respond. 4.7: choose by option.kind (allow_once|allow_always|reject_once|reject_always), never by position; anything other than a selected allow is a denial on the Claude side; unanswered requests fall back to cancelled / cancel when the turn ends. Agent-initiated mid-turn cancellation of a pending request ($/cancel_request) is not surfaced separately: SDK 1.4.0's ClientSideConnection hands handlers params only, so the harness voids pending requests at turn boundaries instead (the SDK drops a late response anyway).

ENVIRONMENT (env.ts)
• Allowlist from the base env: PATH HOME LANG LC_ALL LC_CTYPE TERM TZ USER LOGNAME SHELL TMPDIR (empty values dropped). HOME is NOT overridden: Claude uses CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (set by the shim from --config-dir), Codex uses CODEX_HOME; both set from configHome.
• Family additions (not denylist-checked): codex -> CODEX_HOME, NO_BROWSER=1, CODEX_PATH (only when command given). claude-code -> none (the shim sets CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and strips NON_SUBSCRIPTION_AUTH_ENV itself).
• startSession env extras are merged last but any denied name throws AgentEnvError: AGENT_ENV_DENIED_NAMES (CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_SCOPES, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK/VERTEX/FOUNDRY, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN, NODE_OPTIONS, LD_PRELOAD, DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES) + prefixes ANTHROPIC_ OPENAI_ CM_ AWS_ AZURE_ GOOGLE_CLOUD_ VERTEX_ MASTRA_. CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is allowed as an extra (how a pasted setup-token reaches the CLI). Tests prove ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN, OPENAI_API_KEY, CM_SECRETS_KEY, CM_ADMIN_PASSWORD, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, NODE_OPTIONS, EDITOR never reach the child.

LAUNCH PER FAMILY (families.ts resolveFamilyLaunch)
• claude-code: process.execPath <claude-acp>/dist/cli.mjs --config-dir <configHome> [--claude <command>] [--turn-timeout-ms N] -- <flags...>. Bin found via createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve('@candy-mountain/claude-acp/package.json'); AcpLaunchError if dist is missing (root pnpm build required). Verified the built daemon bundle (tsdown) resolves it from apps/daemon/dist.
• codex: process.execPath <codex-acp>/dist/index.js <flags...>, env CODEX_HOME/NO_BROWSER/CODEX_PATH as above. The adapter resolves @openai/codex/bin/codex.js itself when CODEX_PATH is unset (its own dependency), so nothing else is needed on PATH. The adapter reads INITIAL_AGENT_MODE, CODEX_CONFIG (JSON), DEFAULT_AUTH_REQUEST, APP_SERVER_LOGS, MODEL_PROVIDER from env: 4.3 passes those through startSession env. Default adapter mode is NOT changed here (4.3's job).
• Process: spawn detached:true (own process group), stdio pipe, stderr -> onDiagnostic + 4KB tail. Kill = SIGTERM to -pid, SIGKILL to -pid after killTimeoutMs, plus a best-effort SIGKILL to the group after the direct child exits (reaps a CLI child the shim left). Verified: closing the harness kills the agent and a grandchild it spawned (no-orphans test) and a SIGTERM-ignoring agent is SIGKILLed.

POSTURE PASSTHROUGH FOR 6.7
• flags: string[] goes verbatim after '--' to claude (--permission-mode, --allowedTools, --disallowedTools, --settings, --append-system-prompt, --agent) and as argv to the Codex adapter. command: executable override (claude path / CODEX_PATH). env: Codex posture (INITIAL_AGENT_MODE=read-only, CODEX_CONFIG={...}). The harness vets none of it (never-bypass is 6.7's rule at the caller).

REGISTRY AND SHUTDOWN
• platform.acpHarness (startPlatform creates createAcpHarness()); platform.close() calls void acpHarness.close() before the watcher and DB. index.ts shutdown: issueWatcher.close(); const agentsStopped = acpHarness.close(); server.close(() => agentsStopped.then(closeMastra).finally(platform.close + exit)). A process is registered the moment it is spawned (status 'starting') so close() during a handshake still kills it; list()/get() hide 'starting' ones; a session leaves the registry when its process exits; startSession after close() rejects. Verified: built daemon boots with a throwaway CM_DATA_DIR and exits ~0.5s after SIGTERM.

TESTS (apps/daemon, vitest project 'daemon', src/acp/*.test.ts: 33 tests + 3 opt-in)
• test-support/fake-acp-agent.mjs: generic stdio ACP agent; prompts: default echo, think, tool, usage, permission, question, hang (until session/cancel), history, env (prints env names), spawn-child (prints grandchild pid), crash, expired (-32000), error; env FAKE_ACP_AUTH=none -> session/new auth_required, FAKE_ACP_START=crash. test-support/index.ts: fakeBins (claudeShim from packages/claude-acp/src/cli.ts via tsx, codexAdapter = fake agent), createTempHome, fakeClaude(dir) (sh wrapper around packages/claude-acp/src/test-support/claude-fixture.mjs), collect, textOf, waitForEvent, waitForGone.
• harness.test.ts (fake agent, 'codex' family path), harness.claude.test.ts (real shim + fake claude: config dir, stripped auth env, flags, --session-id/--resume round trip, permission with DECISION_META_KEY explanation, form question, interrupt cancel, tool_call/tool_result), env.test.ts, families.test.ts, platform-wiring.test.ts.
• integration.test.ts: real CLIs. Claude part runs when claude is on PATH or CM_TEST_CLAUDE_BIN is set (fresh config home -> AcpAuthRequiredError; a real prompt/resume/cancel only with CM_TEST_CLAUDE_CONFIG_HOME); Codex part always runs the fresh-CODEX_HOME -> auth_required check (adapter is a dependency) and a real prompt only with CM_TEST_CODEX_HOME. Ran 2026-10-28 with CM_TEST_CLAUDE_BIN=<vscode ext>/claude 2.1.311: both auth_required checks pass; ~/.claude untouched; no login performed.
close_reason: ACP harness over SDK 1.4.0 with claude shim + codex-acp adapter, env allowlist, no-orphan shutdown; verified

title: Configure the Codex ACP adapter launch safely
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Clanker Corner learned that the Codex adapter's default agent mode auto-approved dangerous commands and that it tries to open a browser. In the harness's Codex launcher: disable the browser, clear the adapter's default auth request, config and log variables, set the initial mode to read-only with on-request approvals reviewed by the user and a workspace-write sandbox, reject the adapter's auto-review mode by refusing any configuration that selects it, pass developer instructions (the persona text, when provided) through the adapter's config, and set the Codex home to the config directory supplied by the caller. Run the adapter via the current Node binary from the workspace's installed package.
acceptance_criteria: A test asserts the launch environment and config for Codex: browser disabled, auto-review refused, read-only initial mode, Codex home set; a manual run completes a prompt without opening a browser.
notes:
Codex launch posture (6.7, 4.4/4.5, 4.6 build on this). Code: apps/daemon/src/acp/families.ts (resolveCodexLaunch), harness.ts, exported from './acp'. Docs: apps/daemon/README.md 'Agent sessions (ACP harness)'.

API
- startSession({ family: 'codex', cwd, configHome, codex?: { mode?, developerInstructions? }, command?, env?, upstreamSessionId?, ... }).
- codex.mode: CodexAgentMode = 'read-only' (DEFAULT_CODEX_AGENT_MODE) | 'workspace-write' (CODEX_AGENT_MODES). CODEX_MODE_POSTURE documents what each means in codex-acp 2.3.0: read-only = approval on-request, reviewer user, read-only sandbox; workspace-write = on-request, user, workspace-write sandbox (no network). The adapter resends the mode's approval policy/reviewer/sandbox with EVERY turn (runTurn), so the mode is the whole posture; config keys cannot override it.
- codex.developerInstructions: persona text; trimmed; blank = none. Sent as CODEX_CONFIG={"developer_instructions": text}; the adapter merges CODEX_CONFIG into the thread config on session/new AND session/load (resume), so it applies to resumed sessions too.

LAUNCH (exact env set by the launcher; wins over caller env): CODEX_HOME=<configHome>, NO_BROWSER=1, DEFAULT_AUTH_REQUEST='', APP_SERVER_LOGS='', INITIAL_AGENT_MODE=<mode>, CODEX_CONFIG=<json or ''>, CODEX_PATH=<command> only when given. MODEL_PROVIDER deliberately NOT set (an empty value would be forwarded to thread/start); it can never be inherited (allowlist) and callers cannot set it. argv = process.execPath <installed @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp>/dist/index.js, no extra args.

REFUSED (AcpLaunchError, thrown before configHome is created or anything is spawned)
- codex.mode 'agent' (the auto-review mode: approvals_reviewer auto_review, Codex approves its own escalations; it is also the adapter DEFAULT, which is why INITIAL_AGENT_MODE is always set), 'agent-full-access' (no approvals, danger-full-access), and any other id (adapter silently falls back to 'agent' for unknown ids).

title: Lift Clanker Corner's Claude shim as a workspace package
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Only the stock `claude` binary may talk to Anthropic, on Jack's own login, with no API keys. Clanker Corner has a self-contained ~750-line stdio ACP agent (its `packages/claude-acp`, at ~/work/new-orange/clanker-corner) that drives the stock CLI in stream-json mode with the stdio permission-prompt protocol, maps the CLI's stream to ACP session updates, relays permission prompts (Allow once, Always allow only for rules the CLI proposed, Deny) and questions as ACP permission and elicitation requests, resumes by session id, cancels via interrupt, reports a missing login as ACP auth-required, and strips every Anthropic API-key, auth-token, Bedrock and Vertex variable from the child environment. Lift it into this monorepo as a workspace package with its tests, removing its dependency on Clanker's per-user config package in favour of taking the config directory and posture flags as launch arguments. Change nothing about its protocol behaviour.
acceptance_criteria: The package builds and its lifted tests pass; running it by hand against a logged-in `claude` completes an ACP initialise and a one-line prompt; with an API key in the parent environment the child does not receive it.
notes:
Claude shim decisions (4.2, 4.3, 6.7 build on these):

PACKAGE
- packages/claude-acp -> @candy-mountain/claude-acp. Library exports '.' -> ./src/index.ts (TS source, no build needed for importers; daemon bundles it via tsdown alwaysBundle). Bin candy-mountain-claude-acp -> ./dist/cli.mjs, built by tsdown (root pnpm build). Deps: @agentclientprotocol/sdk 1.4.0 (exact, same as Clanker; 2.x removed AgentSideConnection/ClientSideConnection in favour of a new app API, so upgrading is a deliberate migration), zod ^4.6.7 (SDK peer). Dev: tsdown, tsx.
- Lifted unchanged: agent.ts, process.ts, translator.ts, permissions.ts (ACP mapping, permission/elicitation relay, resume, interrupt, auth-required). Only auth.ts changed: @clanker-corner/agent-config replaced by an explicit configDir. Imports made extensionless.
- DECISION_META_KEY value kept as 'clanker-corner' (wire-visible _meta namespace for modifiedInput/explanation/acceptsModifiedInput/freeText); the daemon must import the constant, not repeat the string.

EXPORTS (src/index.ts)
- launch({configDir, claudeArgs?, command?, env?, turnTimeoutMs?, onDiagnostic?, stream?}) -> {connection, close()}: serves one ACP session over an SDK Stream, or process stdio when stream omitted.
- createAgent(agentSideConnection, ClaudeLaunchOptions, agentOptions?) -> ClaudeAcpAgent, for use inside a caller-built AgentSideConnection.
- parseLaunchArgs(argv, cwd?) / LAUNCH_USAGE / LaunchUsageError; prepareClaudeLaunch({configDir, env?}) -> {configDir, env}; NON_SUBSCRIPTION_AUTH_ENV; plus the lifted ClaudeAcpAgent, ClaudeProcess, ClaudeEventTranslator, ClaudePermissionBridge, DECISION_META_KEY, CLAUDE_AUTHENTICATION_ERROR, CLAUDE_PROVIDER_ERROR, ClaudeLoginRequiredError, types.

LAUNCH ARGUMENTS (bin)
- candy-mountain-claude-acp --config-dir <dir> [--claude <path>] [--turn-timeout-ms <ms>] [-- <claude flags>...]
- --config-dir required; becomes CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (overrides inherited); mkdir -p 0700, chmod 0700 if it exists, refused if a symlink; relative resolved against cwd. Created lazily at session/new or session/load, so a bad dir surfaces as an ACP error there.
- Everything after -- is forwarded verbatim to claude after the shim's own flags (posture: --permission-mode, --allowedTools, --disallowedTools, --settings, --append-system-prompt, --agent ...). The shim does NOT vet posture flags or block bypass modes: the never-bypass rule must be enforced by the caller (daemon / bead 6.7).
- Old CLAUDE_ACP_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS env replaced by --turn-timeout-ms (default 600000; clock pauses while a permission is open). Bad args exit 2 with usage on stderr.
- Child always gets: --print --verbose --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --include-partial-messages --permission-prompt-tool stdio, then --session-id <uuid> (session/new) or --resume <uuid> (session/load), then the forwarded flags; cwd = ACP session cwd (must be absolute).

HOW THE DAEMON SHOULD RUN IT
- Option A (process per session, as Clanker): spawn(process.execPath, [binPath, '--config-dir', home, '--', ...postureFlags], {stdio:'pipe'}); speak ACP via ClientSideConnection over ndJsonStream(Writable.toWeb(child.stdin), Readable.toWeb(child.stdout)); child stderr = diagnostics. Resolve binPath at runtime with createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve('@candy-mountain/claude-acp/package.json') + '/../dist/cli.mjs' (package.json is exported; add the package as a daemon dependency); requires root pnpm build first.
- Option B (in-process, no shim process, only the claude child): launch({configDir, claudeArgs, stream: ndJsonStream(...)}) with a pair of TransformStreams and a ClientSideConnection on the other ends (see src/launch.test.ts 'launch serves a session over in-process streams'). One agent instance = one session; call close() to kill the child.
- Pass a curated env via the env option (bin: the shim's own env). Do not probe 'claude auth status' right before starting a session (refresh-lock quirk); rely on session/new returning ACP auth_required (-32000 'Authentication required').

ENV STRIPPED FROM THE CHILD
- ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_REFRESH_TOKEN, CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_SCOPES, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_VERTEX, CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY. CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (claude setup-token) passes through, so v2's pasted long-lived token works. ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL etc. are not stripped; a non-firstParty apiProvider in the initialize account summary is rejected as auth_required instead.

TESTS
- pnpm --filter @candy-mountain/claude-acp test (vitest project 'claude-acp', 66 tests, root vitest.config.ts projects list updated). Tests spawn src/cli.ts through tsx; CLAUDE_ACP_TEST_BIN=<abs>/dist/cli.mjs runs the same suite against the build. Fake claude: src/test-support/claude-fixture.mjs (prompt 'launch-env' echoes argv/CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/auth env). Operator REPL: pnpm --filter @candy-mountain/claude-acp acp-client --config-dir <dir> [--cwd ...] [--prompt ...] [-- <claude flags>].
- Lint: package eslint.config.js extends root and turns off no-explicit-any (CLI stream-json is untyped JSON).

MANUAL CHECK (2026-10-28, claude 2.1.311 from the VS Code extension; no claude on PATH)
- Built bin + real claude + fresh empty --config-dir: initialize ok, session/new -> -32000 Authentication required.
- Lifted agent in-process + real claude on the default logged-in config, fake ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN in the parent env: initialize, session/new, one-line prompt -> end_turn 'pong'; keys absent from the child env. Bin + logged-in config not run because --config-dir ~/.claude would chmod the user's ~/.claude (0755) to 0700.
close_reason: packages/claude-acp lifted, 66 tests, env stripping verified with real CLI; DECISION_META_KEY kept (protocol unchanged)

title: Add the Repository plugin type for GitHub and Bitbucket
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Bots, persona checks and deployments all need to talk to the project's remote repository, so the first real plugin is the repository host. Add the `repository` plugin type: project scope only, one instance per project; config is the host (GitHub or Bitbucket), the remote owner and repository name, and the default branch; the secret is a scoped token. Health means the token can read the repository and list branches. Expose daemon-side operations other features will reuse: list branches (recent first, limited), fetch a file's existence on a branch, and the repository's default branch; and expose a branch-list endpoint for the instance so the test-connection result can show real data. Treat the token as the only credential; redact it from errors.

Shared names: Plugin type ids are fixed: `repository`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `netlify`, `heroku`, `slack`.
acceptance_criteria: An instance with a valid GitHub token reports healthy and lists branches; a wrong token reports unhealthy with the host's reason; the same for Bitbucket; a second instance for the same project is rejected; tests mock both hosts.
notes:
Repository plugin type decisions (later beads depend on these). Short how-to also in apps/daemon/README.md "Plugin types" > "### Repository".

FILES
- apps/daemon/src/plugins/types/repository.ts: repositoryPluginType (definePluginType), RepositoryConfig type, repositoryConfig(unknown) parser. Registered in PLUGIN_TYPES (types/index.ts). Built daemon logs "1 plugin type(s) registered".
- apps/daemon/src/plugins/repository/: client.ts (fetch wrapper, RepositoryHostError, redaction, error mapping), github.ts, bitbucket.ts, operations.ts (factory), index.ts (public surface, re-exported from src/plugins/index.ts), fake-hosts.ts (test double: stubHosts()), repository.test.ts.
- packages/shared/src/repository.ts (exported from shared index): REPOSITORY_HOSTS ['github','bitbucket'], RepositoryHost, REPOSITORY_HOST_NAMES, DEFAULT_BRANCH_LIST_LIMIT 30, MAX_BRANCH_LIST_LIMIT 100, clampBranchListLimit(unknown) (accepts query-string values; NaN/absent -> 30, clamps 1..100), RepositoryBranch {name, sha, committedAt: string|null}, RepositoryBranchList {defaultBranch, branches}, REPOSITORY_ERROR_CODES / RepositoryErrorCode.

TYPE: id 'repository', scopes ['project'], singleInstance true.
CONFIG FIELDS: host (select github|bitbucket, required); owner (string, required, pattern [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*; GitHub user/org or Bitbucket workspace slug); repo (string, required, pattern [A-Za-z0-9._-]+; Bitbucket repo slug); defaultBranch (string, OPTIONAL, pattern [^\s~^:?*\[\\]+; blank = use host's default branch, set = override).
RepositoryConfig = {host: 'github'|'bitbucket', owner: string, repo: string, defaultBranch?: string}.
SECRET: token (required). Sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' to both hosts. GitHub: fine-grained PAT (Contents read + Metadata read) or classic/App installation token. Bitbucket: repository or workspace access token (bearer). Bitbucket API tokens needing email+Basic auth are NOT supported (token is the only credential).

HEALTH: createRepositoryOperations(config, secrets, {signal}); getDefaultBranch() (hits repo endpoint unless defaultBranch configured), listBranches({limit:1}); if defaultBranch configured, branchExists(it) else unhealthy "Default branch 'x' does not exist in owner/repo.". Healthy detail: "Can read owner/repo and list its branches; default branch 'main'." Errors are thrown RepositoryHostError -> checkPluginHealth turns message into reason (plus its own redaction). Missing token -> "No GitHub token is set for owner/repo." (no request made).

OPERATIONS FACTORY (daemon-side, import from '../plugins' or '../plugins/repository'):
createRepositoryOperations(config: RepositoryConfig, secrets: PluginSecrets<'token'>, options?: { signal?: AbortSignal, fetch?: typeof fetch }): RepositoryOperations (frozen; never throws itself; reads token once at creation; fetch defaults to globalThis.fetch at call time).
RepositoryOperations = {
  host: RepositoryHost,
  listBranches({limit?}={}): Promise<RepositoryBranch[]>  // most recent commit first, limit clamped 1..100 default 30, single page, no pagination
  fileExists(path, branch): Promise<boolean>  // true only for a file/symlink; false for missing or directory; THROWS RepositoryHostError code 'not_found' "Branch 'x' does not exist in owner/repo." when the branch is missing. Leading/trailing slashes ignored; segments URL-encoded.
  branchExists(branch): Promise<boolean>
  getDefaultBranch(): Promise<string>  // config.defaultBranch ?? host default
}
listRepositoryBranches(ops, limit?): Promise<RepositoryBranchList>  // getDefaultBranch + listBranches in parallel
Typical wiring: createRepositoryOperations(repositoryConfig(instance.config), createPluginSecrets(platform.secrets, instance.id, repositoryPluginType), { signal: c.req.raw.signal }).
Persona check (6.6): ops.fileExists('.claude/agents/<name>.md', base) and ops.fileExists('.agents/<name>.md', base). Bot base branch default (6.5): ops.getDefaultBranch(). Deploy zone (9.x): ops.listBranches({limit}).

HOST ENDPOINTS
GitHub (https://api.github.com; headers Accept application/vnd.github+json, X-GitHub-Api-Version 2022-11-28, User-Agent candy-mountain):
- default branch: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo} -> default_branch
- branches: POST /graphql, repository(owner,name).refs(refPrefix:"refs/heads/", first:N, orderBy:{field:TAG_COMMIT_DATE, direction:DESC}) { nodes { name target { oid ... on Commit { committedDate } } } }. GraphQL is used because REST branch listings have no dates (cannot sort recent first without N extra calls). GraphQL errors (200 + errors[]) map by type: NOT_FOUND->not_found, RATE_LIMITED->rate_limited, FORBIDDEN->forbidden, else host_error.
- branch head: GET /repos/{o}/{r}/git/ref/heads/{branch} (exact match; slashes kept as path separators) -> object.sha
- file: GET /repos/{o}/{r}/contents/{path}?ref={sha}; 404 -> false; array (directory) -> false; type file|symlink -> true.
Bitbucket Cloud (https://api.bitbucket.org/2.0; Accept application/json):
- default branch: GET /repositories/{ws}/{repo} -> mainbranch.name
- branches: GET /repositories/{ws}/{repo}/refs/branches?sort=-target.date&pagelen=N -> values[].{name, target.hash, target.date}
- branch head: GET .../refs/branches?q=name = "<escaped>"&pagelen=1 (q filter avoids slash ambiguity in the path form)
- file: GET .../src/{sha}/{path}?format=meta -> type 'commit_file' true, 'commit_directory' false, 404 false.

ERRORS: RepositoryHostError extends Error { name 'RepositoryHostError', host, code: RepositoryErrorCode, status?: host HTTP status, retryAfterSeconds? }. Codes: no_token (secret unset, no request), unauthorized (401), forbidden (403 without rate-limit headers), not_found (404; message gets hint "(check the owner, the repository name and the token's access)"), rate_limited (429, or GitHub 403 with x-ratelimit-remaining 0; retryAfterSeconds from Retry-After or x-ratelimit-reset; message ends "(retry in N s)"), unavailable (5xx or network failure "Could not reach GitHub: ..."), host_error (other non-2xx), invalid_response (non-JSON or missing fields). Message shape: "<GitHub|Bitbucket> returned <status> for owner/repo: <host reason>" where host reason is GitHub body.message or Bitbucket body.error.message, falling back to statusText. Token string replaced with [redacted] in every message. Abort: if options.signal aborted, the original abort error is rethrown unwrapped. NO retries, NO pagination.

CONTRACT FOR 2.5 (deferred here: the HTTP endpoint and the "second instance rejected" rule both need plugin instances):
- Single instance: reject creating a second 'repository' instance for the same project using type.singleInstance (true) — generic 2.5 rule, nothing repository-specific.
- Branch-list endpoint: GET <instance route>/branches?limit=N (e.g. /api/projects/:projectId/plugins/:instanceId/branches). Handler: load instance; 404 unless type id 'repository'; const ops = createRepositoryOperations(repositoryConfig(instance.config), createPluginSecrets(platform.secrets, instance.id, repositoryPluginType), { signal: c.req.raw.signal }); return c.json(await listRepositoryBranches(ops, clampBranchListLimit(c.req.query('limit')))) -> RepositoryBranchList. On RepositoryHostError respond with ApiErrorBody { error: { code: 'repository_' + err.code, message: err.message } } and a status 2.5 picks (suggested: no_token 409; unauthorized/forbidden/not_found/host_error/invalid_response 502; rate_limited 503 with Retry-After = retryAfterSeconds; unavailable 504/502). err.message is already token-free.

TESTS: src/plugins/repository/repository.test.ts (40 tests) stub global fetch with stubHosts() (in-memory GitHub + Bitbucket serving jack/candy, token 'good-token-123'; pass an override handler to inject responses). Covers: registration/scope/singleInstance, config validation, boot with real PLUGIN_TYPES, healthy + wrong token (host reason) + no token + missing repo + missing configured default branch + echoed token redacted for both hosts; recent-first limited listing, limit clamping, fileExists file/dir/missing/missing-branch/encoded path, slashed branch names, default branch override, rate limit, network failure redaction, abort passthrough, injected fetch, GitHub GraphQL request shape + NOT_FOUND mapping, Bitbucket sort URL + q escaping. No real network calls.
No Drizzle schema or migration.
close_reason: Repository type + GitHub/Bitbucket operations, 40 mocked tests; branch endpoint + single-instance rule deferred to 2.5 per its notes

title: Add the project activity event store
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Later phases (sessions, runs, bot handoffs, incidents, deploys) all report "something happened" to the project, and the Overview page and notifications read that stream. Add a general activity event table owned by a project: type, title, timestamp, an optional link (an in-app path), and an optional small JSON payload; a daemon-internal function to append an event; and a REST endpoint to list a project's events newest first with paging and an optional type filter. Events are written only by the daemon, never by the browser.

Shared names: Activity event types are fixed strings: `session.started`, `run.started`, `bot.handoff`, `incident.opened`, `incident.closed`, `deploy.attempted`.
acceptance_criteria: Appending an event and listing it works; the type filter and paging work; there is no HTTP route that creates events; tests cover append and list.
notes: TABLE activity_events (id text PK uuid, project_id FK projects ON DELETE CASCADE, type, title, occurred_at ISO text, link text null, payload JSON null); indexes (project_id, occurred_at) and (type). Schema apps/daemon/src/db/schema/activity-events.ts. MIGRATION apps/daemon/drizzle/0007_activity_events.sql (tag 0007_activity_events). APPEND (daemon-internal, sync): import { appendActivityEvent } from '../activity'; appendActivityEvent(db: Db, { projectId: string, type: ActivityEventType, title: string, link?: string /*in-app path*/, payload?: Record<string, unknown> }): ActivityEvent. occurredAt = now. Payload serialized > 4096 bytes (ACTIVITY_PAYLOAD_MAX_BYTES) throws ActivityError('payload_too_large'). listActivityEvents(db, projectId, { type?, limit?, before? }) -> ActivityListResponse also exported.
