title: Build the per-project Plugins setup page
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Plugin instances are created and maintained from the UI. Build the Plugins page in the system group: a list of instances for the selected project and the platform-wide ones, a chooser of available plugin types showing each type's description and reach lines before creation, a create/edit form generated from the type's config and secret fields (secrets shown only as "set" with a replace action, never their values), test connection with the result shown inline, and delete with confirmation. Plugin types may contribute an optional extra panel to their instance view for type-specific actions; design the page so a type's layer or component can plug one in without the page knowing the type.
acceptance_criteria: Creating, editing, testing and deleting an instance works end to end; a saved secret shows as "set" and its value never appears in any response or the page; the reach lines show before enabling.
notes:
Plugins setup page decisions (4.8 Claude Code/Codex panels and any later type panel depend on these).

FILES (apps/web/app, all core)
- pages/p/[project]/setup/plugins.vue: thin page. admin = registry.admin ?? isAdmin(user); admin renders <PluginsSetup/>, others get UEmpty 'Only the admin manages plugins' (no /plugins request, which would 403).
- components/plugins/ (auto-imported, Plugins prefix deduped):
  PluginsSetup (all data: instance groups '<Project> plugins' (data-group=project) and 'Platform-wide plugins' (data-group=global), then 'Add a plugin' catalog (data-group=catalog), form modal, toasts);
  PluginsInstanceCard (props instance, type?, neededBy?; emits edit; runs Test connection and Delete itself (confirm via ProjectsConfirmModal + useOverlay); shows config summary, secrets as 'set'/'not set', inline PluginsHealth, action errors as UAlert, then the registered panel);
  PluginsHealth (prop health: PluginInstanceHealth|null; healthy detail / unhealthy reason / 'Not tested since it was last changed.' + NuxtTime relative; data-health=healthy|unhealthy|untested);
  PluginsCatalog (props types, instances, neededBy; emits add(type, scopes); one card per type with description, scope badges, reach lines, 'Needed by <capabilities>' warning (only while no instance of the type exists), Add or 'Added');
  PluginsReach ('Once added, Candy Mountain can:' + reach lines; shown in the catalog AND at the top of the create form, so reach is visible before enabling);
  PluginsFormModal (v-model:open, props type, instance|null (null=create), scopes (available scopes for create); emits saved(instance, created)); fields generated from configFields (string->UInput, select->USelect, boolean->USwitch; names config.<field>) and secretFields (names secrets.<field>); UForm :validate = validatePluginConfig + secret rules; scope radio only when >1 scope is still free; daemon errors shown as UAlert (message + code));
  PluginsSecretField (v-model PluginSecretDraft, props field, saved?: 'set'|'unset'): saved 'set' shows a 'Set' badge + Replace (+ Clear when not required) / Undo; replace shows a password input (autocomplete=new-password) + 'Keep saved'. Values are never prefilled; drafts are reset whenever the modal opens or closes.
  panels/RepositoryPanel.vue: first type panel (see below).
- composables/usePlugins.ts:
  usePluginTypes() -> useApi(GET /plugin-types, key PLUGIN_TYPES_DATA_KEY='plugin-types') + types.
  usePlugins() -> { instances (project's then global), projectInstances, globalInstances, status, error, ...usePluginActions() }; useAsyncData keyed pluginsDataKey(slug)='plugins:<slug>', GET /plugins?project=<slug>; project instances filtered by projectSlug (Nuxt seeds a new key with old data). Admin only.
  usePluginActions() (no fetch, safe to call from any panel) -> { refreshPlugins(), createPlugin(body), updatePlugin(id, body), deletePlugin(id), testPlugin(id), pluginAction<T>(id, action, { method?: 'GET'|'POST', body?, query? }) }. create/update/delete/test ALWAYS (success or failure) run refreshPlugins() = refreshNuxtData('plugins:<slug>') + refreshProjectRegistry(slug), so the list, health, sidebar locks/warnings and view gates update without reload. pluginAction does NOT refresh: call refreshPlugins() after an action that changes the instance (login, revoke).
- utils/plugins.ts (pure, unit tested): pluginInstancePath(id, action?), pluginsDataKey, PLUGIN_TYPES_DATA_KEY, PLUGIN_SCOPE_LABELS {project:'This project', global:'Platform-wide'}, pluginTypeIcon(typeId) (cosmetic map, fallback i-lucide-plug), availablePluginScopes(type, instances) (singleInstance aware), pluginsNeededBy(registry) -> {typeId: capability labels} from plugin/plugin-any reasons, pluginConfigSummary, form helpers pluginConfigDraft / pluginConfigPayload(fields, draft, forUpdate) (create omits blanks; update sends null for blanks so the daemon's merge removes them) / pluginConfigErrors / pluginSecretDrafts / pluginSecretsPayload (only typed values (trimmed) or null for clear; kept secrets never sent) / pluginSecretErrors; PLUGIN_SELECT_NONE sentinel for an optional select left empty.
- utils/plugin-panels.ts + plugins/plugin-panels.ts (Nuxt plugin) = the panel extension slot.
- test/unit/plugins-page.test.ts (8 tests: drafts, payloads incl. null on update, secret rules, summary, availability, neededBy, panel registry).

PANEL EXTENSION MECHANISM (4.8 uses this; the page never knows a type)
- Registry: registerPluginPanel(typeId: PluginTypeId, component: Component) / pluginPanelFor(typeId) in app/utils/plugin-panels.ts (auto-imported everywhere, layers included). A module-level Map; component is markRaw'd.
- Register from a Nuxt plugin. Core's file is app/plugins/plugin-panels.ts:
    registerPluginPanel('repository', defineAsyncComponent(() => import('~/components/plugins/panels/RepositoryPanel.vue')))
  4.8: add two lines there (or a new app/plugins/<name>.ts, or a layer's own app/plugins file):
    registerPluginPanel('claude-code', defineAsyncComponent(() => import('~/components/plugins/panels/ClaudeCodePanel.vue')))
    registerPluginPanel('codex', defineAsyncComponent(() => import('~/components/plugins/panels/CodexPanel.vue')))
- Contract: the card renders <component :is="panel" :instance="instance" :type="type" /> under the health line (data-testid=plugin-panel, separated by a border) for every instance of that type that has a known type. Props: { instance: PluginInstance, type: PluginTypeInfo } (interface PluginPanelProps exported, but declare props inline in the SFC: defineProps cannot resolve auto-imported types). No emits. A panel changes things with usePluginActions(): pluginAction(instance.id, 'start-login', { method: 'POST' }) etc., testPlugin(instance.id), updatePlugin(instance.id, { config, secrets }) (token path), then refreshPlugins() after actions; the instance prop then re-renders with fresh health (the card's PluginsHealth already shows instance.health, so a panel need not repeat it). Errors: toApiError(error) -> {code, message}.
- Panels render during SSR too: fetch type-specific data in onMounted (see RepositoryPanel) so the page never waits on an external host.

REPOSITORY PANEL (components/plugins/panels/RepositoryPanel.vue, data-testid repository-branches / repository-branch): when instance.health.healthy, GET /api/plugins/:id/branches?limit=10 in the browser, re-fetched whenever health.checkedAt changes (each new test) with a stale-request guard; shows branch name, 'default' badge, short sha, relative commit time; reload button; errors (repository_* codes) as UAlert. Not healthy -> 'Branches show here once a connection test succeeds.'

READINESS HINTS: 'Needed by <capability labels>' (registry reasons) shows on the catalog card while the type has no instance, then moves to the instance card the daemon resolves for the project (project's own first, else global) until it is healthy.

VERIFIED: tsx daemon :6901 (throwaway CM_DATA_DIR + CM_SECRETS_KEY, development auth, a fetch preload faking api.github.com only for one fake token; everything else hit the real hosts) + nuxt dev of a scratch copy of apps/web on :6900; agent-hub enabled for the project. Headless Chromium 34/34: reach lines visible in the catalog and the create form before creation; 'Needed by Bots'; empty submit -> Host/Owner/Token required; create Repository with a wrong token -> card shows 'Token set', Not tested; Test -> unhealthy 'GitHub returned 401 for jack/candy: Bad credentials' (real GitHub) inline; edit shows the token as Set with no input; Replace with the fake good token -> health reset to Not tested; Test -> healthy, branches panel lists branches with the default badge; registry refreshed (Needed by gone) without reload; defaultBranch 'nope' -> unhealthy reason; clearing it removes it (null in PATCH); Slack global instance under Platform-wide, test unhealthy invalid_auth (real Slack); 390px no overflow; delete cancel keeps, confirm deletes both; Needed by back after delete; none of the three secret values in any of 35 /api responses or 8 page HTML snapshots (SSR reload included), nor in the data dir or logs; no console errors. Root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (93 files, 883 passed, 3 skipped), build pass.
OPEN: no instance label (multi-instance types would be told apart only by config); toasts stack when saving quickly.
close_reason: Plugins page with generated forms, secrets as set, test inline, panel slot + repository panel; browser-verified 34/34

title: Drive the sidebar, view routes and soft lockouts from the registry
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

The web app must never keep its own map of views; it derives everything from the daemon's registry answer for the selected project. Add a registry composable (fetched per project, refreshed when the project changes or after setup actions), render the sidebar groups from it (module groups with a warning marker when degraded, then the system group), and resolve each capability layer's pages from the manifest's view paths so adding a layer needs no central route edit. Add a view gate component that wraps every capability page: when the capability is not ready for the project it renders a soft lockout naming what to configure with a link to the Plugins page, and when the actor's rung does not include the view it renders a not-granted message. Nothing in a layer may know about another layer.
acceptance_criteria: A project with no modules enabled shows only the system group; enabling a module makes its views appear without a reload of the daemon; a page of a not-ready capability shows the lockout with the missing plugin named; lint still passes the layer rules.
notes:
Registry-driven navigation + view gate decisions (3.4, 6.10, 8.x, 9.x, 2.8/2.9/2.10/2.13 rely on these). Also documented in apps/web/layers/README.md 'Views, the sidebar and the gate'.

COMPOSABLE (app/composables/useProjectRegistry.ts, core)
- useProjectRegistry() -> { registry: ComputedRef<RegistryResponse|null>, status, error, refresh(), loaded: Promise<void> }. useAsyncData with reactive key projectRegistryKey(slug) = 'project-registry:<slug>' (PROJECT_REGISTRY_KEY_PREFIX, app/utils/registry.ts), slug from useSelectedProject(). Refetches automatically when the project (route slug) changes; outside /p/<slug> the handler returns null (no request). registry is null while a project switch is in flight (Nuxt seeds a new key with the old key's data; we drop answers whose project.slug != current slug). SSR awaits it (onServerPrefetch), so the sidebar and gate are server-rendered.
- refreshProjectRegistry(slug?) -> refreshNuxtData('project-registry:<slug>'), slug defaults to the current route's. CALL IT after every setup action: module toggle (2.8), plugin create/edit/test/delete (2.9), grant edit (2.10), bot create/delete (affects hasBots). refreshProjectData() (1.14, refreshes all keys) also covers it. Verified: PUT modules + refresh of that key on the same page adds the group without reload.

SIDEBAR
- app/utils/navigation.ts (pure, unit tested): NavEntry {id,label,icon,to,locked?}, NavGroup {id,label,entries,warning?}; registryNavGroups(registry, slug, admin) -> { capabilityGroups, systemGroup }. capabilityGroups = registry.groups minus kind 'system', in daemon order (modules, then standalone capabilities); entries get locked=true when their view is ready:false (admin only sees those); degraded groups get warning = de-duplicated reason messages from registry.degraded. systemGroup = setupNavEntries(slug, admin) + the registry's system group entries (REGISTRY_SYSTEM_GROUP fallback when no registry). Web SYSTEM_NAV_GROUP was removed (shared REGISTRY_SYSTEM_GROUP is the single source).
- useNavigation() -> { capabilityGroups, systemGroup } (both ComputedRef); admin = registry.admin, else isAdmin(useCurrentUser().user).
- AppNav.vue: module group label shows a warning triangle (data-testid nav-degraded) with a wrapping tooltip of the reasons; locked entries get a lock trailing icon (text-warning).

SETUP ROUTE CONVENTION (2.8 / 2.9 / 2.10)
- Project-scoped setup pages live in CORE under app/pages/p/[project]/setup/: Modules = /p/<slug>/setup/modules (projectModulesPagePath(slug)), Plugins = /p/<slug>/setup/plugins (projectPluginsPagePath(slug)); PROJECT_SETUP_SEGMENT='setup' (never a capability id). Grants is global: /grants (GRANTS_PAGE_PATH), app/pages/grants.vue (dashboard layout). All three sit in the System group, admin only, order Modules, Plugins, Grants, Projects, Settings (Modules/Plugins only when a project is selected). Placeholder pages exist for all three (UEmpty 'not built yet'); 2.8/2.9/2.10 REPLACE those files; no nav edits needed.

VIEW GATE (app/components/CapabilityViewGate.vue, core, auto-imported)
- Usage, EVERY capability page (3.4, 6.10, 8.x, 9.x, 2.13 overview): wrap the page's root UDashboardPanel: <CapabilityViewGate capability="bots" view="bots"> <UDashboardPanel ...> </CapabilityViewGate>. Props: capability: CapabilityId, view: manifest view id. Default slot props { capability: RegistryCapability (rung, tools...), view: RegistryView }.
- States (pure resolveViewAccess(registry, capId, viewId) in app/utils/registry.ts): ready -> slot; not-ready -> own UDashboardPanel with lockout (data-testid view-lockout) titled '<Capability> needs setup for this project', listing reason messages (admins; non-admins get a generic line) and actions from lockoutActions(reasons, slug): plugin/plugin-any reasons or empty -> 'Configure plugins' (/p/<slug>/setup/plugins); project-fact hasBots -> 'Add a bot' (/p/<slug>/bots); other facts -> 'Re-check the project' (/projects). Fact->page map is FACT_ACTIONS in utils/registry.ts (add an entry when a new fact is fixable on a specific page). Actions shown to admins only. not-enabled (admin, capability absent = no enabled module carries it) -> 'Not enabled for this project' + 'Open modules'. not-granted (non-admin absent capability, or view not on the rung) -> 'Not available to you'. Registry loading -> UEmpty loading; error -> retry.
- GOTCHA: the page's own <script setup> runs even when locked; put data fetching in components inside the slot or requests hit the daemon gate (409/403).

ROUTES: no central route table. A layer page path = manifest view path under /p/[project]/ (view path 'bots' -> layers/bots/app/pages/p/[project]/bots/index.vue); registry views' 'to' = projectViewRoute(slug,path) = /p/<slug>/<path>, matching the layer convention; view paths must start with the capability id (cm-layers/layer-pages). Sidebar links come straight from the registry 'to'.

TESTS: apps/web/test/unit/registry-navigation.test.ts (12: nav groups, setup entries, degraded/locked, resolveViewAccess states, lockoutActions incl. plugin-any and hasBots, key).
VERIFIED: tsx daemon :6401 (throwaway CM_DATA_DIR, development auth, real bots/team manifests) + nuxt dev of a scratch copy of apps/web incl. 6.10's real bots/team layers on :6400; headless Chromium 17/17: no modules -> only System group; PUT agent-hub + client-side project switch -> Agent Hub group (Bots, Team) without daemon restart; degraded marker + tooltip; lock icons; /p/acme/bots lockout names Repository and 'one of Claude Code, Codex' with Configure plugins -> /p/acme/setup/plugins; team lockout 'no bots' + Add a bot; inserting a bot row -> team renders its page; PUT [] -> not-enabled state + group gone; 390px no overflow; no console errors. SSR curl /p/acme/bots contains the lockout. Root lint, typecheck, test (83 files/793), build all pass.
close_reason: Registry composable, sidebar, CapabilityViewGate, setup routes; browser-verified 17/17

title: Build the per-project Modules setup page
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Jack enables modules per project from the UI. Build the Modules page in the system group: it lists the three modules with their capabilities, a toggle to enable or disable each module for the selected project, and for each module the plugin types its capabilities need, each with its health for this project and a link to configure it on the Plugins page. Show a module's degraded reasons inline. Toggling must refresh the sidebar immediately.

Shared names: Module ids are fixed: `issues`, `agent-hub`, `operations`.
acceptance_criteria: Enabling Issues from the page adds its group to the sidebar without a reload; the page lists required plugins with health and configure links; disabling removes the group.
notes:
Modules setup page decisions (2.9, 2.10, 2.13 and later module work may rely on these).

NEW DAEMON ROUTE: GET /modules (browser /api/modules; shared MODULES_PATH) -> ModuleListResponse { modules: ModuleInfo[] }. ModuleInfo = ModuleDefinition with capabilities: ModuleCapabilityInfo[] (ModuleMember + the member manifest's label, description, requiresPlugins, requiresAnyPlugins ([] when absent), requiresProjectFacts ([] when absent)), in registration order. Open to any signed-in actor (definitions only, no project state or secrets). Files: apps/daemon/src/modules/routes.ts (moduleRoutes(), moduleInfo(mod, capabilities)), exported from src/modules/index.ts, mounted in app.ts as app.route(MODULES_PATH, moduleRoutes()); test src/modules/routes.test.ts. Shared types appended to packages/shared/src/modules.ts. Distinct from 2.10's admin-only GET /capabilities catalog (rungs, no plugin requirements).

WEB (core, apps/web/app):
- pages/p/[project]/setup/modules.vue: shell; reads useProjectRegistry(); admin -> <ModulesSetup :registry>; non-admin -> UEmpty 'Only the admin can set up modules' (no setup requests are made, so no 403s); error -> retry; loading.
- components/modules/ModulesSetup.vue (calls useModulesSetup, builds cards), ModulesCard.vue (USwitch toggle data-testid module-toggle, card data-testid module-<id> data-enabled; capabilities with Ready/Needs setup badge from registry.capabilities when enabled; degraded UAlert data-testid module-degraded listing registry.degraded reasons with lockoutActions() buttons; plugin list), ModulesPluginRow.vue (name, 'or <alternatives>' for any-of types, 'Needed by ...', instance source, health UBadge with UTooltip detail data-testid module-plugin-health data-health=<state>, Configure UButton -> projectPluginsPagePath(slug), data-testid module-plugin-configure).
- composables/useModulesSetup.ts: useApi of GET /modules, GET /projects/:slug/modules, GET /plugin-types, GET /plugins?project=slug (keys prefixed 'modules-setup:'); setEnabled(id, on).
- utils/modules-setup.ts (pure, tested in test/unit/modules-setup.test.ts): modulePluginNeeds(module, types) = union of members' requiresPlugins and requiresAnyPlugins, once per type, with neededBy labels and alternatives (empty when required outright); pluginHealth(typeId, types, instances) mirrors daemon readiness on the client: project instance first else global; states healthy/unhealthy/untested/secrets-missing/missing + scope + detail; toggledModules(order, enabled, id, on).

HOW TOGGLING REFRESHES: setEnabled PUTs the whole set (MODULE_IDS order) to /projects/:slug/modules, writes the response into the enablement data, then awaits refreshProjectRegistry(slug) so the sidebar groups, degraded markers and view gates update without reload; toast on success/error. VERIFIED: tsx daemon :6801 (throwaway CM_DATA_DIR, development auth, real manifests incl. overview/issues in the Issues module) + nuxt dev of a scratch copy of apps/web on :6800; headless Chromium 18/18: Issues group absent -> toggle Issues -> sidebar Issues group appears with no reload; Agent Hub plugin rows repository=missing, claude-code=untested, codex=unhealthy, each Configure -> /p/acme/setup/plugins (click navigates); enabling Agent Hub shows inline degraded reasons + sidebar degraded marker; disabling Issues removes the group without reload; state persists on reload; 390px no overflow; no console errors. Root lint, typecheck, test (93 files / 882 passed, 3 skipped), build all pass.

title: Add plugin instances with secrets, health checks and REST
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

A plugin instance is one configured connection, owned by a project or by the platform (global scope). Add instance storage and REST: create (type, scope, owner, config, secret values), update config and secrets, delete, list for a project (plus global instances), and "test connection" which runs the type's health check and stores the latest result and time. Secret values are written straight to the encrypted secrets store keyed by the instance and are never returned; responses show each secret field only as set or not set, and updating must allow leaving a secret untouched. Deleting an instance deletes its secrets. Reject an instance whose scope the type does not support and, for types that allow one instance per project, a second one. Config is validated against the type's fields.
acceptance_criteria: Creating an instance with a secret stores it encrypted and every subsequent response shows only "set"; test connection records healthy or the failure reason; deleting removes the secrets; a disallowed scope is rejected; tests cover each.
notes:
Plugin instance decisions (2.6, 2.9, 4.4, 4.5, 6.5, 9.x, 10.4 depend on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md "Plugin instances" + "### Instance actions".

TABLE plugin_instances (src/db/schema/plugin-instances.ts): id uuid PK, type_id text, scope 'project'|'global', project_id FK projects ON DELETE CASCADE (null for global), config JSON (validated PluginConfig), health JSON PluginHealth nullable, health_checked_at nullable, created_at, updated_at. CHECK plugin_instances_scope_owner (project scope <=> project_id not null). Indexes on project_id, type_id. No unique index: singleInstance is enforced in a transaction in createPluginInstance (one per type per project, or per platform for global).
MIGRATION: drizzle/0005_plugin_instances.sql (tag 0005_plugin_instances).

SECRETS: owner pluginSecretOwner(id) = 'plugin:<id>', name = secret field name. Request semantics in `secrets`: non-empty string = set/replace; omitted key or '' = untouched; null = clear (rejected 422 invalid_secrets for a required secret). On create every required secret must be given. Unknown secret name -> 422. Any secret value while the store is locked -> 409 secrets_locked (checked before anything is written; create rolls back the row on a write failure). Delete instance -> deleteOwner. Project delete: DELETE /projects/:slug now calls deleteProjectPluginInstances(c.var, projectId) first (rows also cascade).

SHARED (packages/shared/src/plugin-instances.ts): PLUGINS_PATH '/plugins', PLUGIN_TYPES_PATH '/plugin-types', PluginSecretState 'set'|'unset', PluginInstanceHealth = PluginHealth & {checkedAt}, PluginInstance {id, type, scope, projectId|null, projectSlug|null, config, secrets: Record<name,'set'|'unset'> (every declared secret field), health: PluginInstanceHealth|null, createdAt, updatedAt}, PluginSecretValues, CreatePluginInstanceRequest {type, scope, project?: slug|null, config?, secrets?}, UpdatePluginInstanceRequest {config?, secrets?}, PluginInstanceListResponse {instances}, PluginInstanceResponse {instance}, PluginTypeListResponse {types: PluginTypeInfo[]}, PLUGIN_INSTANCE_ERROR_CODES.

ROUTES (daemon paths; browser /api/...). /plugins is ADMIN ONLY via requireAdmin() (any non-admin 403 forbidden) - decision: plugins hold credentials, so only the admin manages them. /plugin-types is open to any signed-in actor (no secrets).
- GET /plugin-types -> {types: PluginTypeInfo[]} (registration order, healthCheck/actions stripped)
- GET /plugins?project=<slug> -> {instances}: project's own first, then global; within each, type registration order then createdAt. No project param -> global only. Unknown slug -> 422 project_not_found.
- POST /plugins {type, scope, project?, config?, secrets?} -> 201 {instance}
- GET /plugins/:id -> {instance}
- PATCH /plugins/:id {config?, secrets?} -> {instance}. config is MERGED over the stored config then fully validated (null removes a field). type/scope/project are immutable (other keys -> 400). Any real config or secret change sets health back to null; a no-op PATCH changes nothing.
- DELETE /plugins/:id -> 204
- POST /plugins/:id/test -> {instance} with health {healthy:true, detail?, checkedAt} | {healthy:false, reason, checkedAt}. Never fails for an unhealthy check; a stored config that no longer validates is recorded as unhealthy "The saved config is no longer valid: ...". Store guarded on updated_at: if the instance changed mid-check -> 409 instance_changed, nothing stored.
- GET|POST /plugins/:id/<action> -> per-type actions (below).
ERRORS ApiErrorBody: invalid_request 400; not_found, action_not_found 404; project_not_found, type_not_found, unsupported_scope, invalid_config (message lists "field: message"), invalid_secrets 422; instance_exists, secrets_locked, instance_changed 409. SecretsLockedError thrown inside actions also -> 409 secrets_locked.

APP WIRING (merged with 10.6): AppDeps keeps 10.6's `secrets?: SecretsWriter` (index.ts passes platform.secrets.writeOnly) and adds `secretsReader?: SecretsReader` (Pick<SecretsStore,'get'>; index.ts passes platform.secrets; handed only to pluginInstanceRoutes(secretsReader), never c.var) and `pluginTypes?: PluginTypeRegistry` (index.ts passes platform.pluginTypes; default createPluginTypeRegistry(PLUGIN_TYPES)). c.var gains pluginTypes and secrets (SecretsWriter; defaults to lockedSecretsStore().writeOnly from src/secrets when deps.secrets is absent). /plugins and /plugin-types are always mounted; without a reader they use a locked store.

INSTANCE ACTION EXTENSION POINT (4.4 claude-code, 4.5 codex login flows): add `actions` to the type's definePluginType({...}) in src/plugins/types/<id>.ts - no route edits:
  actions: { 'login-start': { method: 'POST', async run({ instance, config, secrets, request, signal, paths }) { ... } }, 'login-status': { method: 'GET', run(ctx) { return new Response(stream, { headers: { 'content-type': 'text/event-stream' } }) } } }
Served at /plugins/:id/<name> behind requireAdmin. Return a JSON value (200) or a Response (returned as is, e.g. SSE). Throw PluginActionError(status, code, message, headers?) for an ApiErrorBody; other throws are 500. Names: /^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$/, 'test' reserved, method mismatch or unknown -> 404 action_not_found; assertPluginType rejects bad actions at boot (PluginTypeError). If an action must WRITE a secret or touch the db, extend PluginActionContext (e.g. add a scoped secrets writer) in actions.ts + the call site in plugins/instances/routes.ts. SERVICE (src/plugins/instances, index.ts re-exports; deps PluginInstanceDeps {db, pluginTypes, secrets: SecretsWriter} - c.var and Platform both satisfy it):
listPluginInstances(deps, {projectId?}), findPluginInstance(deps, id) -> |null, getPluginInstance (throws not_found), createPluginInstance(deps, {type, scope, projectId|null, config?, secrets?}), updatePluginInstance(deps, id, {config?, secrets?}), deletePluginInstance(deps, id), deleteProjectPluginInstances(deps, projectId), testPluginInstance({...deps, secretsReader}, id, {timeoutMs?}), pluginTypeOf(deps, typeId) (throws type_not_found), instanceConfig(type, instance) (re-validated config, throws invalid_config), PluginInstanceError(code).

title: Compute per-actor, per-project readiness and the registry endpoint
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Digital Hub's best idea was one server-owned registry answer that the sidebar, chat rail, view gating and admin pages all read. v3 adds the project axis. Build the registry endpoint, answering for the current actor and a project: the sidebar groups (one per enabled module, each listing the views the actor's rung shows, plus any standalone capabilities granted directly, plus the fixed system group), the full view list with paths, the agents the actor may chat with (where the rung's chat flag is on and the capability is ready), each capability's rung and readiness, and the modules that are degraded with the reasons. Readiness is per project: a capability is ready when every plugin type it requires has a healthy instance for that project (or a healthy global instance), and a capability may additionally declare a project-fact requirement (for example "the project has a `.beads` directory") that readiness also checks. A module is degraded when any of its capabilities is not ready. Admins see degraded modules with reasons; other roles see only what is ready. Also expose rung-gating helpers the daemon uses for routes and tools: given an actor, project and capability, refuse (as a typed value, not an exception) when the rung does not grant the view, tool or chat.

Shared names: Module ids are fixed: `issues`, `agent-hub`, `operations`. Capability ids are fixed: `overview`, `issues`, `chat-claude-code`, `chat-codex`, `bots`, `team`, `uptime`, `deployments`, `platform-agent`.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover: a project with Issues enabled lists the Issues module group; a capability with an unhealthy required plugin is not ready and its module is degraded with the plugin named; a global healthy instance satisfies a project; an ungranted capability is absent; the admin sees everything at top rung; the gating helper refuses a tool below its rung.
notes:
Registry decisions (2.7 sidebar/view routes, 4.9 chat agents, 6.10/3.4 capability registration, 10.7 tool gating rely on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md 'Registry'.

ROUTE: GET /projects/:slug/registry (browser /api/projects/<slug>/registry; shared projectRegistryPath(slug)). Any signed-in actor; 404 not_found for an unknown slug. Answers for c.var.actor and that project. Mounted in app.ts via registryRoutes() from src/registry.

SHARED (packages/shared/src/registry.ts) RegistryResponse field by field:
- project: { id, slug, name }.
- admin: boolean (actor holds ADMIN_ROLE).
- modules: ModuleId[] enabled for the project (MODULE_IDS order).
- groups: RegistryNavGroup[] { id, label, icon, kind: 'module'|'capability'|'system', entries: RegistryNavEntry[] { id (view id), label, icon, to (absolute web route) }, degraded: boolean }. Order: one per enabled module that has at least one entry, then one per standalone capability (a capability belonging to NO module, granted above none; id = capability id, icon = first entry's icon), then the fixed system group last (REGISTRY_SYSTEM_GROUP constant: projects -> /projects, settings -> /settings). Groups with no entries are dropped. Entries map 1:1 onto web NavEntry {id,label,icon,to}; groups onto NavGroup plus icon/kind/degraded, so 2.7 can split on kind === 'system' and render degraded as a warning. Entry content: for the admin every view the rung shows; for other roles only views of READY capabilities. degraded is true only for the admin.
- views: RegistryView[] { id, capabilityId, label, icon, path (manifest, relative), to (absolute), ready }. Every view the actor's rung shows across candidate capabilities, READY OR NOT, for every role, so the web can map a direct URL to its capability and show a soft lockout when ready is false (2.7). Route helper projectViewRoute(slug, path): '' -> /p/<slug>, else /p/<slug>/<path>.
- agents: RegistryAgent[] { id, capabilityId, label, description }: capability candidate + rung.chat + ready (4.9 reads this for the chat rail; unready agents are absent for everyone).
- capabilities: RegistryCapability[] { id, label, rung, chat (rung flag), ready, reasons: ReadinessReason[] (EMPTY for non-admins), modules: ModuleId[] (enabled modules it is in; [] for standalone), views: string[] (view ids at the rung), tools: string[] (tool ids at the rung) }. Only granted candidates: rung above none AND (in an enabled module OR standalone). An ungranted capability is absent; a capability whose modules are all disabled is absent even if granted.
- degraded: DegradedModule[] { id, label, reasons: (ReadinessReason & { capabilityId })[] }, admin only ([] otherwise); considers every member of each enabled module.
- ReadinessReason = { kind: 'plugin', plugin: <type id>, message } | { kind: 'project-fact', fact: ProjectFactId, message }.

READINESS (per project, actor-independent): for each requiresPlugins type id, inst = resolvePluginInstance(c.var, project.id, typeId) (own instance, else global). States (src/registry/readiness.ts assessPluginInstance): missing (no instance) / secrets_missing (a required secret field not 'set') / untested (health null) / unhealthy / ready. Then every requiresProjectFacts entry must be true in project.verification. Ready = no reasons. Readiness reads stored health only; nothing is re-tested.
REASON PHRASING (plugin name = the type's display name, falling back to the id): 'No <Name> plugin is configured for this project or the platform.' / 'The <Name> plugin is missing the secret(s) 'token'.' / 'The <Name> plugin has not been tested since it was last changed; run its connection test.' / 'The <Name> plugin is unhealthy: <stored reason>' / project facts: 'The project has no .beads directory.' / 'The project is not a git repository.' / 'The project has no git remote.'

PROJECT-FACT REQUIREMENT: CapabilityManifest.requiresProjectFacts?: readonly ProjectFactId[] with PROJECT_FACT_IDS = ['hasBeads','isGitRepo','hasRemote'] (packages/shared/src/capabilities.ts; also on defineCapability's parameter). assertCapability rejects unknown or repeated facts ('requires unknown project fact(s) ...'). E.g. the issues capability (3.4) should declare requiresProjectFacts: ['hasBeads'].

CANDIDATE RULE: a capability in one or more modules is a candidate only via an ENABLED module; a capability in no module is standalone and a candidate for every project (project enablement has no axis for it). Grants are not consulted to tell standalone from module (rungs come from resolveActorRungs which already merges module and capability grants).

DAEMON MODULE src/registry (index.ts re-exports): compute.ts computeRegistry(input: RegistryInput) pure over plain data { project {id,slug,name}, capabilities (manifests), modules (definitions), enabledModules, rungs: CapabilityRungs, admin, plugins: Record<typeId, PluginReadiness>, facts: ProjectFacts } plus candidateModules(cap, modules, enabled) and actorRung(cap, rungs) (stale rung name -> none). load.ts: RegistryDeps = AccessDeps & PluginInstanceDeps ({db, capabilities, modules, pluginTypes, secrets}; c.var and Platform satisfy it), loadPluginReadiness(deps, projectId, typeIds), projectFacts(project), loadRegistryInput(deps, actor, project), loadRegistry(deps, actor, project). routes.ts registryRoutes().

GATING (src/registry/gate.ts): gateView(c.var, actor, project, capabilityId, viewId) / gateTool(..., toolId) / gateChat(..., capabilityId) -> GateResult = { allowed: true, rung, scope? (widest level granted on a scoped tool) } | { allowed: false, code: GateRefusalCode, reason, status }. Never throws. Check order and codes: capability_unknown 404 -> not_enabled 404 (not in an enabled module and not standalone) -> not_granted 403 (rung lacks the view/tool/chat) -> not_ready 409 (readiness reasons; the message lists them for the admin only). Pure forms for tests or when access is already resolved: resolveCapabilityAccess(deps, actor, project, capabilityId) -> CapabilityAccess, checkView/checkTool/checkChat(access, ...). MIDDLEWARE requireCapability({ capability, view: id } | { capability, tool: id } | { capability, chat: true }, slugParam? = 'slug') for routes under /projects/:slug: unknown slug -> 404 not_found, refusal -> ApiErrorBody { error: { code, message } } with the refusal status; it stores nothing on the context, so a handler needing the scope level calls gateTool itself. GATE_REFUSAL_CODES exported from shared.

TESTS: src/registry/compute.test.ts (pure, fixture manifests; 14), gate.test.ts (pure checks + DB-backed helpers + middleware; 7), routes.test.ts (instanceHarness + multiPluginType as 'codex'; missing/untested/global healthy/unhealthy/project fact/non-admin/404; 7), manifest.test.ts gained the requiresProjectFacts check. No schema or migration.
VERIFIED: root lint, typecheck, build pass; root test 75 files/683 pass on rerun (first run had one 5s timeout in src/auth/password-rate-limit.test.ts under load, untouched by this bead, passes alone). Live: built daemon on 6274 with throwaway CM_DATA_DIR: POST project, PUT modules ['issues'], GET registry 200 { modules:['issues'], groups:[system], views/agents/capabilities/degraded empty } since no real capability is registered; unknown slug 404.
close_reason: Registry endpoint, readiness, gating helpers + middleware; verified

title: Store per-project module enablement
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Unlike Digital Hub, where a module was on for everyone, each project chooses which modules it uses. Add a per-project record of enabled modules with REST to read and set it (admin only), defaulting to nothing enabled. Enabling a module makes its capabilities candidates for that project's registry; disabling hides them. Validate module ids against the daemon's module definitions.

Shared names: Module ids are fixed: `issues`, `agent-hub`, `operations`.
acceptance_criteria: Enabling and disabling a module for a project persists; an unknown module id is rejected; a new project starts with no modules enabled; tests cover each.
notes: TABLE project_modules (id, project_id FK projects ON DELETE CASCADE, module_id, created_at, updated_at; unique (project_id, module_id)). Schema apps/daemon/src/db/schema/project-modules.ts. MIGRATION apps/daemon/drizzle/0006_project_modules.sql (tag 0006_project_modules). SERVICE apps/daemon/src/project-modules/enablement.ts: listEnabledModules(db, projectId): ModuleId[] (MODULE_IDS order; [] for a new project; 2.6 computes readiness from this), setEnabledModules(db, projectId, moduleIds) replaces the set, returns it. REST (admin-only, per-route requireAdmin, mounted on /projects in app.ts): GET /projects/:slug/modules -> { modules: ModuleId[] }; PUT /projects/:slug/modules { modules } -> { modules }. Errors: invalid_request 400, not_found 404, module_not_found 422 (unknown id vs c.var.modules; set unchanged), 403 forbidden non-admin. Shared types in packages/shared/src/modules.ts: projectModulesPath(slug), ProjectModulesResponse, SetProjectModulesRequest, ProjectModulesErrorCode (2.8 uses these). Not an error to enable a module with unmet plugins; readiness is 2.6. TESTS src/project-modules/enablement.test.ts (8). VERIFIED: typecheck, build pass; live curl on 5931 ok. Root lint/test fail only in src/acp (bead 4.2 in-flight).

title: Define the plugin type contract and registry
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

Plugins are how a project is connected to outside things (a repository host, an agent CLI login, a deploy vendor), and a plugin configured once must serve every capability that needs it. Define a plugin type in code: an id, a display name, a description, plain-language "reach" lines (what the platform will be able to do with it, shown before enabling), supported scopes (project, global, or both), config fields (typed, validated), secret fields (names only; values go to the secrets store), and a health check that receives the instance's config and an accessor for its secrets and returns healthy or a reason. Keep the registry static code (no dynamic loading), validated at boot (unique ids, at least one scope, health check present). Capability manifests reference plugin type ids in their required-plugins list; validate at boot that every referenced id exists. Non-goals: instances, REST, UI.

Shared names: Plugin type ids are fixed: `repository`, `claude-code`, `codex`, `netlify`, `heroku`, `slack`.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover: a plugin type with no scope or no health check is rejected; duplicate ids are rejected; a manifest requiring an unknown plugin type fails boot; a sample type registers cleanly.
notes:
Plugin type contract decisions (later beads depend on these). Short how-to also in apps/daemon/README.md "Plugin types".

SHARED (packages/shared/src/plugins.ts, import from '@candy-mountain/shared'). Wire-safe only; the shared package has no Node/DOM types, so anything holding the health-check function lives in the daemon.
- PLUGIN_TYPE_IDS ['repository','claude-code','codex','netlify','heroku','slack'] as const, PluginTypeId, isPluginTypeId().
- PLUGIN_SCOPES ['project','global'], PluginScope. PLUGIN_FIELD_NAME_PATTERN /^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$/ (camelCase; applies to config AND secret field names; fits secrets-store names).
- Config fields (PluginConfigField union, discriminated by kind): PluginStringField {kind:'string', name, label, description?, required?, placeholder?, pattern? (RegExp source, anchored to the whole trimmed value), default?}; PluginSelectField {kind:'select', options: {value,label}[], default?}; PluginBooleanField {kind:'boolean', default?}. No number kind (no planned type needs one; add a kind + a fieldError case + CONFIG_FIELD_KINDS entry if needed).
- PluginSecretField {name, label, description?, required?} (names only; values go to the secrets store).
- PluginConfigOf<Fields>: typed config object; a field is always present when required:true or it has a default, otherwise optional. PluginConfig = Record<string, string|boolean>.
- validatePluginConfig(fields, input: unknown): {ok:true, config} | {ok:false, errors: {field, message}[]}. Trims strings, empty string = absent, fills defaults, rejects unknown keys, non-object input -> field ''. Usable by daemon (2.5) and web forms.
- PluginSecrets<S> { get(name: S): string | undefined }. PluginHealth = {healthy:true, detail?} | {healthy:false, reason}.
- PluginTypeInfo {id, name, description, reach: string[], scopes, singleInstance: boolean, configFields, secretFields} and pluginTypeInfo(type) -> strips healthCheck for REST responses.
- singleInstance: at most one instance per owner (a project, or the platform for global). Added for 2.5's "one instance per project" rule; required, explicit per type.

DAEMON MODULE apps/daemon/src/plugins (index.ts re-exports everything + PLUGIN_TYPES):
- definition.ts: PluginHealthContext<C,S> {config: C, secrets: PluginSecrets<S>, signal: AbortSignal}; PluginType<C extends readonly PluginConfigField[], S extends readonly PluginSecretField[]> extends PluginTypeInfo { configFields: C; secretFields: S; healthCheck(ctx: PluginHealthContext<PluginConfigOf<C>, S[number]['name']>): PluginHealth | Promise<PluginHealth> } (method syntax so specific types assign to AnyPluginType = PluginType). definePluginType<const C, const S>(type: PluginType<C,S>): PluginType<C,S> runs assertPluginType on import, so config/secrets in healthCheck are typed from the declared fields (secrets.get('undeclared') is a compile error). PluginTypeError (name 'PluginTypeError').
- assertPluginType checks: id in PLUGIN_TYPE_IDS; non-empty name/description; >=1 non-blank reach line; >=1 scope, each known, no dups; singleInstance boolean; healthCheck is a function; config+secret names match pattern and are unique across both; config kind known, label set, string pattern compiles, select has >=1 option with value+label and unique values, defaults pass validatePluginConfig; secret label set. Messages like "Plugin type 'netlify': needs at least one scope." / "...: needs a health check." / "Unknown plugin type id 'gitlab'; add it to PLUGIN_TYPE_IDS in @candy-mountain/shared first."
- registry.ts: createPluginTypeRegistry(types) -> PluginTypeRegistry {list() (registration order, frozen), ids(): readonly PluginTypeId[], byId(id) -> type|undefined, get(id) (throws "Plugin type 'x' is not registered."), has(id)}. Re-asserts each type and rejects duplicate ids ("Duplicate plugin type id(s): 'codex'.").
- secrets.ts: pluginSecretOwner(instanceId) = 'plugin:<instanceId>' (use for set/isSet/deleteOwner too). createPluginSecrets(store: Pick<SecretsStore,'get'>, instanceId, type) -> frozen {get(name)} reading only that owner and only declared secret names (undeclared name throws). Daemon-side only; never in c.var or routes.
- health.ts: checkPluginHealth(type, {config: PluginConfig, secrets: PluginSecrets, timeoutMs = DEFAULT_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS (15000)}): Promise<PluginHealth>. Never throws: thrown error -> {healthy:false, reason: message}; timeout -> aborts ctx.signal and returns "Health check timed out after N ms."; malformed/blank result -> "Health check returned no result."; any secret value the check read is replaced with '[redacted]' in reason/detail. Pass already-validated config.
- types/index.ts: PLUGIN_TYPES: readonly AnyPluginType[] = [] (no real type registered yet).

BOOT WIRING: startPlatform(dataDir, { pluginTypes = PLUGIN_TYPES, capabilities = CAPABILITIES, ... }) builds the plugin type registry first, then createCapabilityRegistry(capabilities, { pluginTypeIds: pluginTypeRegistry.ids() }), both before ensureDataDir, so a bad type (PluginTypeError) or a manifest requiring an unregistered type (CapabilityManifestError "Capability 'deployments' requires unknown plugin type 'netlify'.") stops boot with nothing on disk. Platform.pluginTypes: PluginTypeRegistry. index.ts logs "N plugin type(s) registered". NOT added to createApp/AppDeps/c.var (no REST this bead): 2.5 should add pluginTypes?: PluginTypeRegistry to AppDeps the same way capabilities is. Consequence: a real capability manifest that lists requiresPlugins will refuse boot until those plugin types are registered.

ADDING A PLUGIN TYPE (2.11 Repository, 4.4, 4.5, 9.1, 9.2, 10.3): write apps/daemon/src/plugins/types/<id>.ts: import { definePluginType } from '../definition'; export const repositoryPluginType = definePluginType({ id: 'repository', name, description, reach: [...], scopes: ['project'], singleInstance: true, configFields: [{kind:'select', name:'host', label:'Host', options:[{value:'github',label:'GitHub'},{value:'bitbucket',label:'Bitbucket'}], required:true}, ...], secretFields: [{name:'token', label:'Token', required:true}], async healthCheck({ config, secrets, signal }) {...} }); then append it to PLUGIN_TYPES in types/index.ts. Pass signal to fetch. Types needing instance-specific state (claude-code config dir, codex home) will need the context extended with instance info (2.5/4.4 decide; add fields to PluginHealthContext and checkPluginHealth options).

WHAT 2.5 (instances) IMPORTS: from '@candy-mountain/shared': PluginScope, PLUGIN_SCOPES, PluginTypeId, isPluginTypeId, validatePluginConfig, PluginConfig, PluginHealth, PluginTypeInfo, pluginTypeInfo. From '../plugins': PluginTypeRegistry (platform.pluginTypes), AnyPluginType, createPluginSecrets, pluginSecretOwner, checkPluginHealth. Check scope with type.scopes.includes(scope), single instance with type.singleInstance, required secrets with type.secretFields.filter(f => f.required).

TESTS: src/plugins/fixtures.ts: fixturePluginType(id, health?) -> valid project-scoped singleInstance type with config fields host (select alpha/beta default alpha), account (string required pattern [a-z0-9-]+), verbose (boolean), secret token; health defaults to healthy iff token set, or pass a function to control it. clonePluginType(type) -> mutable deep copy (keeps healthCheck) to break in tests. title: Define capability manifests validated at daemon boot
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

In Digital Hub a capability had no single home: around eight hand-maintained lists had to agree on it. In v3 the server-side manifest is the only declaration of a capability, and everything else is derived from it. Define the manifest shape in the shared contract package and a definition helper in the daemon: a capability has an id, a label, a description, views (id, label, icon, path relative to the project), agents it contributes, tools (with an optional scope), jobs, the plugin type ids it requires, and a ladder of rungs. A ladder starts at a rung named `none`, rungs are monotonic (each grants a superset of the previous rung's views, tools and chat flag), and every view and tool a rung references must exist in the manifest. The daemon holds a registry of capabilities and validates all manifests at boot (unique ids, agents, tools, views and paths across capabilities); a bad manifest must stop the daemon with a clear message. Register no real capability yet beyond what tests need.

Shared names: Capability ids are fixed: `overview`, `issues`, `chat-claude-code`, `chat-codex`, `bots`, `team`, `uptime`, `deployments`, `platform-agent`.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover: ladder not starting at `none` is rejected; a non-monotonic ladder is rejected; a rung referencing an unknown view or tool is rejected; duplicate ids across manifests are rejected; a valid manifest loads; the daemon refuses to boot on a bad manifest.
notes:
Capability manifest decisions (later beads depend on these). Short how-to also in apps/daemon/README.md "Capabilities".

SHARED TYPES: import from '@candy-mountain/shared' (packages/shared/src/capabilities.ts).
- CAPABILITY_IDS (as const: overview, issues, chat-claude-code, chat-codex, bots, team, uptime, deployments, platform-agent), CapabilityId, isCapabilityId().
- NONE_RUNG = 'none'. MANIFEST_ID_PATTERN /^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:[-_.][a-z0-9]+)*$/ for view/agent/job/tool/rung/plugin-type ids. VIEW_PATH_PATTERN: lowercase slug segments joined by '/', no leading/trailing slash, '' = project home (web route /p/<slug>/<path>).
- ViewManifest<V> {id,label,icon,path}; AgentManifest {id,label,description}; JobManifest {id,label,description}; TOOL_KINDS ['tool','operation'], ToolManifest<T> {id, kind, scope?: ToolScopeManifest {dimension, levels (ascending, last widest)}}; ToolPermission {scope?}; Rung<V,T,R> {name,label,description, views: V[], chat: boolean, tools: {[toolId]?: ToolPermission}}; CapabilityManifest<V,T,R> {id: CapabilityId, label, description, views, agents, jobs, requiresPlugins: string[] (plugin type ids), tools, ladder}; AnyCapabilityManifest.

DAEMON MODULE apps/daemon/src/capabilities (index.ts re-exports):
- manifest.ts: defineCapability<const V,const T,const R>({...ladder: readonly [Rung<V,T,'none'>, ...Rung<V,T,R>[]]}): CapabilityManifest<V,T,R|'none'>. Type-level: first rung must be 'none', rungs may only name declared view/tool ids. Runtime: assertCapability(cap) throws CapabilityManifestError (name 'CapabilityManifestError'). Also getRung(cap,name), rungIndex(cap,name) (0 = none, -1 unknown), topRung(cap), duplicates().
- Per-manifest checks: id in CAPABILITY_IDS; non-empty label/description; ids match pattern and are unique per kind (view/agent/job/tool/rung/required plugin); views need label+icon+valid unique path; tool kind valid, scope has dimension + unique non-empty levels; ladder starts at 'none' which grants nothing; rungs reference only own views/tools; chat needs >=1 agent; scoped tool grants must name a level, unscoped must not; monotonic: each rung keeps every view, chat, tool and scope level (>=) of the rung below.
- registry.ts: createCapabilityRegistry(manifests, { pluginTypeIds? }) -> CapabilityRegistry { list() (registration order, frozen), byId(id) -> manifest|undefined, get(id) -> manifest (throws Error "Capability 'x' is not registered."), has(id) }. assertManifests(manifests, opts) re-runs assertCapability on each (manifests may not have come through defineCapability) then checks uniqueness across manifests of capability ids, agent ids, tool ids, job ids, view ids, view paths. pluginTypeIds hook: when given (bead 2.4 should pass the plugin type registry ids), every requiresPlugins entry must be known; omitted now, so plugin refs are only format-checked.
- Error messages read like: "Capability 'uptime': the ladder must start with a rung named 'none'." / "Capability 'uptime': rung 'full' hides view(s) 'uptime-home' that 'read' shows; rungs must be monotonic." / "Capability 'uptime': rung 'full' grants unknown tool 'ghost.tool'." / "Duplicate view path(s) across capabilities: 'overview' (overview, issues)." / "Unknown capability id 'billing'; add it to CAPABILITY_IDS in @candy-mountain/shared first."

REGISTERING A CAPABILITY (file-per-capability): write apps/daemon/src/capabilities/manifests/<capability id>.ts exporting e.g. `export const issuesCapability = defineCapability({...})` (import defineCapability from '../manifest'), then append it to CAPABILITIES in manifests/index.ts (currently empty: no real capability registered). Manifests are pure data (tool ids are strings), so they import no feature code. A bad manifest throws on import (defineCapability) or in createCapabilityRegistry.

BOOT WIRING: startPlatform(dataDir, { capabilities = CAPABILITIES }) builds the registry FIRST, before ensureDataDir/DB, so a bad manifest throws CapabilityManifestError and leaves nothing on disk; index.ts lets it propagate (uncaught -> exit 1 with the message). Platform.capabilities: CapabilityRegistry. index.ts logs "N capability manifest(s) registered" and passes it to createApp. createApp deps gained optional `capabilities?: CapabilityRegistry` (defaults to createCapabilityRegistry(CAPABILITIES)); routes read c.var.capabilities (AppVariables.capabilities). No DB table/migration (none needed: manifests are code).

TESTS: src/capabilities/fixtures.ts: fixtureCapability(id, requiresPlugins?) -> valid manifest with ids prefixed by the capability id (views '<id>-home' path '<id>' and '<id>-admin' path '<id>/admin', agent '<id>-agent', job '<id>-job', tools '<id>.read' and scoped '<id>.search' (dimension project, levels own/all), ladder none/read/full with chat on full), so different-id fixtures never collide; cloneManifest(cap) -> deep mutable copy to break in tests. Build a registry with createCapabilityRegistry([fixtureCapability('overview'), fixtureCapability('issues')]) or boot with startPlatform(temp.root, { capabilities: [...] }). Test files: manifest.test.ts (per-manifest rules incl. @ts-expect-error compile-time checks), registry.test.ts (lookup, cross-manifest dups, plugin hook, real CAPABILITIES list loads), boot.test.ts (bad manifest / colliding manifests refuse startPlatform with no data dir created; valid one reaches c.var.capabilities).

VERIFIED: 31 capability tests; root pnpm lint, typecheck, test (137), build pass. Built daemon boots and logs '0 capability manifest(s) registered'; a tsx probe calling startPlatform with a bad manifest exited 1 with CapabilityManifestError and created no data dir.
close_reason: Manifest types, defineCapability, boot-validated registry; gates green

title: Add module definitions and role grants with rung resolution
description:
Context: Candy Mountain v3 is Jack's personal codebase-management platform, a pnpm monorepo with a long-lived Hono daemon (all state, OS work, SQLite via Drizzle, encrypted secrets) and a Nuxt 4 + Nuxt UI 4 web app whose Nitro server proxies every API call to the daemon so the browser is always same-origin. A 'project' is a registered local codebase; everything is scoped to the selected project. The UI always says 'issue', never 'bead', even though issues are stored by the bd (beads) CLI.

A module groups capabilities for enablement and navigation, and grants decide what a role may do. Declare the three modules in the daemon with their member capabilities and a default rung each (members are filled in by later work; an empty module is valid and renders nothing). A capability may belong to several modules. Store grants in the platform database: a grant gives a role either a module or a standalone capability at a rung per capability. Resolve permissions per actor: the admin role always resolves to the top rung of every ladder; otherwise an actor's rung for a capability is the highest across all grants of all their roles; nothing granted means `none`. Expose grants over REST (list, set) for the admin only, and seed the admin's grants on first start. Resolution must fail closed on any error.

Shared names: Module ids are fixed: `issues`, `agent-hub`, `operations`. Capability ids are fixed: `overview`, `issues`, `chat-claude-code`, `chat-codex`, `bots`, `team`, `uptime`, `deployments`, `platform-agent`.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover: admin resolves to the top rung; two grants at different rungs resolve to the higher; an ungranted capability resolves to `none`; a capability in two modules resolves correctly; grants persist across restarts.
notes:
Modules and grants decisions (2.3, 2.6, 2.10 rely on these). How-to also in apps/daemon/README.md 'Modules and grants'.

SHARED TYPES (@candy-mountain/shared)
- modules.ts: MODULE_IDS ['issues','agent-hub','operations'], ModuleId, isModuleId(), ModuleMember { capabilityId: CapabilityId, defaultRung: string }, ModuleDefinition { id, label, description, icon, capabilities: readonly ModuleMember[] }.
- grants.ts: GRANTS_PATH '/grants', GRANT_TARGET_KINDS ['module','capability'], GrantTarget = {kind:'module',id:ModuleId} | {kind:'capability',id:CapabilityId}, CapabilityRungs = Partial<Record<CapabilityId,string>> (the resolution result shape), RoleGrant { role (slug), target, rungs: CapabilityRungs, createdAt, updatedAt }, RoleRungs { role, name, rungs }, GrantListResponse { grants, roles: RoleRungs[] }, SetGrantRequest { role, target, rungs }, GrantResponse { grant }, GRANT_ERROR_CODES / GrantErrorCode.
- auth.ts additions: FORBIDDEN_ERROR_CODE 'forbidden', isAdmin(actor) (roles includes ADMIN_ROLE).

DAEMON
- src/modules: definitions.ts MODULES = [ISSUES_MODULE, AGENT_HUB_MODULE, OPERATIONS_MODULE], all with capabilities: [] today (add members as { capabilityId, defaultRung }). registry.ts createModuleRegistry(modules, capabilityRegistry) -> ModuleRegistry { list(), byId(), get() (throws), has(), withCapability(capId) }; assertModules throws ModuleDefinitionError on unknown/duplicate module id, empty label/description/icon, unregistered member capability, default rung not on that ladder, duplicate member. Built in startPlatform right after the capability registry, before touching disk. Platform.modules; AppDeps.modules? (defaults to createModuleRegistry(MODULES, capabilities)); c.var.modules. startPlatform option modules?: ModuleDefinition[] for tests. index.ts logs 'N module(s) registered'.
- TABLE role_grants (src/db/schema/role-grants.ts): id uuid PK, role_id FK roles ON DELETE CASCADE, target_kind 'module'|'capability', target_id, rungs JSON {capabilityId: rung}, created_at, updated_at; unique index role_grants_role_target_idx (role_id, target_kind, target_id).
- MIGRATION: drizzle/0004_role_grants.sql (tag 0004_role_grants).
- src/grants: AccessDeps { db, capabilities, modules } (c.var and Platform both satisfy it). grants.ts listGrants(db, roleSlugs?), findGrant(db, role, target), normaliseGrant(deps, req), setGrant(deps, req) (upsert per role+target; module grants store EVERY member explicitly, missing ones filled with defaultRung; capability grants must name exactly their own capability), parseSetGrant(body). errors.ts GrantError(code) with status.
- RESOLVER src/grants/resolve.ts: resolveActorRungs(deps, actor) / resolveRoleRungs(deps, roleSlugs) -> CapabilityRungs with an entry for EVERY registered capability. Admin role -> topRung of every ladder (no DB read). Else per capability the highest rungIndex across all grants of all roles; module grant member rung = grant.rungs[cap] ?? member.defaultRung (so members added to a module later get their default); stale rung names, unregistered capabilities/modules are ignored (none); any thrown error -> console.error + everything 'none' (fail closed). rungOf(rungs, capId) -> rung or 'none'. Bead 2.6: call resolveActorRungs(c.var, c.var.actor) in the registry route and use rungOf/getRung(cap, rung) for views/chat/tools. Module 'held' by an actor is not modelled separately: derive from per-project enablement (2.3) plus the members' rungs.
- SEED src/grants/seed.ts seedAdminGrants(deps): runs in startPlatform after seedAuth on every start; inserts an admin module grant for each module the admin lacks (rungs = each member's top rung, {} today); onConflictDoNothing so edits are never overwritten. Not run by openTestDatabase (tests call it).
- ADMIN GUARD src/auth/admin.ts requireAdmin(): Hono middleware, mount after auth with app.use(requireAdmin()); non-admin -> 403 { error: { code: 'forbidden', message: 'Only the admin may do this' } }. Exported from src/auth.

ROUTES (admin only; browser /api/grants)
- GET /grants -> 200 GrantListResponse { grants (ordered role slug, kind, id), roles: [{ role, name, rungs }] } where rungs is the resolved rung of every registered capability for that role alone (admin = all top). Bead 2.10 can render this directly.
- PUT /grants SetGrantRequest { role, target: { kind, id }, rungs } -> 200 { grant }. rungs optional for modules ({} = all defaults). Errors: invalid_request 400 (bad JSON/shape), role_not_found 422, target_not_found 422 (unregistered module/capability), invalid_rung 422 (rung not on ladder, capability not in module, capability grant naming another capability). No DELETE: revoke by setting rungs to 'none'.

TESTS: src/modules/registry.test.ts, src/grants/{resolve,grants,routes}.test.ts (26 tests) with fixtures in src/grants/test-access.ts (TEST_CAPABILITIES issues/uptime/deployments/team, TEST_MODULES with uptime in two modules, testAccess(db), addRole(db, slug)).

VERIFIED: root lint, typecheck, build pass; root test 506/507, the one failure is src/issues/watcher.test.ts (another bead's in-flight timing test). Live: built daemon on 5622 with throwaway CM_DATA_DIR: 5 migrations applied, '3 module(s) registered', GET /grants shows 3 seeded admin module grants; PUT ok and error codes 400/422; restart -> 0 migrations, same 3 grants, edited updatedAt kept. trusted-header on 5623: no header 401, non-admin 'jack' 403 on GET and PUT, admin PUT 200.
close_reason: Modules, role_grants, resolver, admin-only /grants; verified incl. restart
